This fMRI study of cigarette cue exposure uses visual first-person videotaped cues and reports within-subject contrasts of cigarette cues > neutral (Analysis 17217932_analysis_0 and related contrasts). Group-level voxelwise results were estimated over the whole brain using FLAME and reported as peak coordinates in tables, with cluster-level multiple-comparisons correction; thus qualifying task-evoked whole-brain voxelwise results are available. The study reports participant age/sex and cue type; MRI field strength is not listed in the extracted record but this omission does not preclude inclusion per review guidance. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue fMRI), I4 (within-participant drug cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), and I6 (coordinates/tables reporting acceptable) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears sufficiently represented in the provided record.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Specifically, it uses individually tailored audiotaped (auditory) scripts rather than visual cues (I3 not met). The reported task contrasts are group-level between-group comparisons/interactions (e.g., PCE vs NCE for favorite-food vs neutral) and the NeuroStore record does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., favorite-food > neutral) required by I4. The study does include whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction (satisfying I5 and I6). Because the paper appears to report only between-group contrasts without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast, exclusion criterion E5 applies. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of opioid cue-reactivity using a visual opioid-word Stroop task (meets I3). The paper reports contrasts comparing opioid words to neutral words (opioid>neutral) and defines modulatory change (effective connectivity) and attentional bias based on within-participant opioid vs neutral effects; voxelwise group-level GLM results are reported with 14 peak coordinates (Table tbl0003) and whole-brain inference (Model fit over: whole brain; Inference over: whole brain; FWE cluster-level), satisfying I4 and I5. Coordinate reporting in tables satisfies I6. Although a listed contrast includes a between-group interaction, the abstract and analysis metadata indicate a within-subject opioid vs neutral effect was tested and reported voxelwise. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. fulltext_incomplete set to false.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: (1) It is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using clear visual smoking cues (I3). (2) It reports within-participant contrasts of smoking cue > neutral (analyses 0 and 2) (I4). (3) It includes at least one group-level voxelwise task-evoked result with whole-brain inference (analysis 2 reports whole-brain FWE-thresholded cluster results and reported peaks), and also small-volume-corrected results (I5). (4) Qualifying voxelwise results are reported in tables/peaks (analysis_2 table t0010) satisfying I6. Participant demographics and cue type are reported; MRI field strength and some preprocessing/software details are not listed but missing details do not preclude inclusion per I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual smoking images (meets I3). It reports group-level voxelwise results (whole-brain model fit, thresholding, and 11 reported peaks in Table 1), and results are reported in tables/thresholded maps (meets I5 and I6). However, the NeuroStore extraction does not report any explicit within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (e.g., Smoking > Neutral). The only listed contrast is labeled 'Control [simple effect, within-group]', which does not unambiguously represent a smoking>neutral cue contrast. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are explicitly met by the provided record. Exclusion is based on failure to meet I4 (required).

This fMRI study examines appetitive (monetary) Pavlovian conditioning with clear visual cues (2€ coin images and geometric shapes). The NeuroStore record reports within-participant contrasts CS+app > CS− (analysis_2) with group-level voxelwise inference using FWE small-volume correction (voxel-level), satisfying I3 (visual reward-related cue paradigm), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (small-volume-corrected voxelwise group result), and I6 (results reported as peaks). The study also includes whole-brain task-evoked analyses and does not rely solely on ROI-only or connectivity-only results, so no exclusion criteria (E3–E5,E6) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study uses visual cannabis cues (pictures of cannabis products/paraphernalia) within a multimodal cue-reactivity task (I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of cannabis picture > flower picture and cannabis bimodal > flower bimodal (within-group drug-cue > control-stimulus contrasts), satisfying I4. Analyses were fitted over the whole brain with whole-brain cluster correction and report peak coordinates in tables, meeting the requirement for voxelwise group-level task-evoked results (I5) and allowing coordinate-table reporting (I6). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported; some preprocessing/statistical details (FLAME/FILM) are provided though MRI field strength is not explicitly stated (I7 is not required). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking videos vs control haircut videos). It reports within-participant contrasts of smoking videos > control videos in both stress and non-stress sessions (analyses 19632211_analysis_1 and _2). Results are group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with corrected thresholding and reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study examined smoking cue reactivity with clear visual cues (42 smoking images, 40 neutral) and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (GLM BOLD contrast) and ICA connectivity results. However, the only reported task-evoked voxelwise result is a between-group interaction (slipped > non-slipped for smoking>neutral) rather than a within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli. The other reported analyses are connectivity (ICA) results. Therefore the study does not provide an accompanying within-subject smoking>neutral (drug cue > control) voxelwise result required by the review. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (only between-group/interaction reported without within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cue component), I5 (at least one group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical result reported), and I6 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant drug-cue > control contrast reported).

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue-reactivity using color photographs (visual cues). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of smoking-related > neutral images (prequit and during abstinence). At least one qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result is reported with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference, cluster-level thresholding, and tables of peak coordinates (Talairach), satisfying the requirement that voxelwise results be available. Results are reported in tables and the main text describes them. Participant age/sex and cue type are reported; MRI field strength and software are not listed but missing preferred details do not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This study uses visual smoking cues and task fMRI, satisfying I3. However, the NeuroStore extraction lists only seed-based gPPI connectivity analyses (whole-brain connectivity) testing a between-group interaction (smokers regulation > ex-smokers craving). No within-participant drug-cue > control-stimulus voxelwise task-evoked contrast is reported in the provided document. Therefore the study reports only connectivity/between-group interaction results and lacks a qualifying within-subject cue>control voxelwise result; it meets exclusion criteria E4 (only seed-based/effective connectivity reported without task-evoked voxelwise results) and E5 (only between-group/interaction contrasts without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 and I5. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

The study examines visual smoking cue reactivity (16 videos) and reports a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise smoking > neutral contrast (Analysis 26679479_analysis_0). This provides a within-participant drug-cue > control contrast and a task-evoked voxelwise result suitable for meta-analysis. Participant demographics and cue details are reported. Although the paper also contains ROI and PPI connectivity analyses, these do not exclude the study because a qualifying whole-brain voxelwise cue>control result is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli (cocaine and food pictures) (I3). Analysis 31420667_analysis_0 reports a within-participant contrast involving cocaine-related cues versus control (neutral/food baseline) (within-group contrast of Cocaine-Neutral) with reported peak coordinates (I4). The statistical maps were estimated voxelwise over the whole brain and inference used FWE small-volume correction (SVC), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise or SVC-corrected group-level results (I5). Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables (I6). Participant demographics and cue type are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI or only connectivity analyses, and includes a qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast, so it is includable.

This fMRI study directly examines alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (NAPS alcoholic and non-alcoholic pictures plus additional images), and reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol > non-alcoholic beverage) for the AUD group. Model fitting was performed over the whole brain and coordinates/peaks are reported (Table 3), fulfilling the requirement for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. Coordinate reporting in tables is acceptable. Participant age/sex and cue type are reported (MRI field strength/software not listed but missing details alone do not exclude). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol stimuli (15 alcohol pictures vs neutral controls) and reports a within-participant contrast (alcohol>control) at the group level. The analysis is voxelwise with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference (FWE-corrected results, reported peak coordinates), satisfying the requirement for task-evoked voxelwise results. Participant demographics (age/sex) and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Note: MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software are not reported in the extracted record, but missing these details alone does not exclude the study (I7 preferred, not mandatory).

This study examines neural responses to visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports within-participant contrasts of food > blurred baseline, so it meets I3 and I4. However, all reported analyses were fit over a region-of-interest mask (ROI) and no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level task-evoked results are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual stimuli (drug pictures, drug-use tools, drug-use actions, and neutral pictures). It reports a within-subject cue>neutral contrast (drug-related/Drug/Tool/Action > neutral) and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain inference (model fit and inference over whole brain; FWE cluster-level thresholding) with peak coordinates reported (Table t3). Participant demographics and cue types are reported. Although MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software are not listed in the NeuroStore extract, I7 is a preferred reporting item and missing details do not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes a within-participant cue>control contrast). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual drug cue-reactivity and provides qualifying whole-brain results.

The study reports a whole-brain task-evoked cue-reactivity between-group contrast using visual food cues (natural rewards), but the NeuroStore record does not present any within-participant cue>control (e.g., HiCal>LoCal or HiCal>neutral) contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual food cue-reactivity present), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked result reported), I6 (results reported in tables/peaks), I7 (participant and cue details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no explicit within-participant cue>control contrast reported). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (only between-group contrasts for cue reactivity are provided without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Based on the provided document, the study must be excluded.

The NeuroStore extraction indicates that all reported group analyses were restricted to predefined ROIs (model fit over: region of interest; inference restricted to: region of interest) for the contrast milkshake receipt > tasteless receipt. This means no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level task-evoked result for visual cue-reactivity is provided. Although the study examines natural reward (food) and includes visual stimuli/food pictures in the experimental paradigm (so inclusion I3 is met) and reports participant demographics (I7 met), it does not report a within-participant visual cue > control contrast relevant to cue-reactivity (I4 not met) and does not provide a whole-brain or SVC voxelwise result (I5 not met). I6 is also not met because no qualifying voxelwise results are available in the extraction. Therefore the study is excluded under exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result).

This study reports visual drug-cue (cannabis) fMRI cue-reactivity using photos (I3). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrasts were estimated over the whole brain and inference used small-volume FWE correction with reported peak coordinates (satisfies small-volume-corrected/voxelwise reporting, I5 and I6). Within-participant cue>control contrasts are present (cannabis>neutral and cannabis>baseline) used in within-group cross-subject regressions and other contrasts, meeting the requirement for a within-participant drug-cue>control contrast (I4). Participant demographics and cue details are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-subject cue>control contrasts. Thus the paper meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This study reports fMRI of heroin addicts using visual heroin-related videos versus neutral videos. It includes within-participant contrasts of drug video (salient) > neutral video (analyses 0, 3) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain model fit and reported peak coordinates (Tables). Visual cues are clearly used (colour videos). Although some acquisition/preprocessing details are not listed, those omissions do not preclude inclusion per I7. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper provides whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (so not only ROIs or only connectivity), and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7.

Excluded because the reported analyses are restricted to ROI-only voxelwise modeling and inference (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest) with no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise results. This meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task includes visual component: audiovisual smoking-cue and non-smoking cue clips) and I4 (within-participant contrasts SC > non-SC are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked result). Therefore the study must be excluded under E3 despite meeting I3 and I4. Full text appears complete for screening (no access issues).

This study reports a task-evoked fMRI whole-brain voxelwise analysis of visually-presented anticipatory cues (Monetary Incentive Delay Task with circle/square/triangle cues), satisfying the visual-cue requirement (I3). The reported contrast is a within-participant interaction comparing cue conditions under nicotine vs placebo (Loss Cue > Neutral Cue within-subject; paired t-test/crossover), which qualifies as a within-participant cue>control contrast (I4). The model was fit and inference conducted over the whole brain with FLAME cluster correction and reported peak coordinates (Table 1), meeting the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results (I5) and allowing coordinate reporting (I6). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported; MRI field strength and preprocessing software are not stated but their absence does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

The study is an fMRI investigation using visual cues (Visual Masking Task with cocaine, neutral, sexual, aversive pictures) addressing drug-related cue-reactivity (I3). It reports a within-group contrast of cocaine > neutral, used in a cross-subject regression predicting affective bias (I4). The model was fit over the whole brain and produced voxelwise group-level results with reported peak coordinates (MNI), satisfying the requirement for a whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked result (I5). Reporting of voxelwise results in the record (reported peaks) satisfies I6. Although the NeuroStore record does not list MRI field strength or preprocessing/software (elements noted in I7 are preferred), the record does provide participant age/sex and cue types; missing those preferred details alone do not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements and is INCLUDED.

The study uses visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results, but it does not include a within-participant contrast of reward-related cues > control (e.g., food images > neutral/non-food control). The reported contrasts compare food images with calorie information versus without calorie information, which are experimental condition comparisons within food cues rather than cue>control contrasts required by I4. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study does not satisfy inclusion criterion I4 and must be excluded.

This study used visual alcohol cues in an fMRI cue-reactivity task (I3 satisfied). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results with coordinates using cluster-corrected inference (I5 satisfied) and provides coordinates/peaks (I6 satisfied). Participant demographics are reported (I7 satisfied). However, all reported statistical results in the NeuroStore record are between-group interaction contrasts (e.g., heavy > light for alcohol > neutral) rather than standalone within-participant cue>control contrasts; the record explicitly labels contrasts as interaction, between-group and lists only between-group contrasts. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast) and must be excluded.

This study tests regulation (Regulate CS+ > Attend CS+) of responses to a cigarette-paired cue (visual packet image) using whole-brain voxelwise fMRI in smokers, but it does not report a within-participant cue>control-stimulus contrast (e.g., CS+ > control/CS- or drug-cue > neutral) required by I4. Inclusion met: I3 (drug-related visual cue present — picture of a packet of cigarettes), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain result reported, voxelwise threshold p<0.001, peaks listed), I6 (results reported as coordinate peaks/tables). Inclusion not met: I4 (no within-participant drug-cue > control contrast reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text is available in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study investigates visual food cue reactivity (natural rewards) using seed-based PPI connectivity analyses comparing high- vs low-energy-dense cues, but the NeuroStore record shows only group-level between-group interaction/sex-difference PPI results. No within-participant cue>control (high-ED > low-ED) task-evoked activation contrast is reported as a qualifying voxelwise result. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E4 (only seed-based connectivity/PPI reported without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result) and E5 (reports only between-group interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criterion met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward visual cue reactivity). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 and I5.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual picture stimuli (alcohol, marijuana, polydrug, emotional and neutral images) and reports within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral (alcohol>neutral, marijuana>neutral, polydrug>neutral). Models were fit over the whole brain and group-level voxelwise results are reported as peak coordinates in tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Coordinate-table reporting is explicitly allowed. Participant age/sex, cue types, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported; MRI field strength is not stated but missing details alone do not exclude. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The paper investigates natural reward (food) cue-reactivity with clear visual cues (images of milkshakes), and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. However, all reported voxelwise results in the NeuroStore record are between-group interaction contrasts comparing FTO genotype groups (e.g., AA/AT > TT for milkshake receipt or cue). There is no standalone within-participant cue>control (milkshake>tasteless) group-level contrast reported that would qualify for inclusion. Per exclusion criterion E5 (studies reporting only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast), this study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward with visual cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results present), I6 (results reported in tables/peaks). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast reported).

Exclusion rationale: E3 and E5 met. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E3 (analyses are ROI-only: 'Model fit over: region of interest' and 'Inference restricted to: region of interest' for all reported analyses) and E5 (the report shows only group×time interaction contrasts for cue-reactivity; no explicit within-participant drug-cue > control contrast is reported). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (Cue Reactivity Task used visual smoking-related images vs control images). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (no clear within-participant drug cues > control contrast reported) and I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked result reported). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of appetitive (natural food) cue-reactivity using visual cues (pictures paired with tones) and reports within-subject CS+>CS− contrasts during a reinstatement test. NeuroStore extraction shows group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with inference via small-volume FWE correction (voxel-level) and reported peaks (qualifying as SVC voxelwise results). Participant demographics (n=33, age, sex) and task/cue details are reported. Thus it meets I3 (natural reward with visual cue), I4 (within-participant CS+>CS− contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise SVC result), I6 (results reported/available), and I7 (participant/cue details reported). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual cues (erotic pictures and monetary cues) and reports within-participant cue>control contrasts (erotic rewarded > control; monetary rewarded > control) at the group level. At least one qualifying voxelwise group-level result is reported over the whole brain with cluster-level correction (analyses 2–5,8,9), and small-volume-corrected/svc results are also present for some interactions. Participant demographics and task details are reported. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking vs neutral pictures). It reports a within-participant smoking>neutral contrast and an omnibus tDCS×cue interaction; group-level voxelwise analyses were fitted and inference was performed over the whole brain with reported peak coordinates (Table nsx055-t2). Although MRI field strength is not stated, participant demographics, cue type, task design, and software (AFNI cluster correction, Talairach space) are reported. All required inclusion criteria for voxelwise task-evoked cue>control results are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports a within-subject fMRI contrast of cigarette cues > neutral cues using visual stimuli (IAPS and smoking-related pictures) in chronic smokers (n=35). Analyses were whole-brain (model fit and inference over whole brain) with voxelwise results reported as peak coordinates in tables and cluster-thresholding (FDR, t>3.25, cluster extent), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics and smoking characteristics are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity and voxelwise whole-brain reporting are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports a task-evoked fMRI cue-reactivity paradigm using visual smoking-related images (ISIS), and includes a within-subject contrast of smoking>neutral. Model was fit over the whole brain and voxelwise results (reported peak coordinates in tables) are provided, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant drug-cue>control contrast), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise result), and I6 (results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrast). Some preferred details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software, participant ages/sex) are not reported in the NeuroStore record, but missing these does not preclude inclusion under I7. Overall certainty is high given the clear reporting of whole-brain smoking>neutral voxelwise results in tables.

The study examines smoking vs nonsmoking cues using audiovisual stimuli (meets I3) but the NeuroStore record shows only region-of-interest, between-group interaction results (NW; smoking cues > OB; nonsmoking cues). There is no within-participant cue>control (smoking>control) voxelwise contrast reported. Inference/modeling was restricted to an ROI (region-level thresholding), not a whole-brain or SVC voxelwise group-level result. Therefore it violates inclusion criteria I4 and I5 and meets exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only results with no qualifying voxelwise result) and E5 (reports only between-group/interaction contrasts without an accompanying within-participant cue>control voxelwise contrast). Full text appears available in this record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study meets the meta-analysis criteria: it is a task-based fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol images (I3). It reports a within-participant contrast of alcohol cues > control (pleasant) images (I4). The statistical model was fit over the whole brain and voxelwise peaks (coordinate) are reported, satisfying the requirement for a group-level voxelwise whole-brain result (I5) and acceptable reporting of coordinates (I6). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported (I7 preferred details present); missing preprocessing/field-strength details do not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore include in the meta-analysis.

This study examines fMRI responses to visual food cues (natural rewards) and includes within-participant voxelwise contrasts of appetizing food > control (glasses of water) and appetizing > unappetizing. Analyses were estimated over the whole brain with inference using small-volume correction (FDR SVC) and report peak coordinates in tables, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (small-volume-corrected). Participant demographics and task/cue details are reported; preprocessing/statistical software (SPM) is indicated. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports fMRI with visual alcohol cues (ROC task) and whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE-corrected peaks), so it meets I3 (visual cue component), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported in tables). However, the reported contrasts are regulatory contrasts (LATER>NOW, NOW>LATER), reappraisal contrasts (REAPPRAISE>LOOK), and a craving parametric modulation; there is no within-participant contrast that directly tests drug-cue > control-stimulus (e.g., alcohol > neutral/neutral images) as required by I4. No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., study does not report only ROIs or only connectivity). Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet I4.

This fMRI cue-reactivity study used visual cues (images) and includes within-subject contrasts of tobacco>neutral, satisfying I3 and I4. However, all reported analyses are region-of-interest/region-level (model fit and inference restricted to ROIs) with no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level task-evoked results reported, so it fails I5. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only). Exclusion IDs met: E3. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4. Inclusion IDs not met: I5.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation in opioid use disorder using visual stimuli and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (session × stimulus interaction, corrected whole-brain inference, reported peak). However, the NeuroStore record does not report a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast explicitly; the listed analysis is an omnibus session×stimulus interaction rather than a direct drug>control within-subject contrast. Inclusion criterion I4 (explicit within-participant drug-cues>control contrast) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E5) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet I4.

The study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food pictures vs scenery) with within-subject contrasts (food > scenery). Group-level voxelwise results were reported over the whole brain (model fit and whole-brain inference for the combined analysis), with coordinates/peaks presented in tables. Participant demographics and task details are provided. These elements satisfy the review’s inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual beverage pictures (NAPS) with subjective craving ratings. It reports within-subject contrasts alcohol>beverage and alcohol>control at the group level, with whole-brain voxelwise inference and reported peak coordinates (tables). MRI field strength and participant demographics are provided. Thus it meets the review objective and the required voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results are available.

This is an fMRI study of smoking-related visual cues (pictorial stimuli) with a within-subject contrast smoking-related > neutral. The NeuroStore record reports group-level voxelwise results: whole-brain mixed-effects analyses with cluster-level correction (Analyses 0 and 2) and reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or SVC voxelwise task-evoked results. The study therefore meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity and within-participant cue>control contrasts. Some methodological details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not reported in this record, but their absence does not preclude inclusion per criterion I7. Not excluded under ROI-only or connectivity-only exclusions.

This study examines visual natural reward cues (erotic/romantic IAPS images) and reports within-participant contrasts (romance > everyday), but the romance>everyday and violence>everyday contrasts are reported as region-of-interest analyses only. Although whole-brain omnibus F maps are reported, they do not provide a group-level voxelwise cue>control (natural reward>control) contrast with whole-brain or small-volume-corrected inference. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result). Included criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant natural reward>control contrast present), I7 (participant age/sex reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or SVC voxelwise result for the cue>control contrast).

The study examines visual alcohol cue reactivity and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE-corrected clusters) and coordinate peaks, satisfying I3, I5, and I6. However, the NeuroStore record does not report any explicit within-participant contrast of alcohol cues > control stimuli; the reported results are a Group-by-Distractor interaction (between-group omnibus interaction) and cross-subject regression of craving on cue-related activations. Because the paper appears to present only between-group interaction and cross-subject regression results without an accompanying within-subject cue>control contrast, it meets exclusion criterion E5. Therefore it cannot be included in the meta-analysis that requires a within-participant drug-cue > control contrast (I4 not met). Full text is available in the record (not incomplete).

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using food (natural reward) cues that explicitly includes visual stimuli (congruent pictures of food products) and control stimuli (e.g., fixation cross, grass odor). The reported analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise omnibus F-maps (within-group) with reported peak coordinates (Table), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. Although the NeuroStore extract lists omnibus interaction F-maps rather than a single cue>control t-contrast, the presence of within-group voxelwise F-maps across taste category/protein content in a cue-reactivity task implies within-participant contrasts of food cues versus control/other cue types were tested and reported. Participant demographics are provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This study reports visual cue-reactivity to tobacco (I3 satisfied) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with reported peak coordinates (I5 and I6 satisfied). However, the NeuroStore extraction shows only between-group interaction contrasts (e.g., non-Smokers > Smokers for craving and aversion cues) and does not report any within-participant cue>control (drug-cue > control-stimulus) contrasts required by the meta-analysis. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast) is met. Inclusion criterion I4 (within-participant drug-cue>control contrast) is not met. Other exclusion criteria do not apply. Full text appears available for screening.

This study uses an event-related Monetary Incentive Delay task with explicit visual cues (red/green squares) and reports a within-participant contrast of potentially rewarding > nonrewarding cues. Group-level voxelwise results were reported with whole-brain inference and small-volume corrections (NAcc mask and exploratory spheres) and peak coordinates are provided (table), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or SVC voxelwise evidence. Participant age/sex and cue type are reported. MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not shown in this record but that alone does not exclude the study. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for task, contrast, and voxelwise reporting.

The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise cue-reactivity results for appetizing vs unappetizing food images, but the available reported contrasts are between-group/time interaction contrasts (weight-change group × time × image condition) rather than a within-participant cue>control contrast. Inclusion criteria I3 (natural reward visual cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results available in tables) are satisfied. However, I4 (at least one within-participant cue>control contrast) is not met, and this violates exclusion criterion E5 (studies reporting only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual smoking cues (40 color pictures) and a within-participant contrast Smoke > control (abstinent condition). Group-level voxelwise analysis was performed (one-sample t-test, model fit over whole brain) with reported peak coordinates (tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. These elements meet the meta-analysis objective of visual drug-cue reactivity. Some preferred details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not reported in this NeuroStore record, but the absence of those does not preclude inclusion per the criteria. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied.

The study reports fMRI cue-reactivity to cigarette (drug) cues with a visual component (participants held and viewed a cigarette), includes a within-subject cigarette>control contrast (Analysis 22483100_analysis_0: voxel-wise paired t-test, whole-brain, p<0.001, cluster extent reported), and provides voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results reported as peak coordinates. These satisfy the review objective and inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Some preferred reporting details (MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not given in the NeuroStore record, but missing these does not preclude inclusion per the criteria.

This fMRI study examines smoking cue reactivity using clearly visual stimuli (cigarette and neutral objects) and nicotine-deprived smokers, satisfying the review topic. It reports a within-participant cigarette>neutral contrast (Analysis 16085533_analysis_3, within-group, n=10). Model was estimated voxelwise over the whole brain and inference for some analyses used region-level thresholding (i.e., small-volume correction), and voxelwise whole-brain results are reported for other contrasts (Analyses 0 and 1) with peak coordinates in tables. These meet the requirement for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. Some methodological details (e.g., MRI field strength, software) are not listed in this record but are not exclusionary. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study directly examines drug cue-reactivity using visual cocaine images and includes within-participant cocaine>neutral contrasts (e.g., within-group medication comparisons that test cocaine vs neutral under placebo and modafinil), satisfying the cue>control requirement. It reports group-level voxelwise results: a whole-brain voxelwise analysis (p<0.001, cluster extent 30) and multiple small-volume-corrected voxelwise ROI results (FWE SVC), with peaks reported in tables. Coordinate-space and cue details are provided. Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. Missing MRI field strength and preprocessing/software details do not preclude inclusion (I7 is preferred but not mandatory). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Overall, the study provides qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results for visual drug-cue reactivity suitable for the meta-analysis.

The study is an fMRI investigation of cigarette cue reactivity using visual cigarette cues (participants held and viewed a cigarette), satisfying the review focus on drug-related visual cue reactivity. It reports within-subject Cigarette > Control contrasts (analyses labeled “Cigarette > Control” with reported peak tables) and a whole-brain voxelwise regression/inference (analysis 22288977_analysis_0: model fit and inference over whole brain with cluster-corrected thresholding). Thus it provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain), and coordinate results are reported in tables, meeting inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears available in the provided NeuroStore record.

This study performed resting-state, seed-based functional connectivity analyses within an ROI (compound mask of three networks) and reported group comparisons and correlations. It did not report any task-evoked, within-participant voxelwise cue>control contrasts using visual drug cues. Exclusion IDs met: E3 (ROI/seed-only analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain/SVC result), E4 (resting-state/seed-based connectivity only, no task-evoked voxelwise result), E5 (reports group comparisons/correlations without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion IDs met: I7 (participant demographics and some methodological details reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (no clear visual cue-reactivity fMRI task reported during scan), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (no qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result), I6 (no voxelwise results reported). Full text is complete for screening.

The study reports a cue-reactivity fMRI task using visual alcohol cues (Preferred alcoholic beverage) contrasted with a control (litchi juice) in a within-participant contrast (alcohol > control). Models were fit over the whole brain and group-level voxelwise results are reported as peak coordinates (tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. The NeuroStore extract lists whole-brain model fit, alcohol>litchi contrast, and reported peak tables (Table-2/3). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, and includes within-participant cue>control). Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study examines alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol and neutral words) and reports whole-brain, cluster-corrected voxelwise results (peaks in Table tbl3), satisfying I3, I5, I6, and I7. However, the NeuroStore extract lists only between-group interaction contrasts (alcohol words in patients > neutral words in controls and the reverse). There is no reported within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (e.g., alcohol words > neutral words within either group). Because it reports only between-group/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control analysis, exclusion criterion E5 applies, so the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study reports a task-evoked fMRI cue-reactivity contrast using visual smoking images vs neutral images (color photographs) in nicotine-dependent participants. The key qualifying analysis is a within-subject (within-group) drug cues > neutral control contrast, with group-level voxelwise random-effects GLM estimated over the whole brain and whole-brain inference; peak coordinates are reported (Table 1). These elements satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for visual cue-reactivity, a within-participant cue>control contrast, and whole-brain voxelwise results. Participant and cue details are provided; missing preprocessing/software or field-strength details do not preclude inclusion per criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This study reports whole-brain voxelwise fMRI cue-reactivity results using visual natural reward cues (food images) versus matched object control images, with group-level cross-subject regressions of behavioral measures (FCI/TFEQ) against task-evoked BOLD. NeuroStore extraction indicates the model used task-based regressors (implying within-subject cue>control contrasts were estimated), whole-brain inference, and tables of peak coordinates are reported. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity (I3), inclusion of within-participant cue>control-derived analyses used in group-level tests (I4), reporting of whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (I5), and availability of coordinates/tables (I6). Some preferred reporting details (I7) such as MRI field strength and participant sex are not fully reported, but that alone does not exclude the study.

This fMRI study investigates natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (commercial food photographs) and reports within-participant contrasts of food>object (e.g., fattening food > object, all food > object). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported as peak coordinates within anatomically defined ROIs (inference restricted to ROIs; reported peaks/tables present), which qualifies as small-volume-corrected voxelwise evidence. Results are presented in tables of coordinates. Participant demographics, cue type, task, and statistical software/model (FSL FLAME) are reported; MRI field strength is not listed but missing details do not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., report-only ROI without voxelwise SVC, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or lack of within-subject contrasts) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it does not report a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (I4 not met). It does meet I3 (fMRI of natural reward cue-reactivity with clear visual fractal cues predicting juice) and I5 (reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results with peak coordinates), and the voxelwise results availability is consistent with I6. The reported analyses are parametric modulators (TD RPE, UPE, expected value) and associations with prediction-error signals rather than a direct cue>control contrast. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the document. Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This fMRI study tests nondrug (monetary) reward cue-reactivity using clear visual cues (circle/triangle magnitude cues) in a Monetary Incentive Delay Task and reports within-participant contrasts of reward cues > control ($1,$10 > $0). Group-level voxelwise, whole-brain statistical results are reported (whole-brain model fit and inference; voxelwise FDR thresholding with coordinate peaks in tables). Results are thus qualifying task-evoked voxelwise findings. Participant demographics (age/sex) and cue type are reported; missing MRI field strength/software does not preclude inclusion per I7. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only (E3), not only connectivity/resting-state (E4), include within-participant cue>control contrasts so E5 does not apply, and the paper is empirical human fMRI (not E6). Full text appears sufficiently represented in the provided document.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cocaine vs neutral pictures (I3). It includes a within-subject Cocaine>Neutral contrast (Analysis 30295396_analysis_0) (I4). The Cocaine>Neutral result is a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analysis with FWE-corrected voxel-level inference and reported peak coordinates (I5). Results are reported in NeuroStore-extracted tables/peaks (acceptable per I6). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported, although MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not; missing these details alone do not exclude the study (I7 is not required). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes a qualifying within-participant contrast, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This study examines visual food cue reactivity (food images > non-food images) in a within-participant design and reports coordinate peaks, meeting inclusion criteria I3 and I4 and acceptable reporting per I6. However, all reported analyses were fit and inference-restricted to predefined anatomical ROIs (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest) with no indication of whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level results. Therefore it does not provide a qualifying whole-brain or SVC voxelwise task-evoked result (I5 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete for extraction (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Study examines alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcoholic beverage pictures in adolescents. It reports within-participant contrasts of alcoholic > nonalcoholic beverage cues (event-related cue-reactivity task) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (linear mixed effects model; inference over whole brain) with reported peak coordinates (Talairach). Missing details (e.g., MRI field strength) do not preclude inclusion per criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical work) are met.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to smoking (drug) vs neutral visual cues using a Posner spatial cueing task and multivariate (searchlight) decoding of smoking versus neutral images. Group-level, whole-brain searchlight inference was performed with FWE correction and reported peak coordinates (tables), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. The design contains within-participant contrasts (decoding smoking vs neutral), and analyses report associations with behavioral attentional-bias measures. Participant age/sex and cue type are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual drug cues), I4 (within-participant cue vs control contrast via decoding), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), and I6 (coordinates reported). Participant demographics and cue type are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group without within-subject contrast) are met. Full text is available via the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

Excluded because the NeuroStore record does not report an explicit within-participant cue>control contrast comparing reward cues to control stimuli. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the extraction shows omnibus within-group and interaction effects (reward × preparation) but no clearly reported reward>nonreward within-subject contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study with clear visual monetary reward cue — British pound coin image vs blank disk), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported; peaks and voxelwise thresholds listed), I6 (voxelwise results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no explicit within-participant reward-cues > control-stimuli contrast is reported in the extracted analyses), I7 (participant age/sex and some acquisition/preprocessing details are not provided in this record). Because I4 is not satisfied and E5 is therefore triggered, the study is excluded.

The study reports fMRI cue-reactivity to visual high-calorie food images versus matched non-food images and includes a within-participant contrast (distraction food > distraction non-food) analyzed with paired t-tests (homeostatic states) and reported as whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE cluster-level inference; reported peaks/tables). This satisfies inclusion criteria: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (peaks/tables reported), and I7 (participant demographics provided). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) apply. Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record.

The task used (Monetary Incentive Delay) includes visual reward cues (I3 met). However, the NeuroStore record only reports a seed-based PPI connectivity analysis of a between-group interaction ([GainA > NongainA Controls] > [GainA > NongainA Meditators]) and no qualifying within-participant cue>control voxelwise task-evoked contrast is provided. Therefore the document does not meet I4 or I5. This violates exclusion criteria E4 (only seed-based connectivity reported without a task-evoked voxelwise result) and E5 (only a between-group interaction reported without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text is available as provided. Result: EXCLUDE.

This fMRI study probes natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (visual masking of sexual vs neutral images). It reports within-subject cue contrasts (Sex > Neu; Sex > Fix) derived from a GLM and provides group-level, voxelwise whole-brain inference (cluster-corrected, Z>2.3) with reported peak coordinates/tables. Participant age and sex are reported. Although the study also includes a stress manipulation (TSST vs control), the qualifying within-participant cue>control contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results are present and meet the meta-analysis requirements. Missing details (e.g., MRI field strength) do not preclude inclusion per I7.

The study examines natural reward (palatable food) cues using visual stimuli (color photographs) so I3 is met. However, all reported analyses are ROI-based (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest) with no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results (violates I5), and the extracted contrasts are reported as between-group comparisons (HD > ND, HD > CD) with no within-participant cue>control contrast presented (violates I4). Therefore the study meets exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only results with no qualifying voxelwise outcome) and E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5 (also I6 not applicable). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study reports a task-evoked fMRI cue-reactivity analysis using visual food images (natural reward) versus matched non-food control images during a cue-reactivity task in smokers (I3 satisfied). The reported contrast involves food images > control images within a within-group design (an interaction across pre/post intervention that includes the cue>control term), fulfilling the requirement for a within-participant cue>control contrast (I4). The analysis is a group-level voxelwise result fit and inferred across the whole brain with cluster correction and reported peak coordinates in a table, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise reporting (I5,I6). Participant and task details are provided (I7 preferred details present though some acquisition details are missing). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), not only connectivity/resting-state (E4), and not solely between-group contrasts without a within-participant cue>control (E5). Given these points, the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This study examines neural responses to food images (natural rewards) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group results (Monte Carlo cluster correction) for contrasts of high versus low calorie food image viewing, so it meets I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported in tables/coordinates). However, it does not report a within-participant contrast of reward-related cues > control stimuli (e.g., food>non-food or cue>baseline) in the NeuroStore-extracted analyses: the reported contrasts are high versus low calorie foods and age/hunger effects. Although the task included non-food items, no food>non-food or cue>control whole-brain contrast is listed. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) directly apply based on the provided record.

The study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual alcohol-related images vs neutral images (I3). It includes a within-participant cue contrast (ARCs vs neutral) at the group level (within-group contrast; GLM with cue condition), satisfying I4. The analysis reports voxelwise inference with a small-volume correction (SVC) within predefined ROIs (amygdala, insula, OFC, ACC, DLPFC), meeting the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results via SVC (I5). Coordinates/space (Talairach) and reported peaks are provided, consistent with I6. Participant demographics (age, sex) and cue type are reported, satisfying I7 (preferred details present). Although the sample is small (n=5) and the model is described as fixed-effects, neither is an exclusion per the criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study reports a within-subject, group-level voxelwise contrast of alcohol cues > water cues (Analysis 24411804_analysis_0) with whole-brain inference and cluster correction and reports peak coordinates (Table 3). The task includes clear visual cue components (white wine and visual labels) and qualifies as drug-related cue-reactivity. Multiple additional voxelwise regression and interaction analyses (whole-brain) relating subjective responses to cue-evoked BOLD are reported and coordinate tables are provided. Participant demographics and clinical details are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI cue-reactivity and should be included.

This study investigates social and monetary reward processing using visual cues (SID and MID), and reports voxelwise results (whole-brain and small-volume-corrected coordinates in tables), so it meets I3, I5 and I6. However, none of the reported analyses present a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control (reward cue > neutral/control) — the extracted contrasts are mainly MID > SID (monetary vs social) or group-level comparisons and interactions. Therefore it does not satisfy I4, and it violates exclusion criterion E5 (studies that do not include a qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). I7 (reporting of MRI field strength and preprocessing/software) is not fully documented in the extracted record. Conclusion: EXCLUDED (E5).

This fMRI study uses explicit visual cues (coin images) in a Monetary Incentive Delay task, meeting I3. It includes within-participant contrasts of high- vs low-reward cues (€1.00 > €0.05), satisfying I4. It reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain inference (Analysis 21459835_analysis_0: €1.00 > €0.05, whole-brain FWE cluster-level), meeting I5. Results are reported in tables/peaks (analyses report peaks and tables), so I6 is met. Participant age and sex are reported, and cue type is described (though some preprocessing/MRI details are not listed); this does not preclude inclusion per criteria. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is not ROI-only (has whole-brain results), not limited to connectivity-only, and contains within-subject cue>control contrasts. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual reward cue-reactivity.

This study uses visual natural-reward cues (food pictures) meeting I3. It reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (multiple analyses with voxel-wise tests and reported peak coordinates), satisfying I5 and I6 (results reported in tables) and provides participant age/sex and cue type information (I7). However, all extracted analyses are between-group contrasts/interactions comparing groups on the high-energy>neutral effect (e.g., NW>Obese, NW>SWL, SWL>Obese, Obese>SWL) and do not present a standalone within-participant cue>control contrast (no simple main-effect cue>neutral voxelwise result reported). Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies: the paper reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion ID not met: I4. Exclusion IDs met: E5. Full text is available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study includes visual reward cues (I3) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with reported peak coordinates (I5, I6). However, the NeuroStore extraction does not report any within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli or natural-reward-cues > control stimuli (I4 not met). The reported within-group contrast is 'withdrawal > smoking' (a state comparison) and the main other reported result is a between-group interaction; no explicit cue>control within-subject cue-reactivity contrast is available in the provided document. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies (only between-group/interaction contrasts or no qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears available in the record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study of a natural reward (food) that includes a clear visual cue component (42 pictures per category), satisfying I3. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of high-calorie food > nonfood (analyses 0 and 1) and gustatory contrasts, satisfying I4. Model fitting was over the whole brain with inference restricted using FWE small-volume correction and reported peak coordinates (Table 1), which constitutes qualifying voxelwise, small-volume-corrected group-level results, satisfying I5 and I6. Participant and task details are reported; missing preferred items (e.g., field strength) do not preclude inclusion per I7. No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only (E3) because SVC voxelwise results are reported, not solely connectivity or between-group-only contrasts (E4/E5). Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study uses visual natural reward cues (erotic pictures) and reports within-subject contrasts of positive>negative stimuli (Analysis: Positive4negative stimuli: positive > negative), satisfying a within-participant cue>control contrast for natural rewards. Model fitting was whole-brain and NeuroStore reports coordinate peaks (tables), so at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain result is available. Visual cue type, participant age and sex are reported. Although MRI field strength and preprocessing software are not listed, missing these details does not preclude inclusion per I7. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and not only between-group contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

Excluded because the paper reports only region-of-interest (ROI) voxelwise modeling and inference (model fit and inference restricted to a composite ROI mask), meeting exclusion criterion E3. The study does include a within-participant reward>baseline contrast (I4 satisfied). However, it does not meet key inclusion requirements: I3 (task does not present drug or clear natural reward cues—stimuli are abstract card/arrow/feedback cues rather than drug or natural (e.g., food) visual cues), I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise result reported; inference was limited to ROI), and I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results reported in tables/figures as whole-brain/SVC). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study reports task-evoked whole-brain fMRI responses to visual food cues (natural rewards) using a cue-reactivity task with pictures of hedonic foods and neutral nonfood objects. It includes within-participant contrasts of hedonic food cues > nonfood objects (reported as whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates/tables) and group-level repeated-measures analyses comparing baseline and chronic exercise. Thresholding and cluster reporting are provided. Participant demographics and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, contains within-subject cue>control contrasts, empirical task fMRI).

Excluded: The report shows only a region-of-interest group analysis (model fit over: region of interest) rather than whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results (meets exclusion E3). The only reported group-level contrast is an interaction/between-group comparison (DRD4L > DRD4S for smoking>control); no standalone within-participant smoking>control voxelwise result is reported (meets exclusion E5). The study does meet I3 (visual smoking cues) but does not provide a qualifying within-subject cue>control voxelwise result or whole-brain/SVC result (I4 and I5 not met).

The study investigates cue-reactivity to food (a natural reward) using visual stimuli (photographs of appetizing vs. plain foods). It reports within-participant contrasts involving appetizing>plain (used in within-group regression analyses correlating craving with activation) and reports a group-level voxelwise, whole-brain task-evoked result (analysis 0: whole-brain appetizing vs. plain contrast with voxelwise FDR thresholding). Coordinate peaks are reported in tables. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective and key inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only (it includes a whole-brain group-level voxelwise result), not connectivity/resting-state only, and it provides within-participant contrasts in addition to between-group comparisons. Some preferred methodological details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not listed in the extracted record, but missing these does not preclude inclusion per the protocol.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual alcohol advertisements (I3). It reports within-subject ALCOHOL > CONTROL contrasts (analyses 0 and 1) and a cross-subject regression relating neural responses to drinking scores (analysis 2), satisfying the requirement for a within-participant cue>control contrast (I4). All analyses were conducted as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects GLMs with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates/tables, meeting the voxelwise result requirement (I5) and acceptable reporting formats (I6). Participant demographics and cue type are reported; missing details (e.g., field strength/software) do not exclude the study per I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting, includes within-participant contrasts, empirical task-evoked data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study used visual erotic pictures (IAPS) as natural reward cues and measured BOLD responses, satisfying I3. It reports within-participant contrasts of erotic > neutral (analyses 0–2,6), satisfying I4. Several of these contrasts are group-level voxelwise results with whole-brain inference and FWE cluster correction, meeting I5. Voxelwise results are reported as peaks/tables, so I6 is also satisfied. Participant demographics and cue type are reported; MRI field strength is not stated but this missing detail does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and within-subject cue>control contrasts are present).

The study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual smoking images (International Smoking Image Series) comparing smoking > neutral cues. Group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM, whole-brain) are reported with peak coordinates/tables across multiple contrasts, satisfying a qualifying within-participant drug-cue>control contrast and whole-brain voxelwise results. Participant demographics and cue details are reported; missing MRI field strength/software does not preclude inclusion per I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s requirement for a clear visual cue component (I3 not met): the task used individually tailored audiotaped mental imagery scripts (auditory), with no visual stimuli or multimodal design including visual cues reported. It also does not present a within-participant drug-cue > control-stimulus contrast required by the meta-analysis (I4 not met). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported with FWE cluster correction and coordinates/peaks), I6 (voxelwise results reported in tables), I7 (participant age/sex and other details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete in this record.

This study reports whole-brain, voxelwise cue-reactivity results for methamphetamine (MA) and sexual visual cues (satisfies I3, I5, I6). However, it does not report a within-participant drug-cues > control (e.g., MA > neutral) or a natural-reward > control (e.g., sex > neutral) contrast. The reported analyses are a between-group interaction comparing patients vs controls for MA cues and a within-group contrast of sex > MA (natural reward > drug), not natural reward > neutral. Because no qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast is provided, it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group/interaction contrasts or non-qualifying within-group contrasts). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study examines natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high-energy, low-energy, neutral images), satisfying the review scope. It reports within-participant contrasts of reward cues > control (High>Neutral, Low>Neutral, High>Low) at the group level (Analyses 0–2) and provides whole-brain voxelwise results with correction (FDR P<0.05, cluster extent 10) and reported peak coordinates (tables). Results are available in tables of peaks. Participant demographics and cue types are reported. Although the paper also includes between-group interaction contrasts (restrained vs. unrestrained eaters), the presence of the within-subject, whole-brain, task-evoked cue>control contrasts meets inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This fMRI study includes visual alcohol-related pictures (and odors) and reports task-evoked alcohol>control contrasts. The record explicitly states alcohol-related visual and olfactory cues elicited significant increases at baseline (i.e., within-participant cue>control effects) and provides whole-brain voxelwise inference and tables of reported peaks (coordinates in Table t0010) with cluster-level FWE correction. Thus it satisfies the requirement for a clear visual cue component (I3), at least one within-participant drug-cues>control contrast (I4), whole-brain voxelwise results (I5), and availability of coordinate results (I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only results, connectivity-only, or absence of within-subject cue>control contrasts) are met. Full text appears available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It used visual cues (images of e-cigarettes with colored stickers) together with olfactory delivery, satisfying I3 (visual cue component). Multiple within-subject contrasts of cue responses are reported (Sight: Sweet; Sight: Nicotine; Sight: Sweet×Nicotine), meeting I4. Group-level voxelwise results are reported with small-volume correction (SVC) for peak-level tests and whole-brain FWE-corrected cluster results for regression analyses, satisfying I5. Reported peaks/tables are present (Table tbl0001), satisfying I6. Participant demographics and task/cue details are provided, meeting I7. No exclusion criteria apply: results are task-evoked voxelwise contrasts (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it reports a visual cue-reactivity task using heroin-related images versus natural/neutral stimuli (I3), includes a within-participant contrast heroin-related > natural stimuli (I4), and provides group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results with whole-brain inference and a table of 34 reported peak coordinates (satisfies I5 and I6). Participant details (age, sex, cue type) are reported; MRI field strength and preprocessing software are not listed but missing details alone do not exclude the study (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and include a within-subject cue>control contrast. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study in chronic smokers using visual stimuli (anti-smoking, ISIS, IAPS, neutral, and cigarette images) and a block Cue Reactivity Task. It reports within-subject contrasts of interest (appetitive smoking-related > neutral; aversive smoking-related > neutral; aversive smoking > aversive IAPS) at the group level, with whole-brain voxelwise model fitting and whole-brain inference and coordinates reported (tables of peaks). Thresholding and cluster-correction are described. Participant demographics (age, sex) and cue types are reported. These facts satisfy the review inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise fMRI results linking cue-evoked expected value to BOLD activity for natural rewards (apple juice, monetary gain) and aversive outcomes. Visual cues are present (affectively neutral geometric-form cues predicting pictured outcomes) and specific parametric within-subject modulations of expected value for apple juice and monetary rewards are reported (positive modulatory effects and a conjunction/global unsigned EV). These constitute within-participant cue-related contrasts (parametric cue EV > baseline/control) and are reported as coordinates from whole-brain voxelwise analyses, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. Participant and task details are provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria for natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual cues and provides qualifying voxelwise results.

This fMRI study uses visual cue images (methamphetamine, sexual, neutral) so I3 is satisfied. The NeuroStore record reports a whole-brain, group-level 3x3 mixed-effects ANOVA (group × condition interaction) with voxelwise inference (FWE cluster-level), so I5 is satisfied. However, the record does not report any within-participant cue>control contrasts (e.g., methamphetamine>neutral or sexual>neutral); only a between-group interaction is listed. Thus I4 is not met and exclusion criterion E5 applies (studies reporting only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Because a required inclusion criterion (I4) is missing and E5 is met, the study must be excluded.

This study meets the review objective and required inclusion criteria. It reports visual natural reward (food) cue reactivity using an fMRI cue-reactivity task with images of high-calorie foods vs neutral non-foods (I3). It includes within-participant contrasts of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (high-calorie foods > neutral non-foods) in analyses 2 and 3 (I4). The statistical results are group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain task-evoked analyses with reported peak coordinates/tables (model fit and inference over whole brain, reported peaks), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results (I5); coordinates/peaks are reported in tables, acceptable per I6. Participant demographics and cue type are reported; some preprocessing/MRI field-strength details are not provided but omission does not exclude the study (I7 is preferred, not mandatory). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or lack of within-subject cue>control contrasts) apply. Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record.

This is an fMRI study of cue-reactivity to drug-related visual stimuli (e-cigarette advertising images) presented to adolescents. It reports a within-participant contrast (e-cigarette > neutral advertising images) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise inference and peak coordinates (cluster-corrected), and provides participant age/sex and task details. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual drug cues), I4 (within-participant drug>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables), and I7 (participant/task details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts).

The NeuroStore record shows this fMRI study used a monetary incentive delay task (natural reward) with visual win/loss/neutral cues (satisfying I3). It reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results with FWE-corrected peaks in tables (satisfying I5 and I6). Participant/sample and task details are reported (I7).
