However, the extracted analyses are described as omnibus, between-group contrasts (Contrast: omnibus, between-group) and the NeuroStore extraction does not provide any within-participant cue>control (e.g., reward>neutral) voxelwise contrast or result. Therefore the study reports only between-group/omnibus effects without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast, meeting exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported). Exclusion criteria met: E5. Full text appears available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Although the study is an fMRI task with visual reward cues (erotic, monetary) and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume FWE correction (meeting I3, I5, I6) and reports participant demographics (I7), it does NOT report any within-participant cue>control (reward>neutral) contrasts. Reported contrasts are monetary>erotic (within-group) and between-group interactions (gamblers vs controls). Because no qualifying within-subject reward>control contrast is available (I4 not met), exclusion criterion E5 applies (study reports only between-group/interaction contrasts or non-qualifying within-subject contrasts). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study uses visual cues (drug and neutral words; money reminders) and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with peak coordinates (satisfying I3, I5, I6, and participant reporting I7). However, all listed analyses are between-group contrasts and interactions (e.g., group-by-money condition interactions, patient>control contrasts involving 50¢ vs 0¢ across groups) and no within-participant cue>control (e.g., 50¢>0¢ or drug-cue>neutral) contrast is reported as a standalone within-subject result. Therefore it fails the required within-participant cue>control criterion (I4). This meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Conclusion: EXCLUDE.

The study reports task-evoked fMRI responses to drug-related visual cues (alcohol and cannabis words presented in a Stroop task). It includes within-participant contrasts of cannabis>color (drug cues > control stimuli) in both AUD (n=21) and healthy control (n=18) groups, and group-level voxelwise whole-brain inference (model fit and inference over whole brain) with cluster correction; peak coordinates are reported in tables. Participant age/sex and task details are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria: it is an fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity using clear visual stimuli (photographs of heroin use and neutral scenes), includes within-participant contrasts of heroin-related > neutral (analyses 0 and 1), and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results with FWE-corrected inference and tables of peak coordinates. Although MRI field strength and preprocessing/software details are not reported in the NeuroStore record, missing those items does not exclude the study per I7. No exclusion criteria are met (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and include within-participant cue>control contrasts).

The study uses visual smoking and affective cues (I3 met) but does not report a within-participant cue>control voxelwise contrast (I4 not met) and the reported analysis is an ROI-based group × valence interaction with inference restricted to an anatomical mask (only ROI results). This violates exclusion criteria E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain or SVC voxelwise result) and E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interaction without an accompanying within-participant drug-cue>control contrast). No full-text access issues noted.

The study examines visual food cue reactivity (natural reward) and reports voxelwise whole-brain and small-volume-corrected task-evoked results, and participant details are provided. However, all reported analyses in the NeuroStore record are between-group interaction contrasts (e.g., MC4R-deficient > obese controls for appetizing/disgusting foods vs non-foods) or ROI SVC group comparisons. I find no standalone within-participant cue>control contrast (a subject-level appetizing>non-foods or similar main effect) reported as a qualifying voxelwise result. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast).

The study examines cocaine cue-reactivity using visual word cues (drug and matched neutral words), satisfying I3. NeuroStore lists within-group simple-effect analyses (T CUD, T Control) and regression analyses tied to task conditions, indicating within-participant contrasts of drug vs. control stimuli, satisfying I4. Several analyses report voxelwise group-level results with whole-brain inference (and some with small-volume correction), satisfying I5. Voxelwise results are reported as peaks/tables (Table 1), satisfying I6. Although not all preferred metadata (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are reported, I7 is only preferred and its absence does not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: the paper reports whole-brain and SVC task-evoked voxelwise results rather than ROI-only or connectivity/resting-state-only findings. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

This is an fMRI study using visual cues (greyscale photographs) that contrast monetary reward-predicting cues versus other cues and neutral cues. The NeuroStore record shows within-participant contrasts involving reward-related anticipation (reward > punishment) and contrasts of reward-/punishment-predicting > neutral, and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume FWE-corrected inference and coordinates (Table t0005). Thus it meets the review’s requirement for natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts (reward- and/or reward+punishment > neutral are reported), and provides qualifying voxelwise, small-volume-corrected results. The report includes coordinate tables and sufficient task/cue description. Full text is available via the NeuroStore extraction.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of natural reward (milkshake) cue-reactivity that includes explicit visual cues (images of glasses) and multimodal taste receipt, satisfying I3. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of milkshake cue/receipt > tasteless control (e.g., ‘‘milkshake receipt > tasteless solution receipt’’ and milkshake cue contrasts), satisfying I4. Analyses were whole-brain voxelwise with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates (model fit over: whole brain; inference over: whole brain; reported peaks), meeting I5 and I6. Participant/cue details are provided though some MRI acquisition/preprocessing details are not fully listed — acceptable per I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the cue-reactivity meta-analysis of visual natural reward cues.

The study examines natural reward cue-reactivity using visual cues (images of milkshakes vs tasteless solution) and reports within-participant cue contrasts (unpaired milkshake cue > unpaired tasteless cue) for both low-risk and high-risk groups (analyses 21430137_analysis_3 and _7). Model fits were performed over the whole brain and several within-group contrasts report voxelwise results (voxel-level p<0.001, reported peaks/tables), satisfying the requirement for at least one group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. Between-group contrasts used ROI inference, but this does not exclude the study because qualifying whole-brain voxelwise within-participant cue>control contrasts are present. Visual cue component, within-participant cue>control contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise reporting, and coordinate/table reporting are all met. Some methodological details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not reported, but missing these does not preclude inclusion per I7. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

The study reports task-evoked voxelwise results (small-volume-corrected, pFWE<0.05) for Monetary Incentive Delay reward cues, with group-level within-participant contrasts of gain>nongain (one-sample t-test across participants and within-group regressions in patients). Peak coordinates are reported in tables. Although NeuroStore notes analyses were restricted to prior-defined volumes (ROI), inference used SVC which meets the meta-analysis requirement for small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. The task involves monetary reward cues (Monetary Incentive Delay Task), which are conventionally visual cues and are reported as ‘stimuli: Monetary reward cues’; while modality is not explicitly stated in the extraction, the MID task implies visual cues. Participant demographics and cue-related contrasts are reported. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI without SVC, only connectivity, only between-group without within-subject cue>control) are met.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of high-calorie food vs non-food). It reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results: model fit over whole brain with inference via FWE small-volume correction and reported peak coordinates in tables. At least one within-participant contrast (high-calorie food > non-food) is tested in group-level regression analyses. Participant demographics (age/sex/BMI) are reported. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study uses visual cues (greyscale photographs) and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume FWE correction (coordinates/tables provided), but the NeuroStore record does not include a within-participant contrast of reward-predicting cues > neutral/control. Available within-subject contrasts are reward>punishment and punishment>neutral, and many reported contrasts are between-group (DAT genotype interactions). Because the meta-analysis requires at least one within-participant natural reward-related cue > control contrast, this study does not meet inclusion criterion I4 and therefore must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cue component), I5 (group-level whole-brain / small-volume-corrected voxelwise result), I6 (coordinate reporting). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant reward>control contrast reported). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying qualifying within-participant reward>control contrast).

The study uses the Monetary Incentive Delay task with visual cues signaling monetary reward/loss, and reports group-level voxelwise within-participant contrasts of reward anticipation (anticipation of reward > anticipation of no outcome) and related feedback contrasts. At least one qualifying whole-brain FWE-corrected result is reported (analyses 0 and 1), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics are reported. The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of natural (monetary) reward-related cue processing with visual cues, meeting inclusion criteria and not meeting any exclusion criteria.

The NeuroStore record reports only a between-group omnibus contrast (Contrast: omnibus, between-group) for food-related activation; no within-participant cue>control (e.g., food > control/neutral) contrast is provided. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues — Food-pics images), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise result with reported peaks; model fit and inference over whole brain), I6 (voxelwise results reported as table of coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported). Exclusion criterion E5 applies: study reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast. Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The NeuroStore record describes an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual food images (I3 met). However, the only fully described voxelwise analysis is a group x time interaction reported within a region-of-interest (striatum), and no qualifying within-participant cue>control (e.g., high-calorie > low-calorie or > non-food) whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise result is provided. Therefore the paper appears to report ROI-only and interaction/between-group results. Exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only with no qualifying voxelwise result) and E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast) are met. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast) and I5 (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise result). fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study examines monetary reward anticipation using a Monetary Incentive Delay task with explicit visual cues (nine geometric cues), satisfying visual-cue requirement. It reports within-participant simple-effect contrasts for gain-anticipation (and loss-anticipation) at multiple reward magnitudes (within-subject contrasts of reward-related cues), which correspond to natural reward-related cue>control-type contrasts. Group-level voxelwise statistics were fit and inferred over the whole brain and peak coordinates are reported (Table 4), meeting the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results; coordinates are available. Participant sex and sample size are reported; missing minor details do not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual food stimuli (I3 satisfied). It reports a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrast (HC>LC) with FWE correction and peak coordinates (I5 satisfied) and results are presented in tables (I6 satisfied). However, the reported primary analyses use the within-subject contrast high-caloric > low-caloric food cues (HC>LC) rather than a natural reward-related cues > control-stimuli contrast (e.g., food > non-food). The document does not report any HC or food > non-food whole-brain contrast meeting the criterion. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met, and the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the available report. Full text is complete in the provided record.

Study examines natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food pictures and a cue-reactivity task. It reports within-participant contrasts of high-calorie > control and low-calorie > control (one-sample t-tests at group level), satisfying the required cue>control contrasts. Results are reported as voxelwise peaks with small-volume correction within a priori ROIs (FWE SVC), meeting the requirement for group-level voxelwise, small-volume-corrected evidence (peaks reported in tables). Participant details (n, age, sex) and cue types are provided. No exclusion criteria are met: although analyses were ROI-restricted, they include SVC voxelwise results (so not E3), and task-evoked within-subject contrasts are reported (so not E5). Full text appears available via the NeuroStore record.

The study directly addresses visual cue-reactivity to alcoholic beverage images (I3). It reports a within-participant cue>control contrast (alcpic > con) (I4). The alcpic>con analysis is a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates (I5, I6). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported (and while some preprocessing/MRI field-strength details are not extracted here, missing these does not preclude inclusion) (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: the study reports whole-brain voxelwise task results (not ROI-only), is not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and includes the required within-participant cue>control contrast. Therefore INCLUDE.

The study is an fMRI investigation of natural (food) reward with clear visual cues (pictures of snack baskets) and reports a small-volume FWE-corrected voxelwise finding in medial OFC (so I3 and I5 are satisfied; peaks/results are extracted, satisfying I6). However, the NeuroStore extraction shows only between-group interaction contrasts (patients > controls for receipt of high vs no food reward); no standalone within-participant cue>control (high vs no reward) voxelwise contrast is reported. Thus the paper reports only between-group interactions without an accompanying qualifying within-subject cue>control result, violating exclusion criterion E5. Therefore the study is excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual (natural reward) stimuli (explicit PEN images) with block design and within-subject contrasts (e.g., PEN > NEU). Group-level voxelwise results are reported with whole-brain inference (FWE voxel-level and cluster-level) and small-volume correction reported for specific regions (analysis 7). Coordinate tables and reported peaks are available (Tables 1–3). Participant demographics (age, sex, contraceptive status) and task details are reported. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity, includes qualifying within-participant cue>control contrasts, and provides whole-brain and small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete in the provided record.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual alcohol cues (pictures) in alcohol-dependent participants, meeting I3. It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol > neutral beverage for Scan 1 and Scan 2 (and a Scan2>Scan1 interaction), satisfying I4. Results are reported as voxelwise peaks in MNI space within an anatomically defined striatal region of interest, with multiple-comparison correction and cluster-level thresholding; inference was restricted to the ROI (small-volume-style voxelwise results), fulfilling I5 and I6 (coordinates/peaks reported). No exclusion criteria apply: although analyses were ROI-focused, they constitute small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results rather than only ROI summary statistics, so E3 is not met. Participant demographics and task details are reported; full text appears sufficiently represented in this record.

This study reports a task-based fMRI cue-reactivity experiment using visual alcohol-related pictures and neutral control pictures, with group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (model fit over whole brain; reported peaks = 3). The analysis is a within-group cross-subject regression including a 'condition' term, indicating task-evoked contrasts were used in the model (likely alcohol cues versus control), and produced voxelwise statistical results (thresholding reported). Thus it meets the review objective and inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity and whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked reporting. Although the NeuroStore record does not explicitly label a contrast as 'alcohol cues > control stimuli', the presence of a Cue Reactivity Task with alcohol and neutral picture conditions and a within-group condition term supporting voxelwise reported peaks provides reasonable support that a within-participant cue>control contrast was evaluated. Full text appears available in the record (not incomplete).

The study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it is an fMRI study of natural reward (monetary) cue-reactivity using visual cues (MID task with visual stimuli) (I3). It reports a within-participant contrast of reward vs neutral conditions (win miss > neutral miss) (I4). At least one qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result was tested and reported as whole-brain inference with reported peaks/coordinates (Model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain; Table 2) (I5,I6). Participant demographics (age/sex) and cue type are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete in the provided record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (appetizing vs bland photos), satisfying natural reward cue-reactivity. It reports a within-participant contrast appetizing>bland (analysis 22319604_analysis_0) and provides whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with voxel-level FDR correction and reported peak coordinates. Coordinate tables and peaks are present. Although the paper also reports connectivity and group contrasts, it includes the required within-subject task-evoked voxelwise evidence. Some preferred reporting details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software, participant sex) are not fully listed in the NeuroStore record, but I7 is a non-exclusionary preference. No exclusion criteria (only ROI, only connectivity, lack of within-subject contrast, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion for the meta-analysis of visual reward cue-reactivity.

This is a task-based fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (50 smoking-related pictures vs neutral). It reports within-participant contrasts (smoking > neutral) for control and hypnotic states, with group-level voxelwise results estimated and tested over the whole brain (FWE thresholding) and peak coordinates reported in tables. Participant characteristics and cue type are provided. Although one participant-sex count appears inconsistent, that does not prevent inclusion. All required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study investigates neural responses to food images (natural reward visual cues) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group results (tables of peak coordinates). However, all extracted contrasts are between-group comparisons or interactions (controls vs hypoleptinemic patients across weeks); no within-participant cue>control (food>nonfood) contrast within subjects is reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-subject cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual food cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported), I6 (results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete in the provided record.

This is a human fMRI cue-reactivity study in nicotine-dependent smokers using audio-video clips that include explicit visual smoking cues (multimodal with visual component). It reports within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > non-smoking control clips (SCs > non-SCs) at the group level (random-effects GLM) with whole-brain model fit and reported peak coordinates/tables. These meet the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue content (I3), the presence of within-participant cue>control contrasts (I4), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported as coordinates (I5, I6). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported (I7); MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not detailed in this record, but that missing information alone does not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to visual sexual cues (natural rewards) using a Visual Masking Task with explicit sexual, aversive, food, and neutral visual stimuli. It reports a within-subject contrast of sexual > neutral (analysis 31998091_analysis_3: sexual > neutral) used in a cross-subject regression, and group-level voxelwise results with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates (tables). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant sexual>neutral contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results), I6 (coordinates/tables reported), and I7 (participant and cue details reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes a within-subject cue>control contrast). Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record.

This study examines neural responses to visual food cues (food pictures) and tests a within-subject contrast food > non-food. The analysis is a group-level GLM fit over the whole brain with reported peak coordinates (Table 3), satisfying the requirement for a voxelwise task-evoked result. Thus it meets the review’s criteria for natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical fMRI data).

This study directly addresses drug cue-reactivity using visual heroin-related images vs. neutral IAPS images during an fMRI cue-reactivity task. It reports within-participant contrasts of heroin>neutral (several analyses) at the group level using voxelwise whole-brain analysis (FLAME/FILM) with peaks reported in tables (Table t3), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics, cue type, task design, and statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This study uses visual food cues (palatable food images) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (coordinates in Table 2), and reports participant demographics. However, none of the reported contrasts are a within-participant natural reward-cue > control-stimulus contrast; all contrasts compare cognitive reappraisal instructions (e.g., costs of eating > imagine eating, suppress craving > imagine eating) while viewing food images. Thus inclusion criterion I4 (at least one within-participant cue>control contrast) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the available information.

Study examines cue-reactivity to smoking-related visual images in nicotine-dependent participants using an fMRI delay-match-to-sample working memory task. It reports within-subject contrasts of smoking > neutral (and neutral > smoking) with whole-brain voxelwise inference and cluster-thresholding, and reports peak coordinates (table). Participant demographics and cue details are provided. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria for visual drug-cue fMRI studies with group-level voxelwise results.

The paper reports whole-brain multivariate (PLSC) group-level results for visual cue-reactivity (cannabis and natural reward cues) with peaks in tables, satisfying I3 (visual cue component), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), and I6 (coordinates reported in tables). However, the NeuroStore record indicates contrasts are reported as LVs with simple effect between-group results rather than a within-participant cue>control (e.g., drug cues > control) contrast. No explicit within-subject cue>control contrast is provided in the extracted analyses. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies (only between-group contrasts without qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. Full text appears readable in the record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This fMRI study examines alcohol-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of alcohol-related objects) and reports a within-participant contrast comparing alcohol vs. neutral cues during successful NoGo trials in the AUD group. The analyses are group-level voxelwise (model fit over whole brain) with inference using small-volume FWE correction (voxelwise SVC), and peak coordinates are reported (tables of peaks). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported. These elements satisfy the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity, a within-participant cue>control contrast, and a qualifying voxelwise (small-volume-corrected) group-level result. No exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the NeuroStore record reports only between-group interaction contrasts (sex differences: M>F and F>M for high- vs low-energy food cues) and does not report any within-participant cue>control contrasts. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward cue-reactivity with a visual component — visual and multimodal food cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise results reported over whole brain), I6 (results reported as peak coordinates/tables), I7 (participant age/sex and other demographics reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrasts reported in the document). fulltext_incomplete: false.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food vs scenery). It reports within-participant contrasts of food>scenery (paired t-tests / mixed-effects GLM) across expectancy states. Importantly, several analyses are reported as whole-brain voxelwise results with correction for multiple comparisons (Analyses 5, 6, 7; tables of peak coordinates provided), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics (n=10, age, sex, BMI) and task/stimulus details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROIs only, are task-evoked rather than connectivity/resting-state, and include within-subject cue>control contrasts. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study reports only a seed-based psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity analysis (seed: VTA) comparing treatment conditions (Placebo > Oxytocin) with model terms including condition and PPI, fit and inferred at the whole-brain level. While it involves visual natural reward cues (high-calorie food images) and reports participant demographics, the NeuroStore record does not present any task-evoked voxelwise activation contrast of cue>control (e.g., high-calorie > nonfood) as a within-participant cue>control contrast. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (only seed-based/effective/connectivity analyses without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues present) and I7 (participant age/sex and cue type reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no explicit within-participant cue>control contrast reported) and I5 (no task-evoked voxelwise activation result reported). fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to sexual stimuli and sexual cues (natural rewards) using visual pictures and videos with cue expectation phases, satisfying the review’s focus on visual cue-reactivity. It reports within-participant contrasts SEM>NEUTRAL and CUESEM>CUENEUTRAL at the group level, with whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE voxel-level) and small-volume-corrected ROI results. NeuroStore extraction lists whole-brain analyses (analyses 0 and 4) and reported peak coordinates (tables), meeting the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics and stimulus details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-state-only; includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study investigates visual cocaine cue reactivity and reports whole-brain group-level task-evoked BOLD results (peaks in Table t2) and seed-based gPPI connectivity analyses. However, the reported voxelwise BOLD contrast appears to be a between-group interaction rather than a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast. All other reported voxelwise results are seed-based connectivity (gPPI). The report therefore lacks a qualifying within-participant group-level cocaine>neutral task contrast. Per criteria, this meets exclusion E5 (only between-group/interaction results without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked result reported whole-brain), I6 (results reported in tables), I7 (participant/cue info reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant drug>control contrast). Full text appears complete enough for this judgment.

The study examines neural responses to visual natural reward cues (food images) and reports within-participant contrasts of food cues > control objects (e.g., Pre-Fast/Post-Fast Food > Objects; Pre-HCD/Post-HCD High-calorie > Low-calorie). Group-level voxelwise results are reported and tested with small-volume FWE correction within a priori ROIs, with peak coordinates provided (MNI). These satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for visual natural-reward cue-reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrasts, and group-level small-volume-corrected voxelwise reporting. No exclusion criteria are met (not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical).

The study reports a within-participant contrast of anticipation of monetary reward > anticipation of verbal feedback (Analysis 28488021_analysis_1), which is a cue-reactivity contrast for a natural (monetary) reward. The task includes a clear visual cue component (arrow cue) indicating reward, satisfying the visual-cue requirement. The qualifying analysis is reported as a voxelwise, region-restricted inference (ROI in ventral striatum) with FWE-corrected voxel-level results and reported peak coordinates (2 peaks), meeting the ‘whole-brain or small-volume-corrected’ requirement. Coordinate reporting is present. No exclusion criteria apply. MRI field strength/software not reported but this is allowed. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

The study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual stimuli (25 smoking-related and 25 neutral pictures), meeting I3. It includes within-participant contrasts of smoking pictures > neutral pictures in both normal and hypnotic states (Analyses 1 and 2), meeting I4. Model fitting was performed over the whole brain and inference/thresholding is reported voxelwise (whole-brain FWE/uncorrected thresholds; reported peak tables), satisfying I5 and I6. Participant demographics and cue type are reported; MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not specified but I7 allows missing such details. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), not limited to connectivity/resting-state without task-evoked voxelwise results (E4), and include within-participant cue>control contrasts (not only between-group; E5). Full text appears available via the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This fMRI study uses visual reward cues (faces and peripheral bars) and reports within-participant contrasts of reward>neutral (faces indicating reward > neutral faces). It includes at least one group-level voxelwise, whole-brain result (Analysis 24307490_analysis_1: reward > neutral, FWE voxel-level whole-brain), and also reports small-volume-corrected ROI results; coordinate-space and peak coordinates are provided. Participant age/sex and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual reward cue-reactivity and qualifying voxelwise results.

The study examines visual food cues (320 color photographs) in anorexia nervosa patients and healthy controls, i.e. natural reward-related visual stimuli (meets I3). The NeuroStore record reports within-participant (within-group) contrasts that compare food versus non-food conditions (interaction contrasts in analyses 7 and 8), satisfying the requirement for a within-participant cue>control-type contrast (I4). The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results estimated over the whole brain with voxelwise thresholding (analyses 6–8), meeting the whole-brain/small-volume requirement (I5). Coordinate reporting and peak tables are present, consistent with I6. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting) apply.

This study is excluded because it does not report an explicit within-participant cue>control contrast required by I4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward: food cue-reactivity with visual stimuli), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported with coordinates/cluster-level inference), I6 (results reported in table of peaks). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no clear within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli is reported in the NeuroStore extraction; extracted analyses are main effects for portion size and energy density and their interaction, not a food>control contrast). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text is complete in the provided record.

Excluded because the reported group-level voxelwise analyses are restricted to region-of-interest (ROI) analyses and no whole-brain or explicitly small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise result is reported (Exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual drug cues), I4 (within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral/control are reported), I6 (voxel coordinates/MNI peaks are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no evidence in the document of a whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked result). Therefore the study must be excluded under E3.

This study examines natural reward (food) cue reactivity with clear visual stimuli (90 food images vs 45 non-food images) and reports voxelwise ROI-based results (FWE-corrected TFCE within atlas-defined masks), so it meets I3 and provides small-volume voxelwise results (I5) and reported peaks compatible with I6. However, all reported analyses are between-group interaction contrasts (group × occasion × image-type) comparing standard care vs Mandolean+, rather than reporting a within-participant cue>control (food>non-food) contrast at the group level. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. Exclusion criteria met: E5. Full text is available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study examines natural reward cue-reactivity to visual food images (high- vs low-calorie), meeting the review topic. It contains within-participant task contrasts (HiCal > LoCal) tested at the group level (e.g. analyses 0 and 1: age-adjusted cross-subject regressions on HiCal>LoCal). At least one qualifying voxelwise result is reported with small-volume correction (analyses report SVC FDR p<0.01 in ROIs such as amygdala and BA10), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level task-evoked results. Visual stimuli, participant demographics (age/sex/BMI), and task details are reported. Although several other analyses are ROI-restricted and there are connectivity results, the presence of SVC-corrected task-evoked voxelwise contrasts addressing natural reward visual cues fulfills inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI without SVC, only connectivity, only between-group without within-participant cue>control) are met.

This study examines neural responses to visual natural reward cues (high- and low-calorie food images) in obese endometrial cancer survivors using task-evoked fMRI. It reports within-participant contrasts comparing food cues to non-food controls (e.g., high-calorie > non-food, high-calorie > low-calorie, low-calorie > non-food) and interaction contrasts pre- vs post-treatment. Multiple analyses are described as group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain GLM results with whole-brain cluster-based FWE correction and reported peak coordinates/tables (Tables t2–t4). Participant age, cue type, and relevant task details are reported. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis objectives and required inclusion criteria (visual natural reward cues; within-participant cue>control contrasts; qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain results; results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This study examines neural responses to visual food cues (natural reward) with whole-brain voxelwise, cluster-corrected results reported (Talairach coordinates), satisfying I3 (visual natural-reward cues), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I6 (results reported as coordinate tables), and I7 (participant demographics reported). However, the NeuroStore record lists only between-group interaction contrasts (e.g., OB>NW for high-calorie>object) and does not report any within-participant cue>control contrasts (e.g., food>object) as standalone group-level results. Because the paper appears to report only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast, it fails inclusion I4 and meets exclusion E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking images (ISIS, IAPS) and includes multiple within-participant contrasts of appetitive smoking-related > neutral. Group-level voxelwise analyses (second-level random-effects one-sample t-tests; model fit over whole brain) are reported with peak coordinates/tables for these contrasts (Analyses 1–4 and the within-woman follicular>luteal paired t-test), satisfying voxelwise reporting. Required details (visual cues, within-subject cue>control contrasts, whole-brain group-level voxelwise results, and coordinate tables) are present. Minor missing reporting (e.g., MRI field strength/software) does not preclude inclusion per criteria.

This fMRI study uses visual cues (pink cross, green circle) predicting monetary reward, meeting I3. It includes a within-participant Cue Money > No Money contrast (analysis_5), meeting I4. At least one qualifying analysis is a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result with whole-brain model fit and inference (analysis_5; also other whole-brain analyses), meeting I5. Results are reported as coordinate peaks/tables consistent with I6. Participant and task details are provided (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

This study reports a within-subject fMRI contrast of heroin cues > neutral (analysis 22747521_analysis_0) using visual (audiovisual including images of heroin preparation/injection) cue stimuli, with group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical analysis and reported peak coordinates. The model was fit and inference performed across the whole brain (cluster-corrected), and participant demographics and task details are provided. These features satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue component (I3), within-participant drug>control contrast (I4), and a whole-brain voxelwise result (I5). Reporting in NeuroStore includes peaks (acceptable per I6), and participant age/sex and methods are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study assesses anticipation of monetary (natural) reward using distinct visual cues (CSs: arrows), meeting the visual cue requirement. It reports within-participant contrasts of interest (e.g. mCS+ > CS−) comparing reward-related cues to control stimuli. Analyses are group-level, random-effects, voxelwise, whole-brain inference with voxelwise GRF thresholding and reported peak coordinates (tables), satisfying the requirement for qualifying voxelwise results. Participant demographics (n, mean age, sex) and cue types are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards.

The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results for reward-related contrasts using visual cues (Monetary Incentive Delay task with circle/square cues). The analyses explicitly involve the within-participant contrast of anticipation of rewarding trials > anticipation of neutral/no-reward trials, reported as group-level comparisons (e.g., non-users (reward>no-reward) > cannabis users (reward>no-reward)). Results are whole-brain and corrected for multiple comparisons, with peak coordinates provided in tables. Thus it meets I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant reward>control contrast is present), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain results), and I6 (results reported in tables of coordinates). I7 (reporting of MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software) is not fully satisfied (some methodological details missing), but the criterion notes missing items should not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This fMRI study used visual food cues (a new food picture database) in a within-subject choice task and reports within-participant contrasts (HE > LE and SL > DL). Analyses were estimated and inferred over the whole brain with voxelwise results and peak coordinates reported (FWE cluster-level thresholding), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics (age, sex, BMI) are reported; some methodological details (e.g., field strength, preprocessing software) are not listed but are not required for inclusion. Therefore it meets the review objective of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and satisfies inclusion criteria I3–I7.

This study addresses visual cue reactivity for drug and gambling cues and reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level results (meets I3, I5). Voxelwise peaks are reported in tables (meets I6), and participant details are provided (meets I7). However, the NeuroStore extraction indicates the reported contrasts are omnibus, between-group effects (diagnostic group × video interactions) with model/inference over the whole brain; no within-participant cue>control (e.g., drug-cue > neutral/control) contrasts are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 (no qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Conclusion: EXCLUDE.

The study addresses visual drug cue-reactivity in cocaine-dependent patients and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results, but the documented voxelwise contrasts in the NeuroStore record are reported as between-group interactions (Abuse vs NoAbuse for Drug>Neutral) rather than an explicit within-participant drug-cues>control within-subject contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual fMRI cue task), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked result reported, whole-brain), and I6 (results reported as peaks/tables). Inclusion criterion I4 (at least one within-participant drug>control contrast) is not clearly met in the provided document. Because the record appears to report only between-group interactions without an accompanying qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast, exclusion criterion E5 applies. Therefore exclude.

This study meets inclusion criteria I3 (clear visual alcohol cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported), I6 (results reported as coordinate peaks/tables), and I7 (participant demographics and cue type reported). However, all extracted analyses are between-group interaction contrasts (heavy vs light; FHP vs FHN) comparing alcohol>control between groups, and no within-participant cue>control (alcohol>nonalcohol) main-effect voxelwise contrast is reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (no accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criterion I4 is not met. Full text is available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study investigates smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of smoking and neutral scenes) and reports within-participant cue>control contrasts. Specifically, analyses include LCSP>LCNP and LCSP>PNSP contrasts (e.g., Analyses 5 and 7) with group-level voxelwise inference over the whole brain (FDR- and FWE-corrected voxel-level results and reported peak tables). Participant demographics (age/sex) and cue type are reported. Therefore it meets I3 (visual drug cues), I4 (within-participant drug-cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (results reported in tables/coordinates), and I7 (participant info reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts). Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record.

This study reports fMRI responses to visual natural reward cues (erotic video clips vs neutral) in a within-subject design. A within-participant contrast of erotic minus non-erotic stimulation is used (Treatment-by-Condition interaction and related contrasts), and at least one qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result is reported with whole-brain inference (Analysis 3: whole-brain model fit and inference; cluster-level FWE-corrected results with reported peak coordinates). Participant demographics and cue type are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity (I3, I4) and contains voxelwise whole-brain/small-volume-corrected results (I5, I6), with participant/cue reporting acceptable (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes appropriate within-participant contrasts).

The study is excluded because it does not provide a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (I4). It does include visual food cues (I3), and it reports at least one whole-brain voxelwise group task-evoked result (HiCal>LoCal; whole-brain, FDR-corrected) satisfying I5; coordinates/peaks are tabulated satisfying I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. However, the available analyses compare high- vs low-calorie food and hunger state (HiCal>LoCal; HiCal hungry>HiCal satiated in women) and do not present a food>non-food (cue>control) within-subject contrast required by I4. Participant age/sex and cue type are reported, but MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software are not fully reported (I7 not fully met). Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study using visual food images (natural reward cues) and a cue-reactivity task, matching the review objective. It reports within-participant contrasts of food>non-food and food>baseline (Analyses 5–7), satisfying the requirement for a within-participant cue>control contrast. Group-level voxelwise random-effects models were fit over the whole brain and results are reported as peak coordinates in tables (Talairach), meeting the whole-brain voxelwise evidence criterion. Visual cue type and participant age/sex are reported; missing details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) do not exclude the study per I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains qualifying within-subject contrasts). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study uses a visual card-guessing task probing reward anticipation (natural reward-related cues) and reports a within-participant reward>loss contrast (analysis_3) and group-level voxelwise results: a whole-brain group × anticipation interaction (analysis_1) and ROI small-volume-corrected voxelwise results for BD>HC reward anticipation (analysis_2). Thus it meets I3 (visual reward cues), I4 (within-participant reward>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise results: whole-brain and SVC), I6 (voxelwise peaks reported), and I7 (participant demographics reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Results are sufficiently reported (peaks, thresholding, coordinate space) to qualify for inclusion.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual food images (natural rewards) and reports voxelwise task-evoked results. It includes a within-participant contrast of high-calorie > low-calorie food images (Analysis 5) and reports coordinates (Table t0005). Inference was voxel-level FWE within a combined anatomical/functional mask (i.e., small-volume-corrected), satisfying the requirement for a group-level voxelwise or SVC result. Participant, task, and stimulus details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only without SVC (E3), not connectivity/resting-only (E4), and a within-participant cue>control contrast is present (so E5 does not apply). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study examines neural responses to food images (natural reward visual cues) with group-level whole-brain voxelwise results, so it meets I3 and I5. However, the NeuroStore extraction reports only a sex × BMI z-score omnibus between-group interaction (between-group contrast) and does not report any within-participant cue>control (food>control) contrasts required for cue-reactivity meta-analysis. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies (only between-group/interaction reported without a qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. Full text appears available in the record.

This study directly examines fMRI cue-reactivity to visual smoking images in nicotine-dependent participants and reports a within-subject smoking>neutral contrast across all subjects (Analysis 21764527_analysis_3). It provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference and reports peak coordinates/tables (Analyses 3 and 4), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results. The cue modality is visual and the contrast of interest (drug cues > neutral) is present. Participant demographics and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; includes within-participant cue>control contrast). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the meta-analysis.

This study examines visual food cue reactivity (natural rewards) and reports group-level whole-brain results for adults, but all reported task contrasts are comparisons of two food cue types (unhealthy foods > healthy foods) rather than reward cues > neutral/control stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues — food pictures), I5 (at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain result for the adult UF>HF contrast), I6 (voxelwise results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant contrast of reward cues > control/neutral stimuli; contrasts are reward vs reward). No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) are directly met. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I4 (required).

This study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual sexual stimuli (I3). It includes within-participant contrasts of sexual cues > neutral cues in both PD hypersexuality patients and PD controls (I4). Results are group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain analyses with reported peak coordinates and whole-brain inference (I5 and I6). NeuroStore indicates whole-brain model fit and inference and lists reported peaks for the sexual>neutral contrasts, meeting the requirement for extractable voxelwise results. Missing details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) do not preclude inclusion per criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (palatable food) cue-reactivity using explicit visual milkshake cues (I3). It includes within-participant cue contrasts (palatable milkshake cue > sub-palatable milkshake cue and related cue>control contrasts) meeting I4. Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise statistical results are reported (mixed-effects FLAME1; whole-brain inference; peak coordinates and corrected p-values), satisfying I5 and I6. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, and analysis software are reported; MRI field strength is not listed in the extract but its absence does not preclude inclusion per I7’s guidance. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This study examines alcohol cue reactivity with clear visual stimuli (alcohol beverage pictures) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (Talairach coordinates, cluster-corrected), and participant age/sex are reported. However, the only extracted contrast is a between-group interaction (HD alcohol > CON non-alcohol); no within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast is provided in the document. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrast/interaction without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. Full text appears complete for screening.

The study reports a task-based fMRI cue-reactivity experiment using visual alcohol images in alcohol-addicted patients. It includes a within-participant contrast of alcohol-related cues > non-alcohol cues (Analysis 29343732_analysis_0) and additional contrasts versus control images (Analysis 29343732_analysis_2). Models were fit over the whole brain with voxelwise thresholding and tables of peak coordinates provided, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics (age, sex) and cue type (visual images) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of cigarette cue-reactivity that includes clear visual cues (cigarette, live video feed), satisfying I3. It reports a within-subject contrast (Cigarette > control) tested at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise inference and coordinate peaks (Table 3), meeting I4, I5 and I6. Participant demographics are reported (age, sex, smoking behavior), satisfying I7 (preferred but not required). Thresholding and cluster-level results are reported. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and include a qualifying cue>control task-evoked voxelwise result. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study uses an fMRI Monetary Incentive Delay task with visual cues (circles/squares/triangles) and reports small-volume-corrected voxelwise ROI results, so it meets I3 (natural reward with visual cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise small-volume-corrected result), I6 (results reported as peaks/tables), and I7 (participant demographics reported). However, it does not present a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (I4). The within-subject contrasts reported are primarily loss-avoidance cue > non-incentive (negative incentive) and outcome/regression contrasts; the reported high-reward contrast appears only as a between-group interaction, not as a within-participant reward-cue > control contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are otherwise triggered by the available document. Full text is complete in this record.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It examines cue-reactivity to smoking cues using multimodal (audio-visual) stimuli that include a visual component (I3). It reports a within-participant contrast of smoking cues > non-smoking cues (SCs > non-SCs) at the group level (n=35 and subgroup n=16) (I4). Although analyses were conducted within anatomically defined ROIs, the statistical inference was performed voxelwise restricted to an ROI mask with cluster-level Monte-Carlo correction (p<0.005), which constitutes small-volume–restricted voxelwise group-level task-evoked results (satisfying I5). Peaks are reported in tables (satisfying I6). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported though some MRI processing details are missing; this is acceptable per I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not solely ROI without SVC, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control).

This study uses natural reward (food) cues including visual images (chocolate and moldy strawberry images) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts comparing satiated vs premeal states. However, it does not report a within-participant contrast of reward-related cues > control stimuli (e.g., food-image > control-image) required by inclusion criterion I4. Although a PPI seed-based connectivity analysis is reported, the paper also includes qualifying whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise results, so exclusion criterion E4 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward with visual cues present), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (results reported as peaks/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast). Therefore the study is excluded from the cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

This study assesses neural reactivity to food (a natural reward) using clear visual cues (pictographic menu items and high-resolution food videos). The reported analysis models video condition (food vs non-food control) and treatment (NB32 vs placebo) and reports a group-level voxelwise interaction/contrast with whole-brain inference and peak coordinates (Table tbl2). These features satisfy I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue vs control contrast evident via video condition and pre/post design), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain result), I6 (coordinates reported in table), and I7 (participant age/sex and other demographics reported). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and the report is empirical human fMRI data. Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record.

The study examines natural rewards (monetary and social) with clear visual cues (I3 satisfied). It reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (hit outcome > no outcome contrasts; Talairach coordinates, tables) meeting the requirement for voxelwise evidence (I5 satisfied) and these results are reported as tables of coordinates (I6 satisfied). However, NeuroStore’s extracted analyses do not include any within-participant cue > control contrast (e.g., reward-cue > neutral-cue) required by the review (I4 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore excluded because I4 is not met; inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6; inclusion criteria not met: I4. Full text appears complete for screening.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all inclusion criteria. It is an event/block-design fMRI study of a drug (GHB) affecting natural reward-related (sexual) cue reactivity using clear visual stimuli (erotic vs neutral pictures) (I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of natural reward-related cues>control (Erotic > Neutral in the placebo condition) (I4). It provides qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results: whole-brain group-level contrasts (Analyses 2 and 3) and small-volume-corrected ROI results (Analyses 0 and 1), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or SVC results (I5). Results are reported as peaks/tables and described in analyses, acceptable per I6. Participant demographics and cue details are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrast, and is empirical fMRI data).

This study meets the meta-analysis objective (fMRI cue-reactivity to alcohol visual stimuli) and satisfies all required inclusion criteria. I3: Task uses visual alcohol-related images (60 alcohol, 45 neutral). I4: Includes a within-participant contrast (analysis 24314346_analysis_1: alcohol > neutral within AA patients). I5: Reports voxelwise group-level results with inference restricted to anatomically defined ROIs (amygdala) using FWE-corrected voxel-level thresholding, i.e., a small-volume-corrected voxelwise result. I6: Peaks/coordinates are reported (reported peaks: 2), satisfying acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not limited to ROI-only without SVC (E3 not met because SVC was performed), it includes a within-participant contrast (E5 not met), and it is not a connectivity-only or non-empirical study (E4/E6 not met). Participant and task details are provided. Therefore include.

The study meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria. It investigates neural responses to visual food cues (natural reward) and uses images as stimuli (I3). It reports a within-participant contrast of high-calorie > low-calorie foods (interaction with treatment) within a randomized crossover design (I4). A group-level voxelwise task-evoked result is reported with voxel-level small-volume correction in the hypothalamus (ROI) (I5). The voxelwise SVC result is clearly reported in the NeuroStore extraction (I6). Participant characteristics and cue type are reported; some preprocessing/MRI details are not provided but this does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., this is not ROI-only without SVC voxelwise results). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli (high-calorie food pictures vs car images) in obese participants, directly addressing natural reward-related (food) cue reactivity. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of high-calorie food > control (car images) and multiple group-level voxelwise results: several whole-brain analyses (cluster-level FDR-reported; Tables of peaks) and small-volume/ROI-corrected results (FWE voxel-level in reward ROIs/VTA). Participant demographics (age, sex, BMI) and task details are reported. These facts satisfy inclusion criteria I3 (visual cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain and small-volume-corrected results), I6 (results reported in tables/peaks), and I7 (participant/sample details provided). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This study should be excluded because all reported fMRI analyses were conducted and inferred only within predefined regions-of-interest (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest), with no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise results reported. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (multiple within-participant cues>control contrasts reported, e.g., A>N and N>A contrasts), I6 (voxelwise peaks/tables reported in tables t5-t7), and I7 (participant age/sex and other sample details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group result) and I3 (the document does not clearly specify that cue exposure used a visual cue component). Because E3 is met, the study must be excluded.

The study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual food stimuli (natural reward), and includes within-group task-related contrasts (food-cue responsivity / main effect of food-cue induced activation). It provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results with whole-brain inference (Analyses 2 and 3) and also regionally restricted SVC results in the DLPFC (Analyses 0 and 1). Peaks are reported. Participant age and sex and cue type are reported; MRI field strength/preprocessing software are not listed in this record but their absence does not preclude inclusion per the meta-analysis guidance. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Meets all required inclusion criteria for the review: this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking-related pictures (I3). It reports a within-participant contrast of smoking cues > neutral cues (within-group contrast) (I4). The analysis is a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result with cluster-level thresholding and reported peak coordinates in MNI space, constituting whole-brain voxelwise reporting (I5); NeuroStore extraction indicates peaks and cluster-level inference, and coordinate space is provided. Reporting of results in tables/peaks is acceptable (I6). No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical fMRI data. Some ancillary details (MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not reported, but I7 is preferred rather than mandatory. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an fMRI study of natural (food) reward cue-reactivity using visual cues (images of milkshake and water) (I3). It reports within-participant cue>control contrasts (anticipatory milkshake cue > tasteless solution cue; milkshake receipt > tasteless solution receipt) (I4). At least one qualifying voxelwise group-level result is reported with whole-brain inference and cluster correction (analyses 0 and 1), and additional small-volume-corrected ROI results are reported for the caudate (analyses 2 and 3), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked voxelwise results (I5). Results are reported as peaks/coordinates and participant demographics are provided (I6, I7). No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the NeuroStore record reports only between-group contrasts/interactions (patients>controls; omnibus between-group contrasts) and does not present a within-participant drug-cue > control-stimulus contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual alcohol cues present: advertisements and pictures), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported with peaks/coordinates), I6 (results reported as peaks/tables), I7 (participant age/sex and clinical details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant alcohol-cue > control contrast reported). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). fulltext_incomplete=false

This fMRI study uses visual erotic film segments (a natural reward) and reports within-participant contrasts of erotic > neutral (E > neutral) for group-level analyses in healthy participants. Model fitting was performed over the whole brain and inference was restricted to regions of interest (i.e., small-volume/ROI inference), with voxelwise peaks reported in tables — satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain fit and ROI inference qualifies as small-volume-corrected evidence). Visual cue component, within-subject cue>control contrasts, voxelwise (tabled) peaks, and participant demographics are reported. Missing MRI field strength is noted but not exclusionary. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only without qualifying voxelwise results, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for natural reward (visual) cue-reactivity.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it used fMRI cue-reactivity with visual alcohol drinking videos (I3); reports a within-participant contrast alcohol>mosaic (I4); provides group-level voxelwise whole-brain RFX GLM results with FDR correction and reported peak coordinates (I5); coordinates/peaks are reported in tables making voxelwise results available (I6); participant demographics and task details are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete in the NeuroStore record.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (videos of foods being grasped). It reports multiple within-subject cue>control contrasts (e.g., UF>O, F>O, UF1PP>UF3PP, UF1PP>O1PP) at the group level. Crucially, several analyses report voxelwise whole-brain group results with FWE cluster-level correction (analyses flagged as whole-brain with FWE p<0.001), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise evidence. Results and peaks are reported in tables. Participant age and sex are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-participant contrasts). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward-related (sexual/erotic) visual cues using block-design video stimuli and reports within-participant contrasts EVS > NVS. Analyses were estimated over the whole brain and report voxelwise peak coordinates (tables of peaks) with voxel-level thresholding, satisfying requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics and cue type are reported. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria for visual cue component (I3), within-participant cue>control contrasts (I4), whole-brain voxelwise reporting (I5), and acceptability of coordinate-table reporting (I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts). Full text is available via the NeuroStore record.

This study uses visual natural-reward stimuli (infant faces/baby schema) and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-level FWE; MNI coordinates table). However, the only extracted voxelwise contrast reported in the record is a within-participant Pre-XRNTX > On-XRNTX (treatment effect) contrast. The record does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast comparing natural reward-related cues (e.g., high baby schema > low/control faces) vs control stimuli, which is required (I4). Therefore it does not meet all required inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the available record.

This fMRI study examines cannabis cue-reactivity using visual (and tactile) cannabis paraphernalia and natural reward (fruit) cues. It includes within-participant contrasts of drug cues > control (e.g., Cannabis > pencil) reported as group-level voxelwise results with whole-brain inference and tables of peak coordinates. Participant demographics and cue types are reported. Although the study also reports between-group interactions, the presence of within-subject cannabis>control whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (and coordinate tables) satisfies the meta-analysis requirements. MRI field strength and preprocessing software are not listed in this record, but missing these details does not preclude inclusion per I7.

This study examines neural responses to monetary and social rewards using explicit visual cues (wallet images, faces), so it meets I3 (visual natural-reward cues). Participant age/sex and cue types are reported, satisfying I7 (preferred reporting). However, the NeuroStore record shows only a region-of-interest analysis (model fit and inference restricted to the right NAcc ROI) and reports an omnibus between-group interaction contrast; there is no reported within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., reward-cue > control-cue) nor any whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. Therefore exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only with no qualifying voxelwise result) and E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-participant cue>control contrast) are met, and inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not satisfied. On that basis the study must be excluded.

This study examines neural responses to food pictures (a natural reward) using an fMRI affective picture-viewing task with explicit visual cues (IAPS food images). At least one analysis uses a within-participant contrast of food>neutral (Analysis 19806158_analysis_6: ‘food > neutral [cross subject regression]’), and group-level voxelwise results are reported with whole-brain inference and FDR voxelwise correction (Analyses 2 and 6 report whole-brain, FDR-corrected peaks). Peaks/coordinates are reported. Participant demographics and stimulus details are given. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrast).

The study includes a cue-reactivity task with visual alcohol and water words (I3 met) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (parametric PE analyses) with coordinate peaks in a table (I5 and I6 met). However, it does not report any within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or equivalent cue>control voxelwise contrast (I4 not met). I7 (reporting MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software) is not fully reported. No exclusion criteria E3 or E4 clearly apply. Exclusion is based on failure to meet inclusion criterion I4 (no within-subject drug-cue>control contrast available).

NeuroStore extraction shows the study used visual sexual stimuli (natural reward) and reports within-subject contrasts Sexual>Neutral with coordinate peaks in tables, satisfying I3 and I4 and acceptable reporting format I6. However, all reported analyses have 'Model fit over: region of interest' and 'Inference restricted to: region of interest' (ROI-only) despite voxel-level correction; no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise results are reported. This violates inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only results with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study uses a food-picture cue-reactivity task (natural reward) so I3 is met. There is a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise association (FWE-corrected) relating GLP-1 changes to food-cue-related orbitofrontal activity, so I5 is met. However, the document does not report an explicit within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., food cues > control stimuli) for a task-evoked effect — the reported whole-brain voxelwise result is a cross-subject (between-group) regression and the only within-group analysis is an ROI-based regression in a predefined OFC cluster. Therefore the review’s required within-participant cue>control contrast (I4) is not clearly present, and the study effectively reports only between-group voxelwise associations plus ROI results, triggering exclusion E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast).
