Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

Excluded because the study does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the task involved gustatory (taste) cues (preferred alcoholic beverage vs litchi juice) with brief prompts, and the NeuroStore record does not indicate a clear visual alcohol-cue component required by the review (visual-only or multimodal including visual cues). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrast alcohol cue > control), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain result reported; FWE cluster-level), I6 (results reported with coordinates/MNI and peak table). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (visual cue component). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) applied.

The study is excluded because it does not address the review’s required visual cue component (I3): the task is a mental-imagery paradigm with personalized stress and neutral audio scripts (auditory/imaginative stimuli), not visual drug or natural-reward cues. It also does not present a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control or natural reward cues > control (I4). The paper does report whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with peak coordinates (meets I5) and reports peaks in tables (meets I6). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4. fulltext_incomplete=false.

Excluded because the paper does not report a within-participant drug-cue > control contrast (I4 not met). The study assesses alcohol cue-reactivity with visual stimuli (I3 met), reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results within an anatomically defined ROI with FWE correction (small-volume-corrected) and peak coordinates in tables (I5 and I6 met). However, all reported analyses are ROI-restricted and primarily between-group contrasts or interactions (e.g., between-group simple effects and group x condition interactions); no qualifying within-subject alcoholic > non-alcoholic beverage contrast is provided. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without within-participant cue>control) applies. Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visually-presented alcohol and neutral pictures and a block-design cue-reactivity task. The paper reports within-subject alcohol>neutral whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (Analysis 2: Alcohol > Neutral Cues) with reported peak coordinates (Table tbl2), and cross-subject regressions of alcohol>neutral (Analyses 0 and 1). Whole-brain inference and cluster-level FWE correction are indicated. Participant demographics (age, sex) and cue type are reported. Although MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not listed in the NeuroStore record, that absence does not preclude inclusion per the review’s stated allowances. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria for visual reward/drug cue reactivity with qualifying voxelwise results.

This fMRI study uses visual food cues and reports group-level voxelwise results (ROI/SVC with reported peak coordinates) and participant demographics, so it meets I3, I5, I6, and I7. However, all reported contrasts compare conditions of food availability or calorie content (e.g., available > non-available; high > low calorie) rather than a reward-cue versus control/neutral stimulus contrast. The meta-analysis requires at least one within-participant contrast of drug or natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (I4), which is not present. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore exclude because I4 is not met.

This is an fMRI study using visual tobacco-related cues (20 tobacco-related and 20 neutral pictures) meeting the review objective. It reports within-participant contrasts of tobacco-related > neutral pictures (multiple within-group analyses) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results fit over the whole brain with voxelwise t-tests and corrected thresholds; coordinates/peak tables are reported. Thus it provides qualifying whole-brain voxelwise cue>control results (not ROI-only), and tables of coordinates are available. Preferred reporting details (age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are incomplete in the extraction but that alone does not exclude the study.

The study assesses natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (192 color photographs). It reports within-participant contrasts (high- and low-calorie cues > nonfood cues) and provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked results: whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported peak coordinates/tables (and an ROI analysis as well). Participant age/sex and clinical details are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met because the paper includes whole-brain voxelwise task results (not ROI-only or connectivity-only), and it is an empirical task-based fMRI study.

The study uses an fMRI task with clear visual cues (Monetary Incentive Delay Task with geometric cue stimuli) examining reward-related cue anticipation (natural reward: monetary gain). It reports within-subject contrasts of gain cues > neutral cues (analyses 2–4) at the group level using voxelwise SPM second-level models. At least one qualifying voxelwise result is reported whole-brain (analysis 19560123_analysis_2: multiple regression, p<0.001 cluster extent threshold, reported peaks) and several analyses use small-volume FWE correction. Participant demographics and task details are reported. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

The study examines fMRI responses to visual food cues (natural reward) so meets I3. However, the NeuroStore record reports only within-study contrasts comparing portion-size conditions (e.g., Large PS > Small PS) and does not report any within-participant contrast of food cues > control stimuli (e.g., food > furniture/scrambled), so I4 is not met. Furthermore, all reported analyses were fit over regions of interest (Model fit over: region of interest) with region-level thresholding and no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group results are reported, so I5 is not met. Because the paper reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result, it meets exclusion criterion E3. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study examines natural (social) reward cue-reactivity with visual cues (videos) and reports group-level voxelwise results, but it does not report a within-participant contrast of natural reward cues > control stimuli. The reported analyses are between-group contrasts and interactions (group × condition) and ROI interaction; therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI of natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise results reported whole-brain and SVC), I6 (results reported as voxelwise inference). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported). Full text is complete as provided.

The study uses visual smoking cues (I3 satisfied) and reports group-level voxelwise results within an anatomically defined ROI with inference restricted to that ROI (small-volume-corrected), with peaks reported in tables (I5 and I6 satisfied). However, the reported contrasts are NoGo > Baseline separately for Smoking and Neutral image trials rather than a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast required by the meta-analysis (I4 not met). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., the study does not report only between-group contrasts nor only non-task analyses). Therefore it must be excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I4 (no drug>control cue contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion criterion not met: I4. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (120 food pictures vs matched non-food images). It reports within-participant contrasts of food>non-food at the group level with voxelwise whole-brain inference (corrected cluster significance) and lists peak coordinates in tables. Participant demographics and task details are reported. Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-evoked fMRI cue-reactivity using visual meth-related pictures versus matched neutral visual control pictures and a within-participant contrast (Meth cues > Neutral cues). Analyses were random-effects one-sample t-tests fit over the whole brain with reported peak coordinates (table), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise results. Participant demographics (age, sex) and cue type are reported. MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistics software are not listed in the NeuroStore record, but their absence does not prevent inclusion per I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

Exclusion: E3 and E5. This study reports only region-of-interest analyses (Model fit over and Inference restricted to: striatal ROI) and the extracted contrast field lists 'omnibus, between-group', indicating reported results are between-group/omnibus rather than a within-participant drug-cue > control contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (functional MRI cue-reactivity with clear visual cues—marketing clips). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported), I5 (no whole-brain or explicit small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level result reported). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study reports within-subject contrasts comparing reward-related cues (monetary and erotic/natural rewards) versus neutral/control cues (e.g., reward cues > non-incentive; partial/continuous reward > neutral/control) using visual stimuli. At least one qualifying group-level voxelwise result is reported with voxel-level FWE small-volume correction (SVC) in bilateral ventral striatum, satisfying the requirement for a small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked result. Results are reported as coordinates/peaks (tables) and participant demographics (age/sex) are provided. Therefore the study addresses natural reward cue-reactivity with clear visual cues and provides qualifying within-participant voxelwise analyses. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI without voxelwise SVC, connectivity-only analyses, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This study examines neural responses to visual (and auditory) food cues (natural rewards) and reports within-participant contrasts of high-energy-density (HED) vs low-energy-density (LED) stimuli (HED>LED), including correlations for HED>LED with GLP-1 changes. NeuroStore lists multiple whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses with reported peaks (e.g., analyses 2 and 3: whole-brain cross-subject regressions; analyses 0 and 1: whole-brain group effects), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise results. Results are reported as coordinates/peaks. The study is not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study reports a within-subject contrast comparing high vs low price cues (€18 > €3) that modulates experienced taste pleasantness, with group-level voxelwise results subjected to small-volume FWE correction and coordinates reported. The stimuli list includes ‘Price and payment condition information,’ indicating a visual cue component conveying value about the wine. Participant demographics and peak coordinates are reported. Thus the study provides a qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast for a natural reward (wine) and a qualifying small-volume-corrected voxelwise result. Some uncertainty remains because the modality of the price cue is not explicitly labeled as visual in the extracted record, so confidence is moderate.

This fMRI study used visual food cues (high- and low-calorie images) vs. control (car images), matching the review’s focus on natural reward cue-reactivity with visual stimuli. It reports a foods > cars contrast and provides group-level voxelwise results (model fit over whole brain; voxel-level thresholding; reported peak coordinates), satisfying the requirement for a qualifying task-evoked, group-level voxelwise result. Although the paper also reports effective connectivity analyses, it does include the necessary task-evoked voxelwise contrast, so exclusion criterion E4 does not apply. Participant and task details are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This study examines fMRI responses to visual food cues (natural rewards) using a cue-reactivity task and reports within-participant contrasts of high-hedonic foods > neutral/neutral nonfood objects (H > U). Critically, Analysis 17921372_analysis_2 is a group-level whole-brain, voxelwise result (random-effects GLM; FDR voxel-level; 7 reported peaks), which satisfies the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result. Visual stimuli and participant demographics are reported. Although some analyses are ROI-based, the presence of a whole-brain voxelwise H>U contrast meets inclusion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study) are met.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to food cues (natural rewards) using visual pictorial stimuli (pepperoni pizza, fudge sundae, raw vegetables, office supplies) and reports within-participant contrasts involving high- vs low-calorie food cues across pre- and postsurgery sessions. The reported analysis is a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked result (model fit and inference over whole brain; voxel-level peaks reported in a table), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise results. Although MRI field strength and preprocessing software are not reported, participant age/sex and cue type are provided; missing those details alone do not exclude the study. The high-ED > low-ED within-subject contrast represents natural reward cue reactivity with visual stimuli and thus meets the meta-analysis objective. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports fMRI cue-reactivity to visual natural reward (food) images in obese patients using a within-subject preoperative vs postoperative design. It includes within-participant contrasts involving food versus nonfood stimuli (stimulus × condition repeated-measures ANOVA, interaction contrasts reported) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (FDR-corrected whole-brain inference, peaks reported in a table). These satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue-reactivity, a within-participant cue>control contrast (through reported food>nonfood contrasts/interactions), and voxelwise whole-brain results. Some methodological details (MRI field strength, preprocessing/software) are not reported in the NeuroStore record, but missing this information does not preclude inclusion per the criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

This study tests visual natural-reward cues (food images) and reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise results, but it does not present a within-participant cue>control (food>object or food>baseline) voxelwise contrast required for inclusion. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI with visual natural reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported), and I6 (voxelwise results/peaks are reported in the record). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant food>control voxelwise contrast is shown in the extracted analyses). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (the paper reports primarily between-group contrasts/interactions and ROI or within-group object anticipation results, but no qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast). Therefore the study is excluded under E5 despite having relevant whole-brain group results.

This study investigates fMRI responses to food images (natural rewards) with whole-brain group-level voxelwise results, but the NeuroStore record reports only between-group interaction contrasts (patient vs control for food>neutral). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual food cues present), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I6 (results reported in coordinate table), I7 (participant demographics and cue details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast is reported). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported without an accompanying within-participant cue>control result). Full text appears available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The NeuroStore record describes an fMRI study of smoking-cue distractors with visual stimuli and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (omnibus Delay Condition main effect and Memory Load × Delay Condition interaction, plus load contrasts). However the extracted analyses do not include an explicit within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (e.g., Smoking > Neutral or Smoking > Control). Although the abstract mentions effects specific to smoking-cue trials, no smoking>control pairwise voxelwise contrasts or coordinates are listed in the extracted analyses. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 (requiring at least one within-participant drug-cue>control contrast) is not met, so the study cannot be included. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly triggered by the provided record.

This study examines neural responses to visual food cues (food pictures vs objects), i.e., natural reward-related cue-reactivity, in anorexia nervosa. NeuroStore reports within-participant contrasts (Foods - Objects; High palatability - Low palatability foods) and group-level voxelwise models fit over the whole brain with inference including separate a priori ROI correction and cluster-corrected whole-brain results; peaks are reported in Table t2. Participant demographics (age, sex) and task/cue details are provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity (I3), contains within-participant cue>control contrasts (I4), reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain and ROI-corrected inference (I5) with peaks in tables acceptable (I6), and reports participant/task details (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and include within-participant contrasts alongside group tests. Full text appears sufficiently represented by the NeuroStore record.

This study includes clear visual cues (geometric symbols predicting monetary gain/loss), satisfying I3. It reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume FWE correction and coordinates in tables, satisfying I5 and I6. However, all reported statistical contrasts are between-group comparisons/interactions (e.g., patient loss cue > control neutral cue; successful vs unsuccessful loss avoidance: patient vs control), and no within-participant cue>control (e.g., loss cue > neutral cue within the same subjects) voxelwise contrasts are reported in the provided record. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. This triggers exclusion criterion E5 (studies reporting only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text is complete in the record provided.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual pictures of appetizing foods vs control (locations), i.e., natural reward visual cues. It reports a within-participant contrast (Foods > Locations) and a group-level voxelwise second-level random-effects analysis fit over the whole brain with reported peak coordinates (Table 1). These elements satisfy the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity, a within-subject cue>control contrast, and whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Although MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software are not reported in the NeuroStore extract (I7 is preferred but not required), this does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study is included.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the review's cue-reactivity requirements and reports only ROI results. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only region-of-interest analysis with no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (some participant information reported: age mean provided). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (study does not assess drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with clear visual cues — the task was a Trust Game/economic decision task, not visual drug cue exposure), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli or equivalent cue>control contrast reported), I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked result reported), I6 (not applicable because there are no qualifying voxelwise results to be reported in tables/figures). Reported analysis is a within-group cross-subject regression on left mid-insula using an ROI mask; thresholding was region-level. Therefore the paper does not provide the required visual cue-reactivity voxelwise results for inclusion.

The study investigates natural reward (monetary) cue-reactivity with visual cues (I3 met). However, the NeuroStore extraction presents only seed-based connectivity (gPPI) results (right NAc seed) and no group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrast of reward cues > control stimuli is reported in the provided document. Thus the study fails required inclusion criteria I4 and I5 and meets exclusion E4 (reports only seed-based connectivity without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). Note: the abstract mentions whole-brain and ROI analyses, but the extracted record contains only connectivity analyses, so per the provided document there is no qualifying voxelwise result available for inclusion.

The study examines natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images and includes within-subject contrasts of High-calorie > Low-calorie food cues (natural reward > control). Multiple group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (Analyses 1–4: whole-brain, cluster-level inference using GRF, random-effects models), satisfying the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise result. Participant demographics, cue type, and analysis software details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, is empirical).

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) voxel estimates rather than any group-level whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results (exclusion E3). The record shows the model was fit over a region of interest and thresholding reported at the region level. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study involves drug-related cue-reactivity with a multimodal design that includes visual stimuli — IAPS neutral slides were used). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no clear within-participant drug-cue > control contrast is reported; the listed analysis is an omnibus within-group contrast), I5 (no whole-brain or SVC voxelwise group-level result reported). Therefore the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete in this record.

Exclusion summary: E5 is met because the article does not report a within-participant drug-cue>control (or natural reward>control) contrast. The reported fMRI analyses focus on Pavlovian-to-instrumental transfer contrasts (incongruent>congruent) and between-group effects; no within-subject alcohol-cue > control stimulus contrast is provided.
Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study includes clear visual alcohol and water beverage pictures as cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported using whole-brain second-level SPM analyses), I6 (peak coordinates/tables are reported). 
Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant drug-cue>control or natural reward>control contrast identified).
Conclusion: EXCLUDED due to E5 (only between-group/PIT contrasts reported without an accompanying within-subject cue>control contrast).

This fMRI study examines sexual (natural reward) cue reactivity with clear visual cues (images of undressed females) and reports group-level voxelwise results (whole-brain FWE cluster-level and SVC), so it meets I3, I5, I6 and I7. However, all reported voxelwise contrasts in the NeuroStore record are reported as between-group contrasts/interactions (e.g., “CS+Sex > CS− [contrast, between-group]”) with no explicit within-participant cue>control voxelwise result (no one-sample or within-subject cue>control map reported). Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria not met: I4. Fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is an fMRI investigation using visual drug-related picture cues (alcohol, marijuana, polydrug) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group results (cluster-corrected peaks in MNI coordinates), so it meets I3 (visual drug-cue paradigm), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), and I6 (voxelwise results reported in tables). However, the reported within-subject contrasts are comparisons of non-studied versus studied drug pictures (e.g., alcohol non-studied > alcohol studied) rather than a drug-cue > control-stimulus contrast (drug > neutral or drug > non-drug control). The meta-analysis requires at least one within-participant drug-cue > control contrast (I4), which is not present here. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I4.

This study examines natural reward (erotic) visual cue-reactivity using IAPS erotic vs non-erotic pictures and expectation cues. First-level within-subject contrasts (erotic>non-erotic) were computed and used in a paired t-test (within-participant) comparing menstrual phases, satisfying a group-level within-participant analysis. Group-level voxelwise results were fitted over the whole brain with voxelwise thresholding and reported peak coordinates (tables), meeting the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise results. Results (peaks/tables) are available in the paper (NeuroStore extracts). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes a within-participant contrast).

This study uses visual erotic stimuli (natural reward) and reports task-evoked voxelwise results (both small-volume-corrected ROI analyses and a whole-brain FWE analysis), but the NeuroStore extraction labels the reported contrasts as between-group comparisons and does not clearly present a within-participant cue>control contrast. Inclusion met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (voxelwise SVC/whole-brain results present), I6 (reporting available). Inclusion not met: I4 (no clear within-participant cue>control contrast is documented). Exclusion met: E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Therefore the study must be excluded under E5.

This fMRI study examines appetitive (monetary) conditioning with clear visual cues (blue/yellow rectangles and a white square target) and reports within-participant contrasts CS+ > CS- (analyses 0 and 1). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with FWE small-volume correction (voxel-level SVC) and peak coordinates in tables, satisfying the requirement for small-volume-corrected voxelwise evidence. Participant demographics are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (small-volume-corrected voxelwise results), I6 (results reported as tables of coordinates), and I7 (participant/cue details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only without SVC, not connectivity-only, and within-subject contrasts are present).

This fMRI study examines natural (food) reward cue-reactivity using visual cues (pictures/graphical snack baskets), and reports within-participant contrasts of reward>no-reward (anticipation of 10 SP > 0 SP). Analyses are group-level random-effects voxelwise GLMs with small-volume FWE correction within a defined bilateral ventral striatum ROI and report MNI peaks, satisfying the requirement for small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. Participant and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only without voxelwise SVC, includes within-subject contrasts). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study uses visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group results (peaks in table), but the reported contrasts are within-subject timepoint comparisons (post vs pre for dessert/vegetable no-go) rather than a within-participant cue>control (food cues > control stimuli) contrast required by I4. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. I3, I5, and I6 are met (visual natural-reward cues; whole-brain voxelwise results; results reported in table). I7 (reporting of MRI field strength and preprocessing/stat software) is not fully reported. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Main exclusion reason: missing within-participant cue>control contrast (I4).

The study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual images of highly desirable vs less desirable foods (I3). It includes within-participant contrasts of highly desirable > less desirable food images (first-level contrasts and paired t-tests across treatment) and reports group-level voxelwise results (whole-brain model fit and reported peak coordinates for the interaction and regressions), meeting I4 and I5. Results are reported as coordinates/tables (NeuroStore peaks and Table t4), acceptable per I6. Participant demographics and cue type are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/rest-only (E4), and include within-participant cue>control contrasts rather than only between-group contrasts (E5); the paper is empirical (not E6). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study reports a task-evoked fMRI contrast of erotic (natural reward) vs sport movies (control), using visual stimuli (erotic movies), satisfying the visual cue requirement. It contains a within-participant contrast (erotic > sport) at the group level and reports a voxel-wise whole-brain random-effects analysis with reported peak coordinates (Table), meeting the requirement for a qualifying group-level voxelwise result. Participant age/sex and cue type are reported; MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not listed in the NeuroStore record but missing methodological details do not alone exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Excluded because the NeuroStore record shows only ROI-based, between-group task contrasts and does not report any within-participant cue>control (reward>neutral) voxelwise contrasts. Extraction notes: 'Contrast: omnibus, between-group' and 'Model fit over: region of interest' for all analyses, with reported peaks in ROI tables (ventral striatum, parietal, PCC). Thus the paper lacks a qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast (I4 not met) and lacks group-level whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results (I5 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual monetary reward cues present) and I7 (participant demographics reported). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (ROI-only results) and E5 (only between-group contrasts/no within-participant cue>control). Full text is complete in the provided record.

This study examines fMRI cue-reactivity to visual food cues (150 images) relevant to natural rewards. It reports within-participant contrasts of high-calorie > low-calorie foods (fasted and fed sessions). Group-level voxelwise results are reported: whole-brain one-sample t-tests for the contrasts and small-volume-corrected voxelwise (FWE SVC) regression results in amygdala subregions. Peaks/tables are reported. Participant demographics and YFAS scores are provided. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears sufficiently represented in the document for screening.

This study reports task-evoked fMRI responses to visual food cues (color photographs) in children and includes a within-participant contrast of food>non-food (Analysis 30019454_analysis_0) using a group-level random-effects whole-brain GLM with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates (Table t2). It therefore meets the meta-analysis objective (natural reward visual cue-reactivity) and satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (visual cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (results reported in coordinate tables), and I7 (participant demographics and cue details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and contains within-participant contrast). Full text appears complete in this NeuroStore-derived record."
,

This study uses visual erotic stimuli (I3 met) in a within-subject drug (reboxetine/amisulpride/placebo) crossover with contrasts of erotic versus non-erotic pictures (within-participant cue>control contrast; I4 met). Participant demographics are reported (I7 met). However, all reported analyses were performed and inferred within predefined regions of interest ("Model fit over: region of interest" and "Inference restricted to: region of interest"). No whole-brain voxelwise or small-volume-corrected group-level task-evoked results are reported, so the study provides only ROI results. This violates the requirement for at least one qualifying whole-brain or SVC voxelwise result (I5 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Therefore the study is excluded.

This study assesses cue-reactivity using first-person perspective color videos (visual stimuli) and reports a within-participant Cigarette Cues > Neutral Cues contrast. At least one analysis is a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result with whole-brain inference and coordinate peaks reported in tables (cluster-corrected), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. Participant demographics and cue/task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control).

The study uses fMRI Monetary Incentive Delay task with clear visual anticipation cues (green/blue/red) for monetary reward/loss, satisfying reward-related visual cue requirement. It reports within-participant contrasts (reward > loss; reward/loss vs neutral) and also reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction (FWE SVC; model fit over whole-brain, inference restricted to ROI), meeting the requirement for qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results. Reported peak coordinates are present. Although some methodological details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not listed in this record, their absence does not exclude inclusion per criteria. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or lack of within-subject cue>control contrasts) apply.

This fMRI study of food (natural reward) used visual food images and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (analyses 0 and 1), so it meets I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence), and I6. However, it does not report a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (no neutral/control image contrast is presented). The reported contrasts compare regulation versus craving for the same food images (e.g., CRAVE_TASTY vs REGULATE_TASTY and PPI terms tied to REGULATE_TASTY4CRAVE_TASTY), which are instruction/condition contrasts rather than cue>control contrasts required by I4. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore exclude because inclusion criterion I4 is not met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images (foods with visible chili peppers vs foods without). It reports within-participant contrasts (spicy > non-spicy) for groups and group comparisons, and provides group-level voxelwise whole-brain inference (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain; FWE-corrected threshold; reported peak coordinates/tables). Participant demographics and cue details are reported. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrasts, and at least one qualifying whole-brain voxelwise result; reporting in tables satisfies acceptable result reporting. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts).

The study examines visual food cue reactivity (I3 satisfied) but the NeuroStore record reports only seed-based and PPI connectivity analyses (task-evoked connectivity and resting-state seed-based connectivity). There are no reported within-participant voxelwise task-evoked cue>control activation contrasts or small-volume-corrected task activation results. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 and I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only connectivity/resting-state/ppi results reported). Reported analyses are cross-subject regressions of connectivity with BMI; thresholding noted is for connectivity maps, not task-evoked contrasts. Inclusion criteria applied: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria applied: E4.

Exclusion E3 met: the critical reward-cue contrast (PR_no-go > PU_no-go) is reported only within a region-of-interest with inference restricted to that ROI; no group-level voxelwise (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) task-evoked result is reported for reward cues. Inclusion: I3 (fMRI with visual reward cues — conditioned monetary cues presented visually) and I4 (within-subject contrast PR_no-go > PU_no-go exists). Inclusion not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or SVC voxelwise task-evoked result for the cue>control contrast). Other whole-brain analyses present (no-go>go, age interactions) but do not provide the required cue>control voxelwise result; connectivity (PPI) is reported but is not a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise contrast (see E4). Therefore exclude.

This study used visual romantic cues (natural rewards) in an fMRI cue-reactivity task, and reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level results with cluster correction and peak coordinates (satisfying I3, I5, I6). Participant demographics and cue type are reported (I7). However, the NeuroStore extraction does not report any simple within-participant contrast of romantic cues > neutral/control stimuli; reported contrasts are interactions (between-group or hunger-state within-group interactions). Therefore the study does not provide a qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast required by I4, and meets exclusion criterion E5 (only interactive/between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

Study meets meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria: uses visual drug cues (cannabis and alcohol images) in a cue-reactivity task; includes within-participant contrast comparing substance images > comparison images (main effect of cue stimulus type); reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results with reported peak coordinates (Talairach) and cluster-thresholding details. Not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and provides voxelwise tables of peaks. Therefore qualifies for inclusion.

This study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: it uses visual drug cues (marijuana pipe/pencil) in a cue-reactivity fMRI task (I3). It includes a within-subject contrast of marijuana cues > control cues (analysis 20010552_analysis_2) (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results were estimated over the whole brain (FLAME group analysis) and reported with cluster-corrected peaks/tables (whole-brain cluster correction), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or SVC results (I5). Results are reported in tables of coordinates consistent with allowance in I6, and participant age/sex and other details are provided (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and a qualifying within-subject contrast is present, so E3–E6 do not apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This randomized, double-blind within-subject fMRI study used visual natural reward cues (IAPS erotic scenes) and includes at least one within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > neutral (Analysis 29959970_analysis_3: erotic stimuli > neutral stimuli, OT + PLA). That analysis is a group-level voxelwise result reported over the whole brain with FWE correction. The task and stimuli are visual. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cues>control contrast), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise result), and I6 (results reported as voxelwise peaks). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and not non-empirical). Full text is available in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports whole-brain voxelwise fMRI contrasts of food cue reactivity, but the contrasts compare healthy vs. unhealthy food (healthy>unhealthy and unhealthy>healthy) rather than reward-cues > control/neutral stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward food cues presented as visual images), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported with cluster correction), I6 (coordinates/peaks reported in tables), and I7 (participant age/sex etc. reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant contrast of reward cues > control/neutral stimuli is reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not provide a qualifying cue>control within-subject contrast required by I4.

This study used visual drug-word cues (I3 met) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume correction/whole-brain inference (I5 met). NeuroStore also reports coordinate tables/peaks (I6 met). However, the extracted analyses do not include any within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (drug>neutral) — instead the reported voxelwise results are medication contrasts (MPH>placebo), group comparisons, or regressions on drug- or neutral-word conditions separately. Because the review requires at least one within-subject drug>control cue contrast, and none is present in the document, this study must be excluded under exclusion criterion E5 (studies lacking a qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion IDs met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion ID not met: I4. Exclusion criterion met: E5.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high- and low-calorie food pictures vs. neutral object pictures). The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing food cues to neutral objects (e.g., high/low calorie food > neutral object) and a whole-brain random-effects ANOVA with reported peak coordinates (Talairach) in tables. Participant demographics are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, empirical task-evoked voxelwise results are presented). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion criteria met: E3 (study reports only region-of-interest analyses; model fit and inference restricted to ROI) and E5 (no qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast present). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using clear visual cues — Monetary Incentive Delay task with colored cue circles). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant contrast of reward cue > control stimulus is reported), I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked results; all inference restricted to ROIs), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results reported). Full text is available in the provided document. Given the ROI-only reporting and absence of a cue>control within-subject voxelwise contrast, the study does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

The study uses visual gaming cues (natural reward) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster-corrected), satisfying I3, I5, I6, and I7. However, the NeuroStore record only provides group-level interaction and between-group contrasts (group x condition interaction; between-group comparisons after training) and does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., win>loss within participants). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group/interaction contrasts without an accompanying within-participant cue>control analysis). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

The NeuroStore extraction shows only a genotype x reward category omnibus between-group interaction (analysis 28507526_analysis_0) with inference restricted to an ROI and FWE small-volume correction. The study includes visual reward cues (photographs, money) satisfying I3 and reports a small-volume-corrected voxelwise result satisfying I5. However, no within-participant cue>control (reward cue > control stimulus) contrast is reported in the extraction (I4 not met). Because the only reported voxelwise result is a between-group interaction with no accompanying within-subject cue>control contrast, exclusion criterion E5 applies. Therefore the study is excluded.

This fMRI study investigates neural responses to food cues (natural reward) using standardized visual images (food vs. non-food), fulfilling the review objective. It reports within-participant contrasts of food>non-food (Analysis 29426874_analysis_0) and treatment-related interactions (Analysis 1). Analyses were conducted and reported as whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in tables (whole-brain inference and reported peaks), meeting the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Results are presented in tables of coordinates (reported peaks), which is acceptable. Participant demographics and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, or only between-group contrasts) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is included.

The study examines neural responses to visual sexual images (natural rewards) during an fMRI task, meeting the review topic. It reports within-participant contrasts of sexual > neutral images (SexPC>NeutralPC; SexLO>NeutralLO) as group-level voxelwise results with voxel-level FWE thresholding, but inference restricted to anatomical regions (ROI masks), consistent with small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. Peaks are reported in tables. Participant demographics (age, sex) and stimuli are described. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural-reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise small-volume-corrected results), and I6 (results reported as peaks/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Some preprocessing/MRI field-strength details are not shown in this record, but I7 is preferred and missing details alone do not exclude the study.

This fMRI study tested smokers (nicotine dependence) viewing visual cigarette-related stimuli (graphic warning labels) vs scrambled control images in a within-subject block design and measured craving — directly addressing cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component. It reports within-participant contrasts of LABEL (HIGH/LOW) > CONTROL and whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results (FILM single-group t tests) with cluster-level FWE correction and reported peak coordinates (tables/figures). Although MRI field strength and preprocessing/software details are not provided in the record, missing these details does not exclude the study per review guidance. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met; I7 (preferred reporting of all acquisition/processing details) is not fully satisfied but is not required. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports fMRI cue-reactivity to visual water-related (natural reward) and drug-related images in 14 heroin-dependent participants. It includes within-subject contrasts Thirst (Water) > Neutral and Drug > Neutral at the group level, estimated with a standard SPM second-level one-sample t-test over the whole brain and reports peak coordinates (table). Thus it provides qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain) for both natural reward-related and drug-related visual cue contrasts. Reporting includes participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength (1.5T) and SPM analysis. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity analysis using visual food cues (images of milkshake and water) and a within-participant contrast (anticipated milkshake > anticipated tasteless solution) evaluated in whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level correction (AFNI 3DClustSim; p<0.001) and reported peak coordinates. Participant demographics (age/sex) are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study reports task-evoked fMRI cue-reactivity to visual food images (child-friendly high- and low-calorie food images vs non-food objects) in children with obesity. It includes within-subject contrasts of natural reward-related cues > control (high-calorie > objects; low-calorie > objects; high-calorie > low-calorie) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (model fit and inference over whole brain with cluster correction; coordinate peaks reported in Table t3). Participant demographics and cue types are provided. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; I7 (preferred details) is met sufficiently for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and include within-participant cue>control contrasts. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual reward cue-reactivity.

This fMRI study examines natural reward-related visual cues (erotic and sadomasochistic pictures) and reports within-participant contrasts of reward-related cues>neutral (Sm>Neutral) within the patient group. It includes group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results with whole-brain inference for Sm>Neutral and other contrasts (whole-brain, corrected). Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. Therefore the study addresses the review objective and meets required criteria for visual natural-reward cue-reactivity, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) results. ROI analyses are present but whole-brain results are also reported. Full text appears readable in the provided record.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study with visual smoking stimuli (I3 met). It reports voxelwise, ROI-restricted (small-volume) corrected task-evoked results with peak coordinates/tables (I5 and I6 met). Participant details are provided (I7 met). However, the NeuroStore record does not report any within-participant contrast that is explicitly smoking-cues > control stimuli (e.g., smoking images > teeth-brushing or neutral images). Reported within-subject contrasts are BEGIN vs END (different stages of smoking) or condition activations without an explicit cue>control contrast; many reported contrasts are between-group or stage comparisons. Therefore the required inclusion criterion I4 (within-participant drug-cues > control contrast) is not satisfied. Because the study lacks a qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast, it meets exclusion criterion E5. Full text is complete per the provided record.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, with whole-brain voxelwise group-level results (cluster-corrected peaks reported in a table). However, the NeuroStore record shows only between-group interaction contrasts (women vs men responses to hedonic vs control images) and does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast result at the group level. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cue fMRI), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I6 (results reported in table of coordinates). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported).

This study uses visually presented card stimuli that cue monetary reward (natural reward), with within-participant contrasts of reward anticipation > baseline (visual cue-driven reward anticipation). It reports voxelwise results restricted to a bilateral ventral-striatum ROI with FWE voxel-level inference (i.e., small-volume-corrected voxelwise evidence) and provides coordinate peaks and participant details. These elements satisfy I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (small-volume-corrected voxelwise result), I6 (reported peaks/coordinates), and I7 (participant demographics reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This fMRI cue-reactivity study includes visual heroin-related cues (I3 met) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level task-evoked results with coordinate peaks (I5 and I6 met). Participant demographics and cue details are reported (I7 met). However, all extracted statistical contrasts are omnibus or between-group interaction contrasts (ABT>Ctrl, MMT>Ctrl, ABT>MMT, and a main group F), and the NeuroStore record does not show a within-participant drug-cues > control (drug>neutral) simple effect reported at the group voxelwise level. Because the paper appears to report only between-group/interactions without a qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast, it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5. Therefore the study is excluded.

This study examines BOLD responses to visual food cues (72 color photographs) with within-participant Food > Non-Food contrasts reported for multiple groups and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain inference (model fit and inference over whole brain; FDR thresholding) with peak coordinates. It therefore satisfies I3 (natural reward visual cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables), and I7 (participant age/sex reported). No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts so E5 is not met. Full text is represented by the NeuroStore extraction, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Excluded because it does not contain a qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast of natural reward (food) cues versus control stimuli (I4 not met). Instead, reported contrasts are attentional contrasts (alerting: double cue>no cue; reorienting: incongruent>congruent) that use food pictures as task targets but do not compare food cues to control stimuli. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the study reports only contrasts other than the required within-participant cue>control contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI of natural reward-related visual cues: food pictures), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (results reported as peaks/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant reward>control contrast). I7 (reporting of MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software) is partially incomplete in the document. Full text is complete for screening purposes.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E3. The NeuroStore extraction states the model was fit over a region of interest for the reported analyses, indicating the paper reports only ROI-based results with no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group result. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward-related cue: erotic visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant contrast ERO > HA reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked result available). Full text is complete in the provided record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study is an fMRI investigation using visual erotic videos (natural reward-related cues) and includes within-participant contrasts of erotic > sports (analyses 0 and 2). Model fit was conducted over the whole brain and voxelwise peaks are reported in tables, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Results and participant demographics are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7.

This study does not report any task-evoked fMRI cue-reactivity contrast (drug cues > control) required for inclusion. Although participants rated cigarette pictures behaviorally, the fMRI scans reported were an interoceptive attention task and resting-state connectivity. The only voxelwise task result (interoception > exteroception) is unrelated to visual cue-reactivity. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, and I5 are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list are directly triggered by the study document (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Full text is complete for screening purposes.

This study is excluded because it reports only ROI-based voxelwise/model-fit results and does not present any whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. This violates inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity to natural reward visual stimuli—food images), I4 (within-participant contrast: high-calorie > low-calorie food images), and I7 (participant age/sex and cue details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or SVC group-level voxelwise task-evoked result). No other exclusion criteria (E4, E5, E6) apply. Full text appears complete in the provided NeuroStore record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The NeuroStore record reports visual food cue reactivity (I3 met) and a group-level voxelwise result using small-volume correction (SVC) (I5 met; I6 also satisfied since peaks/SVC are reported). However, the only extracted analysis is a between-group interaction (MetS criterion × cue) / subgroup comparison (interaction specified as between-group); no within-participant cue>control (e.g., highly desirable > less desirable) simple contrast at the group level is reported in the document. Therefore the study reports only between-group/interaction results without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast, meeting exclusion criterion E5. Full text appears available in this record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study assesses natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images and an instructed imagery task, fulfilling the review’s stimulus modality requirement. It reports within-subject cue contrasts (High-energy > Low-energy foods), satisfying the cue>control within-participant contrast requirement. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results were estimated and inferred over the whole brain (voxel-wise t-tests/ANOVA) with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinate peaks reported in tables, meeting the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results (and acceptable coordinate/table reporting). Although MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software are not reported in the NeuroStore extract (I7 is preferred but not required), this alone does not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (only ROI results, connectivity/resting-state only, or lack of within-participant cue>control contrasts) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

The study uses visual reward-predicting cues (grey-scale cue pictures for monetary reward), and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results with coordinate tables — satisfying I3, I5, and I6. However, all extracted statistical contrasts in the provided document are between-group interaction contrasts (e.g., group × condition comparisons) and no within-participant cue > control (reward-predicting cue > neutral cue) voxelwise contrast is listed. Because the document does not contain an explicit within-participant cue>control contrast, this violates inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group/interaction contrasts reported without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control result). Note: the abstract describes within-group effects, but the NeuroStore-extracted analyses provided here do not include a qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast; per instructions I base the decision on the provided document.

This fMRI study examines monetary reward cue processing with clear visual cues (rectangle/diamond cues with currency symbols) and concurrent threat; it reports within-subject contrasts of reward > no-reward (and related contrasts) during an event-related task. Analyses were estimated and tested at the whole-brain voxelwise level with cluster-corrected inference and reported coordinate peaks (Table 1), satisfying group-level voxelwise result requirements. Participant demographics (n=20, age mean and SD, sex) are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant reward>control contrasts), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise group results), I6 (coordinates/tables reported), and I7 (participant details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text is available via the NeuroStore record representation.

This study examines visual reward cues (colored squares/star) in a Monetary Incentive Delay task (natural reward-related cues). It reports within-participant cue>no-outcome contrasts (win/loss > no-outcome; Analysis 19631753_analysis_6) satisfying the cue>control requirement, and also reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (Analyses 19631753_analysis_10–15) with coordinate/cluster tables. Thus it meets I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (at least one group-level voxelwise result), and I6 (results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper does not report only ROI analyses (whole-brain results present), is not connectivity/resting-only, and includes within-participant cue contrasts, so E3–E5 do not apply. Document appears complete for screening. Included for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity with visual stimuli.

This study reports visual cue-reactivity to food (natural reward) using a block-design fMRI cue-reactivity task with image stimuli (sweets, snacks, fast-food, meats/fruits/vegetables vs nonfood). It includes within-participant contrasts of food>nonfood and specific food-category>nonfood (e.g., sweets>nonfood) at the group level (second-level random-effects GLM), with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates (Tables tbl2/tbl3). Participant age/sex and clinical characteristics are reported. These elements satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for visual natural reward cue-reactivity and voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

The study directly investigates visual natural-reward cues (food images) and reports within-subject contrasts of food > non-food (Analyses 0 and 1). Both qualifying contrasts are group-level, voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain inference (FWE cluster-level thresholds) and reported peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise evidence. Visual stimuli are clearly used. The NeuroStore extract lists participant demographics (age/sex) and cue type; MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistics software are not reported in the extract, but I7 is a preferred (not mandatory) item. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Thus the paper meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This study investigates erotic (natural reward) visual stimuli and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (Talairach coordinates, cluster peaks), and provides participant demographics. However, the NeuroStore record lists only omnibus between-group contrasts (e.g., sex, age, sex×age×group) and does not report any within-participant cue>control contrasts (e.g., erotic>neutral) required by I4. Therefore it violates exclusion E5 (only between-group contrasts reported without a qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I6 (results reported in tables/peaks), I7 (participant age/sex reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast). fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study examines monetary (financial) reward cues (coin images) rather than drug cues or natural rewards (e.g., food, sexual, social). The review objective is drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity; monetary secondary rewards do not meet that scope. Although the study includes within-participant contrasts of reward>absent and reports group-level voxelwise results (small-volume-corrected and whole-brain results are present) and provides coordinate tables, the critical content requirement (I3 and I4: drug or natural reward-related cues) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded for not addressing the specified reward types in the review objective.

This fMRI study examined neural responses to food cues (natural rewards) using visual photographs and a cue-reactivity task, meeting the review objective. The report includes within-participant contrasts comparing food cues versus control objects (e.g., fattening>object; fattening>non-fattening) (I4). Group-level voxelwise statistical results were estimated and reported within anatomically defined regions of interest with cluster-level inference per ROI (cluster-thresholding per ROI and reported peak coordinates in tables), which constitutes small-volume-corrected voxelwise results satisfying I5 and I6. Participant age/sex, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported (I7). Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not limited to connectivity or non-empirical work; includes within-subject cue>control contrasts).

This study examines natural reward (erotic) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (IAPS images) and reports within-participant erotic>neutral contrasts in both blocked and event-related designs. Crucially, group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical results are reported for erotic>neutral (Analyses 18647397_analysis_0 and _2) with voxelwise FDR thresholds and peak tables, satisfying the requirement for qualifying whole-brain task-evoked results. Participant age and sex and cue type are reported; MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software are not reported in the NeuroStore extract but missing methodological details do not exclude the study per I7. ROI interaction analyses are present but are not the only results. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Thus the paper meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 (I7 partially met as participant/cue details reported).

This study examines neural responses to visual food cues (high- and low-calorie images) versus control objects in humans (natural reward cue-reactivity), meeting the review focus. It reports within-group, within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > objects; low-calorie > objects) used in cross-subject regression, satisfying a cue>control within-participant contrast. Group-level voxelwise results were reported with small-volume FWE correction and peak coordinates (reported peaks: 5 and 1), which meets the requirement for qualifying voxelwise small-volume-corrected results. Results are available as coordinate peaks in tables, satisfying acceptability of coordinate reporting. Participant and task details are provided. No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only seed-based connectivity or resting-state analyses, and it includes task-evoked voxelwise small-volume-corrected results rather than only ROI-unreported voxelwise data. Therefore all necessary inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This study examines natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (erotic video sequences). It includes a within-participant analysis comparing menstrual phases (paired t-test: mid-luteal vs menses) that involves the erotic>neutral contrast (analysis 16604320_analysis_2, reported as an interaction within-group). The model was fit over the whole brain and voxelwise peaks are reported (Table 1), satisfying the requirement for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. Coordinate/peak reporting is present. Participant demographics and cue type are reported in the NeuroStore record. MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not reported in the extract, so I7 is not marked as satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met: the study reports a whole-brain voxelwise result (not ROI-only), reports task-evoked contrasts (not only connectivity or resting-state), and includes a within-participant cue>control contrast rather than only between-group contrasts. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria and is INCLUDED.

The study examines neural responses to erotic (natural reward) visual stimuli (I3 satisfied) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group results with peak coordinates (I5 and I6 satisfied). However, all reported contrasts in the NeuroStore record are between-group interactions (e.g., healthy erotic > pedophilic emotional; interaction contrasts) and do not present a within-participant cue>control (e.g., erotic>neutral) contrast at the group level that would qualify per the review’s I4. Therefore the study meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-subject cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual cues (IAPS images) as natural reward stimuli and reports within-subject contrasts (Sexual Images > Non-Sexual Images) at the group level with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference. Voxelwise results are reported as peak tables. Participant demographics (age, sex) are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This fMRI study investigates brain reactivity to visual food cues (natural reward). It reports within-participant task contrasts of food cues (e.g., high-calorie > low-calorie; food images > neutral/non-food images) used in group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with reported peak coordinates (MNI). Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise, and thresholded with cluster-correction; peak coordinates/tables are reported. These features satisfy the review’s requirements for visual cue reactivity, a within-participant cue>control contrast, and a group-level voxelwise whole-brain result. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; contains task-evoked voxelwise contrasts).

Exclusion E5 met: the reported voxelwise task results do not include a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli. Although the study examines food cue conditioning with visual abstract images (I3) and reports a task-evoked small-volume-corrected voxelwise result during food-odor conditioning (I5) and reports peaks (compatible with I6), the only cue-related contrast extracted is CS- > CS+ (air-paired images > odor-paired images) which is the opposite direction required by I4. The other reported significant result is an interaction of ghrelin > saline (drug administration effect) rather than a within-participant cues>control contrast. Therefore it fails the required inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5.

The study uses visual alcohol cues and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE, voxel-level) and peak coordinates (so I3, I5, I6 are satisfied). However, the NeuroStore extraction shows only between-group/interaction contrasts (HC > ADP for emotion conditions including alcohol vs neutral) and does not report a within-participant drug-cue > control-stimulus contrast. Therefore the study does not meet inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group/interaction results without an accompanying within-subject cue>control contrast). fulltext_incomplete=false

This study examines cue-reactivity to Internet video game visual stimuli (450s videotape) and reports a within-subject contrast of Internet video game stimuli > neutral stimuli (Analysis 21220070_analysis_0). That analysis is a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects GLM with FDR voxelwise thresholding and reported peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result. Participant demographics and cue type are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise result), and I6 (voxelwise results/peaks reported). This fMRI study tests responses to pornographic (visual) cues (natural reward) during a letter n-back task, so it addresses the review objective (visual reward cues). It reports a within-participant contrast Explicit > Neutral with whole-brain, FWE-corrected voxelwise results (peaks/tables reported), and additional whole-brain interaction and connectivity analyses. Thus it meets I3 (visual fMRI cue study), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast present), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported), and I6 (voxelwise results available in tables). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only (E3), not limited to connectivity-only (E4), and the within-subject cue>control contrast is present (so E5 does not apply). Full text appears accessible in the provided NeuroStore record. Therefore INCLUDE.

The study is excluded because it does not include a within-participant cue>control contrast of natural reward cues versus control stimuli (I4 not met). The paper reports task-instruction contrasts (inhibition, imaginary eating, passive viewing) all using food images, but no cue versus neutral/control stimulus contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues—food images), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (results reported in tables/figures), I7 (participant age/sex and MRI field strength reported). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (no qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast; study reports only task-instruction contrasts and between-group interactions relevant to cue reactivity). Full text was available in the provided record.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI task assessing natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (∼150 food and non-food images) (I3). It reports a within-participant contrast of highly desirable foods > less desirable foods (an appropriate natural reward-related cue>control contrast, interaction within-group) (I4). The analysis is a group-level voxelwise GLM with model fit over the whole brain and FWE thresholding, with reported peak coordinate(s), satisfying the whole-brain voxelwise result requirement (I5, I6). Participant demographics and task details are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Sample is randomized double-blind crossover but that does not conflict with inclusion.

This study reports a visual cue-reactivity fMRI task using food images (natural reward) with a within-subject contrast (food > non-food). Group-level, voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses were performed with whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference, and peak coordinates are reported (tables). MRI field strength (3T), participant sex and sample size are provided. These elements satisfy the review’s requirements for visual cue type, within-participant cue>control contrast, and qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical human fMRI data). I7 (preferred reporting items) is partially reported but is not required for inclusion.

The study uses visual erotic film stimuli (natural reward) and reports whole-brain voxelwise cluster-thresholded results with peak coordinates (meets I3, I5, I6, I7). However, all reported statistical maps are interaction contrasts comparing menstrual phases (e.g., (erotic>neutral)_OTH > (erotic>neutral)_OVU). The article does not report a standalone within-participant cue>control (erotic > neutral) group-level contrast. Per exclusion criterion E5, studies that report only between-group contrasts or interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast must be excluded. Therefore, despite meeting other inclusion criteria, the lack of a direct within-subject cue>control contrast prevents inclusion.

The study reports a cue-reactivity fMRI task using visual heroin-related photographs (I3). It includes a within-participant contrast drug cues > neutral with group-level voxelwise results (Analysis 24720731_analysis_1: drug cues > neutral; FWE voxel-level; reported peaks), satisfying I4 and I5. Coordinate/peak tables are reported (I6). Participant age/sex and cue type are provided; although some preprocessing/MRI details are not shown, their absence does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrast).

The NeuroStore record documents only between-group interaction contrasts (e.g., “Alcohol nogo > Nonalcohol go between ADP > HC”, “Geometric_nogo > Geometric_go between HC > ADP”), reported as whole-brain voxelwise results.
