While the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (visual alcohol-cue fMRI), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported with coordinates/peaks), I6 (results available in tables/peaks), and I7 (participant demographics reported), it does NOT report any within-participant cue>control contrast (drug cues > control stimuli) at the group level. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 is met: the paper reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast. Excluded for failing I4 (no within-participant drug-cue>control contrast).

This study uses visual natural reward cues (food pictures) and reports whole-brain voxelwise within-subject contrasts with peak coordinates (meets I3, I5, I6, and I7). However, the only extracted within-participant contrast is unpleasant > pleasant (within-group). The meta-analysis requires at least one within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (I4). No reward>control (e.g., pleasant>fixation, pleasant>neutral, or pleasant>nonfood) contrast is reported in the provided document. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Because inclusion criterion I4 is not met, the study must be excluded.

The study examines natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual food pictures (meets I3). However, the NeuroStore record only reports region-of-interest (fROI) analyses and region-level thresholding (model fit over ROI; no whole-brain voxelwise or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results reported), and the reported contrasts are between-group (overweight > healthy-weight) and group × attention interactions rather than a within-participant cue>control contrast. Therefore it violates inclusion criteria I4 and I5 and meets exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only, no qualifying voxelwise result) and E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study used visual erotic film clips (natural reward-related visual cues) and reports a within-subject contrast of erotic > neutral film segments (block design, pooled group data N=10). The analysis is a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical result (model fit over whole brain, voxel-level threshold p<0.001) with reported peak coordinates (Table 2). Participant demographics and cue type are reported. These elements satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue-reactivity, a within-participant cue>control contrast, and a qualifying whole-brain voxelwise result. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical human fMRI data). MRI field strength and software are not reported in this record, but missing preprocessing/software details do not preclude inclusion per criteria.

The study uses visual alcohol cues (I3 met) and reports a whole-brain voxelwise cross-subject regression (analysis_1) and ROI omnibus interaction (analysis_0), with reported peak coordinates (I5 and I6 met). However, no analysis in the NeuroStore record explicitly reports a within-participant cue contrast of drug (alcohol) cues > control stimuli. The reported analyses are (a) a medication-by-image-type omnibus, reported as a between-group omnibus ROI interaction, and (b) a cross-subject regression relating activation to number of infusions (whole-brain). Because there is no explicit within-subject alcohol-cue > control contrast reported, the study does not satisfy inclusion criterion I4 and falls under exclusion E5 (studies reporting only between-group contrasts/interactions or cross-subject regressions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete in the NeuroStore record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study reports task-based fMRI using visual food cues (natural rewards) and includes within-subject contrasts of hedonic food cues > nonfood objects (analyses 2 and 3). Multiple group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain results are reported (FWE/FDR thresholding; whole-brain inference; second-level GLM), satisfying the requirement for qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results. Visual stimuli and participant demographics are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only without within-subject cue>control, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This fMRI study uses visual erotic pictures as natural reward cues and reports a within-participant CS+ > CS− contrast (Analysis 26936075_analysis_0) with whole-brain voxelwise inference (one-sample t-test, reported peaks). That satisfies visual cue-reactivity (I3), a within-participant cue>control contrast (I4), and a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result reported at whole-brain level (I5). Results are reported as peaks/tables (I6) and participant age/sex etc. are provided (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only connectivity, includes within-subject contrast). Full text is available in the record.

This study investigates neural responses to erotic (visual) stimuli (natural reward) and reports group-level voxelwise results; however, all extracted analyses are between-group contrasts/interactions (controls > ED, ED > controls, and group-by-within-subject interactions for onset/sustained erection > dance baseline). The document does not report a standalone within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., erotic>dance) as a primary within-subject result. Therefore it meets exclusion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues present), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain/small-volume-corrected results reported), I6 (coordinate/table reporting acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no reported within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text is available in the NeuroStore record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study reports fMRI cue-reactivity to visual food cues (high-caloric vs low-caloric images) in a within-subject crossover design (event-related Cue Reactivity Task). It includes a within-participant contrast HC>LC at group level (Analysis 29247796_analysis_0). The statistical results are voxelwise within an a priori region of interest (ventral tegmental area) with FWE thresholding and peak coordinates reported in a table, consistent with small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. These facts satisfy inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise small-volume-corrected result), and I6 (reported peaks/tables). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not limited to non-task connectivity, not only between-group contrasts, and it provides qualifying voxelwise ROI/SVC results (so E3 does not apply). Participant demographics and cue type are reported; MRI specifics are not extracted here but missing details do not preclude inclusion. Full text appears complete for screening.

The study investigates nalmefene effects on emotion processing using emotional face stimuli (angry/fearful) versus neutral geometric forms. Although it reports within-participant, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (faces>forms) with coordinate peaks (meeting I5 and I6), the stimuli are not drug-related cues nor clearly natural reward-related cues. Therefore it does not satisfy I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual cues) nor I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues>control or natural reward-related cues>control). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text is complete for screening.

This study uses fMRI with visual erotic (natural reward) stimuli and reports voxelwise peaks (Table 1) with inference restricted to ROIs (small-volume approach), so it meets I3 (visual natural reward cue), I5 (group-level voxelwise/SVC result), I6 (coordinates reported), and I7 (participant age/sex reported). However, all extracted contrasts are between-group interaction contrasts (e.g., Male erotic > Female nonerotic; Male erotic > MTF nonerotic) and the document does not show a within-participant cue>control contrast (erotic > nonerotic) reported at the group level. Because no qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast is available, the study violates exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast) and does not satisfy I4. Therefore exclude.

This study used only ROI-based voxelwise analyses (Model fit over: region of interest; ROI mask), and does not report any whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). The study does meet I3 (natural reward-related cue reactivity with visual package images). It does not clearly meet I4 (no clear within-participant contrast of reward cue > neutral control; contrasts compare two food-package types) and does not meet I5 (no whole-brain or SVC voxelwise results).

This study examines fMRI responses to alcohol visual cues (meets I3) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results with coordinates in tables (meets I5 and I6). However, all reported contrasts are between-group interactions (e.g., Transitioned-to-heavy × alcohol vs non-alcohol groups) and the NeuroStore record does not report any within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-subject cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast absent); I7 not fully reported (MRI field strength/preprocessing/software not provided). Full text is available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study uses natural food rewards with visual cues (chocolate pictures and control images) and reports voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (FWE-corrected, reported peaks), so it satisfies I3, I5 and I6. However, the NeuroStore record does not provide any explicit within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (I4) — the extracted contrasts are drug comparisons (placebo vs naltrexone) and lack a clear cue>control contrast. Because I4 is not met, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met. Detailed reporting (e.g., MRI field strength or preprocessing software) is incomplete but does not affect this exclusion.

This fMRI study examines anticipation of primary taste rewards signaled by visual cues (clear visual cue component) and reports within-subject cue>control contrasts (e.g., ANTglc > ANTneu, ANTslt > ANTneu). It provides voxelwise task-evoked results: at least one contrast with whole-brain inference (ANTglc > ANTslt) and other contrasts reported with voxelwise thresholds or small-volume correction; peak coordinates are reported. Participant age/sex and cue types are reported. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper does not report only ROI or only connectivity analyses, and it includes within-participant cue>control contrasts. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue reactivity to natural rewards.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study in non-treatment-seeking heavy drinkers that includes visual alcohol cues (visual cues paired with taste delivery), and reports a within-participant contrast Alcohol Taste > Water Taste at the group (higher-level) voxelwise whole-brain level with reported peak coordinates (tables). These satisfy inclusion criteria I3 (visual/multimodal with visual cues), I4 (drug-cue > control within-participant contrast available at group level), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported), I6 (results reported as coordinate tables), and I7 (participant age/sex reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears available from the NeuroStore-derived record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study uses visual food cues and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (peaks), but it does not report any within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control (e.g., food > baseline/control). Reported within-group contrasts are control>food (LLB > food; Non-Food control > food) and between-group interactions. Therefore it fails the required within-participant cue>control contrast (I4). Excluded under E5.

The study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports a within-participant group-level contrast (Food > Nonfood) tested with a whole-brain voxelwise one-sample t-test and provides peak coordinates (Table t1). Additional whole-brain multiple regression analyses are also reported. Participant demographics (age/sex), cue type, and task details are provided. Thus the paper satisfies the requirement for a task-evoked voxelwise result (whole-brain), includes a clear visual cue component, and reports necessary details. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

The study used an fMRI task with visual food cues and nonfood control images and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (peaks/tables) from within-group cross-subject regressions linking subject measures (e.g., HOMA-IR, TFEQ, Baecke indices) to BOLD responses. The GLM terms include stimulus blocks, and inference was performed over the whole brain with reported peaks, indicating qualifying task-evoked voxelwise analyses. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for natural reward (food) visual cue-reactivity, contains within-participant task contrasts modeled and tested at the group voxelwise level, and provides coordinate results in tables.

This fMRI study assesses natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (40 high-calorie food pictures vs 40 non-food pictures). It reports within-participant contrasts (Food > Non-food) for AN, BN, and HC groups. Several group-level voxelwise task-evoked results were fit over the whole brain and reported as peak coordinates (tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results. Although the paper also reports seed-based/effective connectivity analyses, it additionally provides the qualifying task-evoked contrasts, so exclusion criteria for connectivity-only or ROI-only studies do not apply. Key inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6, and participant details satisfy I7 (reported age/sex and cue type); no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This fMRI study examines reactivity to visual sexual cues (photographs), qualifying as natural reward-related cue-reactivity (I3). The NeuroStore record reports within-participant cue>control contrasts (e.g., ‘expectancy of adult sexual stimuli > fixation’ and picture-viewing > fixation/child contrasts), satisfying I4. Multiple analyses report group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates/tables (Analyses 0, 3–10 and follow-up contrasts with reported peaks), meeting I5 and I6. Participant demographics and task details are reported (age, sex, stimuli, software), so I7 is satisfied. Although several reported contrasts are between-group interactions, within-participant cue>control contrasts are present, so exclusion E5 does not apply. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual natural reward cue-reactivity and is included.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to visual food cues (visual-only stimuli) in obese subjects, directly addressing natural reward-related cue-reactivity (I3). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of food > non-food (within-group) at specific states (analyses 0 and 1: Wtinitial and Wt-10%leptin) satisfying I4. At least one qualifying voxelwise result was reported with inference restricted to a hypothalamic ROI (voxelwise ROI analysis/masked area) which constitutes a small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise result (I5). Additionally, the study reports whole-brain group-level random-effects voxelwise interaction contrasts (analyses 2–5) with peaks listed in tables, satisfying I6. Participant demographics and cue details are provided (I7). None of the exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (whole-brain voxelwise results are reported), not connectivity-only, and include within-participant cue>control contrasts (so E3–E5 do not apply). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study investigates natural reward cue-reactivity to palatable food and uses visual cues (pictures of milkshake and water), and includes a within-participant contrast (milkshake anticipation > water anticipation), so inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are met. However, all reported task analyses are restricted to region-of-interest (ROI) masks for model fitting and inference; no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported. Therefore the study fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). PPI connectivity analyses are also reported, but these do not substitute for the required task-evoked voxelwise results (E4 does not apply because a task ROI contrast is present). Full text is available in the provided document (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This fMRI study uses visual erotic (natural reward) cues from IAPS and an affective picture viewing task (I3). It reports within-participant contrasts comparing bodily/sexual pictures to non-bodily/control pictures (e.g., positive bodily > positive non-bodily), satisfying the required cue>control within-subject contrast (I4). Analyses are second-level, random-effects, voxelwise whole-brain group results with thresholding and reported peak coordinates/tables, meeting the voxelwise whole-brain result requirement (I5) and acceptable reporting formats (I6). Participant demographics (age, sex) and task details are provided (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-participant contrasts. Full text is available via the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual food images (natural rewards) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results. However, the NeuroStore extraction lists only omnibus between-group contrasts (commercial condition, weight status, interaction) and does not explicitly report a within-participant cue>control (e.g., food images > blurred controls) voxelwise contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural-reward cues present), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I6 (coordinates/peaks reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no explicit within-participant cue>control contrast identified). Exclusion criterion triggered: E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study examines natural reward (high-calorie food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (color photographs) and reports within-subject contrasts of high-calorie cues > nonfood control (pre-post Visit2 vs Visit1) and associated regressions with appetite change. Crucially, the paper includes group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported as whole-brain analyses (reported peaks/tables) as well as ROI results. The sample and stimuli are clearly described. Although some methodological details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not reported in this NeuroStore record, the presence of whole-brain voxelwise cue>control contrasts satisfies the meta-analysis requirements.

The study presents fMRI evidence of responses to visual food cues (food pictures) and includes a within-participant contrast of food > object pictures (Analysis 1). That analysis is a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked result with reported peak coordinates (meets requirement for voxelwise reporting). Participant demographics and MRI details (7T) and thresholding/statistical software (AFNI 3dClustSim) are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

The study reports an fMRI investigation of a natural reward (food) using visual cues (snack images) and includes within-participant contrasts comparing food vs nonfood (e.g., snack onset > trinket onset) and food-specific effects after sleep deprivation. At least one qualifying group-level voxelwise result is reported with small-volume correction (FWE-SVC) and voxel-level peaks (coordinates reported). Results and peaks are available and participant demographics and cue type are reported. These satisfy inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity and voxelwise task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical human fMRI data).

The study examines visual cue-reactivity to natural (erotic) and monetary rewards using explicit visual cues in an fMRI Monetary Incentive Delay task. It reports within-participant contrasts (monetary cue > control and erotic cue > control) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical results with cluster-level correction and reported peak coordinates. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. The preferred reporting elements in I7 (e.g., MRI field strength, full age reporting) are not fully reported but are not required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This fMRI study directly assesses alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using explicit visual cues (beer-predicting cues listed) and a task where beer vs water trials are contrasted. It reports within-subject contrasts (beer > water) for anticipation, notification, and tasting phases. Analyses were whole-brain voxelwise (model fit and inference over whole brain) with peak coordinates reported (cluster-level FWE thresholding), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Although MRI field strength and some preprocessing/software details are not listed here, the document provides participant demographics and cue information; missing preprocessing details do not exclude the study per I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

The NeuroStore record reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results comparing responses to monetary and pleasant-image rewards in MDD vs controls (coordinates/tables available). It therefore meets I3 (natural reward-related visual cues present), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), and I6 (coordinate tables available). However, all extracted contrasts are described as between-group interaction contrasts (patient vs control; interactions of Group x Reward type/Trial type) with no clearly reported within-participant cue>control (e.g., images>neutral) voxelwise contrast in the extraction. Because the study appears to report only between-group/interactions without an accompanying within-subject cue>control voxelwise result, it meets exclusion criterion E5. Thus the study is excluded.

Excluded because all reported analyses were ROI-based with inference restricted to regions of interest and no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level results are reported (meets exclusion criterion E3). The study does satisfy I3 (fMRI with clear visual natural reward cues — food images) and I4 (within-participant Food>Neutral contrasts are reported). However it fails I5 because no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results are provided (only ROI inference, uncorrected thresholds). Therefore the paper does not meet all inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This fMRI study used visual erotic videos (natural reward sexual stimuli) and reports within-participant contrasts of erotic vs neutral stimuli (explicitly stated in abstract and represented by within-group 'COR' simple-effect analyses). Multiple group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects results are reported (analyses 2–5: whole-brain, p<0.001; and group contrasts/interactions also available), with coordinate tables/peaks provided. Although an ROI (preoptic area) analysis is present, qualifying whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results are also reported, so the study is not excluded by E3. Participant demographics and task are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI visual natural reward cue-reactivity and provides qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results.

Excluded because the study does not meet the visual-cue requirement (I3) and does not report any within-participant cue>control contrasts (I4). The task used personalized audiotaped imagery scripts (auditory), so there is no clear visual cue component (I3 not met). All extracted contrasts are described as omnibus between-group contrasts; no within-subject drug- or reward-cue > control contrasts are reported, triggering exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts reported). The study does provide whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (Model fit over: whole brain; inference over: whole brain), satisfying I5, and reports participant age/sex and cue type, satisfying I7. Therefore the paper must be excluded for meta-analysis focused on visual cue-reactivity and requiring within-participant cue>control contrasts.

Excluded because the paper reports only ROI-based task analyses and does not provide a qualifying within-participant cue>control voxelwise result. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (only region-of-interest analyses reported; model fit and inference restricted to ROIs). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward-related visual cues — food images), I7 (participant demographics reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant contrast of reward cues > control stimuli reported — reported contrasts are Large vs Small portion and High vs Low energy density, not cue>control), I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level results reported), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results reported in tables/figures/supplement). Therefore the study must be excluded under E3.

The study reports fMRI cue-reactivity to visual food stimuli (food pictures vs baseline) and examines group-level voxelwise effects of genotype on that contrast. It meets I3 (visual natural reward cues: food pictures), I4 (analysis involves food cues>control/baseline within-participant contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise result with whole-brain inference and reported peak), and I6 (reported peak coordinate available). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported; MRI field strength/software are not but this is only preferred (I7 not required). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not only connectivity/resting-state (E4), and a qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast is present so E5 does not apply. Full text appears complete in the NeuroStore record. Therefore INCLUDE.

This fMRI study used visual heroin-related cues (24 heroin-related images vs 24 matched neutral images) in a block-design cue-reactivity task and reports within-subject contrasts (heroin-related > neutral) for early and late scan periods. Analyses were group-level voxelwise one-sample t-tests and paired t-tests with model fit over the whole brain and peak coordinates reported in tables, satisfying the requirement for task-evoked whole-brain voxelwise results. Thus it meets I3 (visual drug cues), I4 (within-participant drug>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), and I6 (results provided in tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts). Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual picture stimuli (Cue Reactivity Task: high-calorie food > control pictures). It reports a within-participant contrast (high-calorie food > control) and provides group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical results (longitudinal voxel-wise LME, whole-brain inference, FWE correction) with reported peak coordinates (Table tbl2). Results are presented in tables/figures as allowed. Participant demographics (n=30, BMI) and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7).

This fMRI study examines neural responses to erotic (natural reward) versus non-erotic visual cues using event-related visual stimuli (40 erotic and 40 non-erotic pictures). It reports within-participant contrasts (Erotic > Non-erotic) for both healthy and HSDD groups (analyses 0 and 1) and group-level voxelwise results with whole-brain inference and FWE correction (analytic reporting of peak coordinates in tables). The paper therefore meets the review’s requirement for visual cue-reactivity, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and provides qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results (reported peaks). Participant demographics and cue type are reported; missing MRI field strength/software does not preclude inclusion per criteria. fulltext_incomplete: false

This study used fMRI with visual drug cues (cocaine words in a Stroop task) and reports within-subject contrasts of cocaine words (CW) > neutral words (NW). NeuroStore indicates group-level voxelwise GLM analyses with whole-brain model fit and inference and reported peak coordinates (CW>NW and NW>CW peaks), satisfying a task-evoked voxelwise result. Although the paper also reports DCM effective connectivity, voxelwise whole-brain task results are present, so exclusion for connectivity-only analyses (E4) or ROI-only (E3) does not apply. Participant and cue details are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used explicit visual erotic stimuli (natural reward cues), so I3 is satisfied. However, the NeuroStore record reports only a seed-based psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity analysis (task-modulated functional connectivity) and a cross-subject regression with testosterone; no group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation contrast (e.g., within-participant EVES>control) is reported. The review’s inclusion criterion I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast) and I5 (a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result, whole-brain or SVC) are not met. Per exclusion criterion E4, studies that report only seed-based/effective connectivity analyses without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result must be excluded. Therefore EXCLUDED.

Exclusion: E5 met — the paper reports only between-group interaction contrasts (group x condition) comparing monetary vs neutral conditions across groups, without reporting a standalone within-participant cue>control (monetary>neutral) contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using clear visual monetary cues in the MID task), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported), and I6 (voxelwise peaks reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no explicit within-participant drug or natural reward cues > control within-subject contrast reported). Because E5 is satisfied, the study must be excluded.

The study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images (I3). The abstract and NeuroStore entries report contrasts comparing high- versus low-calorie food cues and pre- to post-surgery changes, and regressions linking neural changes to changes in wanting/liking, indicating within-participant task contrasts of food cues versus control/other-food cues (I4). Analyses were whole-brain voxelwise with reported peak coordinates and cluster correction (AlphaSim in AFNI), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (I5); NeuroStore notes whole-brain inference and tabulated peaks, acceptable per I6. Participant demographics and some preprocessing/statistics details are reported, though MRI field strength is not explicitly listed (I7 is partially met but not required). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

The study used a Cue Reactivity Task with visual natural reward cues (personally relevant high-calorie drinks) and a within-subject contrast of high-calorie taste cue > water. Analyses were group-level whole-brain voxelwise (model fit and inference over whole brain) with peaks reported in tables, satisfying the meta-analysis requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. Missing MRI field strength is noted but acceptable per inclusion guidance. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

The study examines natural reward (food) cues with visual food pictures and reports a group-level whole-brain voxelwise result (omnibus RFX ANOVA of cognitive control strategy). However the paper does not report a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (I4 not met). The available voxelwise result tests the main effect of regulation strategy (omnibus F) rather than a cue>control contrast (e.g., food > neutral or food > baseline) required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues present), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain result reported), I6 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Because the key within-subject cue>control contrast is not present in the provided document, the study must be excluded.

Excluded because the paper reports only between-group interaction contrasts and does not present any within-participant cue>control (natural-reward>control) contrasts required by I4. Exclusion criterion E5 applies. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task uses visual monetary reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results are reported for analyses 1–3), I6 (voxelwise peaks are reported in tables/figures), I7 (participant age/sex and other details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrasts are provided in the study document). Full text is complete in this record.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual food images (natural reward). It reports within-participant contrasts of high-calorie (reward) > neutral stimuli (High > neutral, within-group analyses in patients and group-level analyses) and other within-group contrasts (High > Utensil). Group-level voxelwise statistics were performed with whole-brain model fit and small-volume-corrected inference; peak coordinates are reported in tables. Participant demographics (age/sex), cue type, and contrasts are provided. MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not listed in this NeuroStore record, but the absence of those preferred details does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and includes qualifying within-participant cue>control contrasts).

The study examines natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images (high- vs low-calorie), meeting the review objective. It includes within-participant contrasts of food cues (HC > LC) reported as group-level voxelwise task-evoked results: two analyses report whole-brain FWE-corrected voxelwise results (AA genotype, HC>LC regressions), and one analysis reports small-volume FWE-corrected ROI results. Participant demographics (age, sex, BMI) and cue type are reported. Although MRI field strength and preprocessing details are not provided in this document, the absence of those does not preclude inclusion per the criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion.

The study examines visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards (food images) using fMRI (3T) and reports within-participant contrasts of interest (HiCal>Cars and LoCal>Cars) for both groups. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results were reported with small-volume correction within predefined ROIs (SVC in SPM2) and peaks are tabulated (Tables). Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength, and software are provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply: although analyses were ROI-based, qualifying SVC results are reported (so E3 does not exclude), and within-participant cue>control contrasts are present (so E5 does not apply). Full text appears complete in the provided record.

The study reports an fMRI within-participant contrast of positive (reward-related) visual images > neutral images (Look Positive > Look Neutral) using IAPS stimuli, which qualifies as natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component. The analysis was a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM with whole-brain cluster-level correction (FSL, z>2.3, cluster-level) and reported peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics and task details are reported. Although monetary reward was assessed behaviorally outside the scanner, the fMRI contrast uses positive social images as natural rewards, meeting the review objective. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This study used visual food cues in a within-subject crossover fMRI design and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction, but the only extracted within-participant contrast is high-calorie foods > low-calorie foods (reward vs less-reward). The inclusion criterion I4 requires at least one within-participant contrast of cues > control stimuli (e.g., natural reward-related cues > control stimuli such as objects). The NeuroStore record does not report a cue>control (food > non-food objects) voxelwise contrast—only high>low-calorie—so I4 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. Exclusion criteria met: none (listed [])." ,

This fMRI study uses visual food images (natural reward cues) in a cue-reactivity task and reports a within-participant contrast (High calorie > Low calorie). The analysis reports group-level voxelwise results with voxel-level FWE small-volume correction (SVC) using atlas-defined ROIs and reports peak coordinates (Table). Participant demographics and task details are provided. Although the model was fit within ROIs, the presence of SVC voxelwise inference satisfies the requirement for small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI results without SVC, connectivity-only analyses, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study assesses alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (30 alcohol-related and 30 neutral IAPS pictures) during task fMRI neurofeedback and rest. It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol-related pictures > neutral (within-group/session interaction contrasts) for patients and controls, satisfying a cue>control within-subject contrast. Multiple analyses are group-level voxelwise task-evoked results fit over the whole brain with reported peak coordinates/tables, meeting the whole-brain/small-volume-corrected requirement. Results are reported in tables of peaks. Some preferred descriptive details (e.g., participant age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not fully reported in the NeuroStore extract, but per criteria this does not exclude the study. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review objective and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used free viewing of an erotic movie (visual natural reward cues), so I3 is satisfied. However, analyses are ICA-derived intrinsic network (DMN, SN, FPN, VN) comparisons between patients and controls (multivariate, network-level thresholding) with no reported within-participant cue>control (e.g., erotic>neutral) task-evoked contrasts. The results are connectivity/ICA-based between-group effects rather than task-evoked voxelwise activation contrasts. Therefore the study meets exclusion criteria E4 (only ICA/resting-style connectivity reported without task-evoked voxelwise results) and E5 (reports only between-group contrasts without a within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5, I6, and I7 (MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistics not fully reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual food stimuli (natural rewards). The NeuroStore record reports within-participant contrasts of food>nonfood and high-calorie>low-calorie (within-group contrasts). Analyses were estimated and inferred over the whole brain with cluster-corrected voxelwise inference and reported peak coordinates (tables). Participant age/sex and cue type are reported. Although MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not listed, missing these details does not preclude inclusion per criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This study examines visual food (natural reward) cue reactivity in children and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (peaks reported). However, the NeuroStore record does not report any within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., food images > blurred/control images). The reported analyses focus on stimulus-type comparisons (high vs low calorie) and exercise-condition effects/interactions, not a reward-cue versus control contrast required by inclusion criterion I4. Therefore I4 is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues: food), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise inference), I6 (results reported as coordinates/peaks), I7 (participant demographics reported). No exclusion criteria from the list are explicitly met in the record. Exclusion is based on failure to meet I4 (required within-participant cue>control contrast).

This study reports an fMRI Monetary Incentive Delay task using clear visual cues (nine cue shapes) and provides group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical results reported as peak coordinates. It includes within-participant contrasts of natural reward cues versus control (e.g., reward > nonreward; gain > failure to win reward), satisfying the requirement for natural reward-related cue>control contrasts. Analyses were fit over the whole brain and report thresholded peaks/tables, meeting the whole-brain voxelwise result criterion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical human fMRI data). MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not reported in the NeuroStore extract (I7 not fully satisfied), but that absence does not preclude inclusion per the protocol. Hence the study should be included.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to visual food cues (30 healthy and 30 unhealthy images), meeting the review’s focus on natural reward-related cue-reactivity (I3). The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing unhealthy vs healthy food conditions (e.g., ‘Unhealthy food avoidance > Healthy food avoidance’ and other within-group contrasts/interactions), which provide within-subject cue-related contrasts suitable as natural reward > control (I4). Multiple task-evoked, group-level voxelwise whole-brain results are reported with FWE-corrected inference and peak coordinates in tables (model fit and inference over whole brain), satisfying the requirement for qualifying voxelwise results (I5) and allowance for tabulated coordinate reporting (I6). The study uses exclusively visual stimuli and reports task contrasts and whole-brain results; it therefore does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E5). Although some methodological details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not visible in this NeuroStore summary, missing these preferred items does not preclude inclusion per guidelines. Overall the study provides eligible whole-brain task-evoked contrasts of natural reward (food) cues using visual stimuli and is appropriate for inclusion.

This study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual food images (natural-reward cues) and a clear food > natural scenes contrast. A group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM was fit and inference conducted over the whole brain, with coordinates reported (Table T2) and cluster correction described (AlphaSim). The food > natural scenes contrast (within-participant cue vs control) is present and reported as voxelwise results, satisfying the requirement for a task-evoked, voxelwise group result. Participant demographics and cue type are reported; missing details (e.g., field strength/software) do not preclude inclusion per criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group-without-within-participant-contrast) apply based on the documented analyses. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for natural reward visual cue-reactivity and provides whole-brain coordinate results appropriate for the meta-analysis.

This study examines natural reward (food) cue-reactivity including visual food images and taste, reports within-participant contrasts of appetitive versus unappetitive food images predicting future weight gain (per abstract), and provides group-level voxelwise whole-brain inference (whole-brain thresholding reported; peaks/tables present). Participants and demographics are reported. Although some NeuroStore-extracted analyses focus on taste contrasts, the paper explicitly reports whole-brain image-based cue>control effects (coordinates/peaks), satisfying the visual-cue requirement and voxelwise reporting. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Confidence is slightly reduced because the NeuroStore extraction emphasizes taste contrasts and the image contrast appears only in the abstract/extracted text, but the available record clearly indicates qualifying voxelwise visual cue results.

This study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual images of palatable foods (natural rewards) vs neutral items (visual cue component). It includes a within-group contrast palatable > neutral, reported as a whole-brain voxelwise group-level analysis (model fit and inference over whole brain) with voxel-level FWE thresholding and reported peak coordinates. These features satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for natural reward visual cue-reactivity and a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result. Some preferred reporting details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software, full participant demographics beyond n=23) are not present in the NeuroStore extraction, but missing preferred details do not exclude the study. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study uses a Monetary Incentive Delay Task with visual reward/loss cues (I3 met). NeuroStore reports group-level voxelwise results with voxel-level FWE small-volume correction within atlas-defined ROIs (I5 met) and reports coordinate peaks (I6 met). Participant demographics and task details are reported (I7 met). However, the extracted analyses are exclusively group-level between-group contrasts (patients vs. controls; omnibus and pairwise group comparisons) and do not report any within-participant cue>control (e.g., reward cue > neutral) voxelwise contrasts in the provided document. Because no qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast is shown, this meets exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying within-participant cue>control result). Inclusion criteria not met: I4. Therefore the study is excluded.

Excluded because the paper does not report a qualifying within-participant task-evoked contrast for natural reward (monetary win) cues > control stimuli (I4 not met). The study does meet I3 (uses visual fractal cues and assesses cue-reactivity with monetary and shock cues), I5 (reports a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result with small-volume correction for shock CS values), and I6 (results are reported in a form acceptable for inclusion). However, the reported win-related effects are connectivity (PPI) analyses rather than task-evoked voxelwise activation/SVC for reward cues, and the only SVC task-evoked result is for shock (punishment). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., it does not report only connectivity or only ROI results). Inclusion IDs met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion IDs not met: I4. fulltext_incomplete=false

This study is excluded because it does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast required by I4. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual reward cues present — $100 bill image and cue stimuli), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported; model fit and inference over whole brain; coordinate peaks provided), I6 (voxelwise results are reported as coordinate tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug or natural reward-related cues > control stimuli is reported; extracted contrasts are Nicotine > Placebo and Placebo > Nicotine only). Although the design includes reward and expectation factors, the NeuroStore-extracted analyses list only drug-condition contrasts rather than cue>control contrasts, so the study does not provide the required cue-reactivity contrast for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study includes a visual monetary reward anticipation task (cues for monetary reward vs passive control), satisfying the visual cue requirement. It reports a group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrast for monetary>control with whole-brain inference (Analysis 7: whole-brain, FWE voxel-level, 27 reported peaks/table), which qualifies as a within-participant cue>control contrast aggregated at group level. Coordinate results/peaks are reported (tables), satisfying acceptable reporting formats. Participant demographics are provided. Therefore I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met; participant reporting satisfies I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group without a within-subject cue>control) apply based on the presence of whole-brain voxelwise monetary>control results. Inclusion is made with moderate-high confidence due to some labeling ambiguity of analyses as between-group in parts of the record, but the presence of a whole-brain monetary>control contrast and reported peaks supports eligibility.

This fMRI study used visual CSs (colored rectangles) paired with monetary reward (natural reward), meeting the cue modality requirement. It reports within-participant contrasts CS+>CS− during acquisition and extinction (within-group one-sample t-tests), satisfying the cue>control contrast requirement. Statistical results are group-level voxelwise models fit over the whole brain with inference using small-volume FWE correction (SVC), and peak coordinates/tables are reported, meeting the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. Participant demographics and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study does not report an explicit within-participant cue>control contrast required by I4. While it uses a visual monetary reward (card-guessing) task (satisfying I3) and provides group-level voxelwise models (model fit over whole brain) with reported peaks (satisfying I5 and I6) and reports participant demographics (I7), the NeuroStore record only describes associations with BOLD during 'reward anticipation' and 'reward outcome' across subjects without specifying a within-subject contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Because I4 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This study examines alcohol cue reactivity with visual alcohol taste cues (I3 met) and reports voxel peaks in tables (I6 met). However, the NeuroStore record shows only region-of-interest (ROI) voxelwise modeling (model fit over: region of interest; anatomically defined ROIs) and reports only between-group genotype × cue interaction contrasts (e.g., DRD4.L > Controls for alcohol taste > control taste). There is no presented within-participant cue>control contrast at the group level, nor clear whole-brain or explicit small-volume-corrected (SVC) group-level voxelwise results. Therefore exclusion criteria are met: E5 (only between-group/interaction contrasts without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast) and E3 (ROI-only reporting with no qualifying whole-brain or SVC result). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast not shown) and I5 (no clear whole-brain or SVC group-level voxelwise result).

The study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity task in alcohol-dependent participants including visual cue components (written CT/CCT statements and participant’s favorite alcoholic beverage), satisfying I3. The documented analyses include within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol-related cues to control stimuli (e.g., CT/alcohol, CCT/alcohol and alcohol>control contrasts are listed), satisfying I4. Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (model fit over: whole brain) with cluster correction and tables of peak coordinates, satisfying I5 and I6. Participant demographics (age, sex) and cue type are reported, meeting I7 (missing MRI field strength/software does not preclude inclusion). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and within-participant cue>control contrasts are present). Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of drug-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

The study examines natural reward (food) cue-reactivity with visual cues (meets I3). It reports group-level voxelwise results (whole-brain analyses 6–9 with reported peaks/tables) and region-level small-volume results (meets I5 and acceptable reporting per I6). Participant age/sex are reported (meets I7). However, the provided document does not report any clear within-participant contrast of reward-related cues > control (food cues > neutral object cues). Most contrasts probe reward-identity or identity-adaptation (e.g., comparisons among rewarding items or identity interactions), and some are explicitly restricted to rewarding food items rather than contrasting reward vs neutral. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Based on these facts I exclude the study.

The study examines natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual food pictures and reports voxelwise ROI results (FWE cluster-level within food cue-related ROIs). However, the only extracted statistical result is an oleoylethanolamide × obesity group interaction (a between-group interaction). No within-participant cue>control (food>neutral) voxelwise contrast is reported in the provided document. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrast/interaction without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Document details: Cue Reactivity Task with food pictures vs neutral IAPS; n=45; ROI inference; reported peaks=2; model included OEA×obesity and covariates.

This study examines natural reward (food) cues with clear visual components and includes within-participant cued>non-cued contrasts, but all reported analyses are ROI-restricted (model fit and inference restricted to regions of interest). No whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked result is reported. Therefore it fails the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward visual cue MRI), I4 (within-participant cued>non-cued contrast), I7 (participant age/sex reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain or SVC voxelwise task-evoked result). Full text appears complete for screening.

The study tests brain responses to erotic (natural reward) and other emotional visual stimuli using IAPS pictures and reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level results (model fit over whole brain, reported peak coordinates). Analysis 0 explicitly reports Emotional (including ERO) > Neutral contrasts with voxelwise GLM and reported peaks, which constitutes a within-participant cue>control contrast for natural reward cues. Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise statistics (tables of peaks), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics and cue type are reported. Although one analysis is labelled an interaction and NeuroStore notes some contrasts as between-group, the presence of the Emotional>Neutral voxelwise results and whole-brain peak tables meets inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or absence of within-participant cue>control contrasts) are met.

This study investigates neural responses to visual food cues (high- and low-calorie photographic images) and includes within-participant contrasts of natural reward-related cues > nonfood control (e.g., high-calorie > object; low-calorie > object). Crucially, it reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (Analyses 4–7: whole-brain inference, FDR-corrected), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected evidence. Participant demographics and cue types are reported. ROI analyses are also present but do not preclude inclusion because qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual images of food (natural reward), with within-group contrasts of low-calorie foods > control. Group-level voxelwise results were reported with voxel-level small-volume correction (SVC) in SPM99 and peak coordinates (tables), covering predefined ROIs (OFC, ACC, insula). These SVC-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results satisfy the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected evidence. Participant and task details are provided; missing MRI field strength does not preclude inclusion per criteria. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-evoked BOLD responses to visual food cues (natural reward) using a within-subject contrast (food > nonfood) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM) with inference across the whole brain. Peak coordinates are reported in a table. The cue stimuli are pictures (visual), task is cue-reactivity, and analyses directly test association between pre-surgical activation and subsequent BMI change. Required details (age, sex, task, software BrainVoyager) are provided; missing MRI field strength does not preclude inclusion (I7 allows missing elements). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrast). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food pictures (I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (Food-Go > Object-Go) (I4). It provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume-corrected inference (FWE SVC p<0.01) for the Food-Go > Object-Go contrast and related prednisolone interactions, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or SVC-corrected voxelwise results (I5). Results are reported in tables/peaks (Table tbl0005), satisfying I6, and participant demographics and stimulus details are provided (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, empirical fMRI data).

This fMRI study assesses natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using clear visual stimuli (sexually stimulating photographs vs neutral) and includes within-participant Sexual>Neutral contrasts (analyses 0 and 4). Analyses are group-level voxelwise one-sample t-tests with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference; significant peaks are reported in tables (coordinates), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. The record reports participant demographics and stimulus details. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it uses visual natural reward-related cues (snacks) in a Pavlovian-to-instrumental transfer task (I3); it reports a within-participant contrast of cue-related activation (CS+ parametric modulation / within-subject general PIT; analysis 32188908_analysis_2) consistent with a cue>control contrast (I4); it provides a group-level voxelwise second-level whole-brain task-evoked analysis with reported peak coordinates (I5, I6); participant demographics are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper includes a qualifying whole-brain voxelwise result (so not ROI-only), is not connectivity-only, and includes an appropriate within-subject cue>control analysis. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study assesses natural reward cue-reactivity (palatable food and monetary reward) using clear visual cues (images of milkshake; coin displays), and reports within-subject cue>control contrasts (e.g., Milkshake cue > tasteless solution cue; Winning cue > neutral cue). Analyses are group-level voxelwise results estimated and inferred over the whole brain with cluster-correction (Monte Carlo/3DClustSim) and reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics and task/cue details are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included.

The study examines neural responses to food (milkshake) cues using visual stimuli (images of milkshake vs tasteless solution), satisfying the review focus on natural reward cue-reactivity. It reports a within-participant contrast of unpaired milkshake cue > unpaired tasteless cue (within-group regression), meeting I4. The analysis was estimated voxelwise (model fit over whole brain) and inference used small-volume correction (FDR SVC) with reported peak coordinates (Table), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise or SVC results (I5) and allowing coordinate-table reporting (I6). The presence of visual cues (images) satisfies I3. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not an ROI-only study without voxelwise results (E3), not a connectivity/resting-state only study (E4), not between-group-only (E5), nor non-empirical (E6). Minor reporting inconsistencies (e.g., task labeled N-Back and an impossible sex count) are noted in the record but do not preclude that the necessary voxelwise cue>control contrast and SVC-corrected results are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6.

This fMRI study uses visual sexual stimuli (natural reward-related cues) and reports within-participant contrasts of couples (sexual) > neutral stimuli (Analysis 15004563_analysis_2), satisfying the cue>control requirement. The within-subject contrast is tested at the group level (one-group t-test, n=14 males) with inference restricted to anatomically defined regions (left/right amygdala, hypothalamus) and correction for multiple spatial comparisons within each region — qualifying as small-volume-corrected voxelwise evidence. The record includes whole-brain analyses as well (analyses 0 and 1), participant demographics (ages, sexes), and MNI coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met: the study does not report only ROI analyses without small-volume-corrected results (it does provide small-volume-corrected results), it includes task-evoked voxelwise results, and it is empirical human fMRI data. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual natural reward cue-reactivity.

This study reports an fMRI task with visual natural reward cues (food pictures) and a within-participant contrast (high-calorie food > non-food). The model was fitted voxelwise over the whole brain and thresholded with correction for multiple comparisons; peaks are reported (Table). These facts satisfy the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity, a within-subject cue>control contrast, and a qualifying whole-brain voxelwise result. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical task-evoked fMRI). Although the sample is small and some preprocessing/software details are not reported, that does not preclude inclusion per the stated criteria.

The study uses visual cues (colored squares) predicting monetary reward and reports within-participant contrasts comparing reward-predictive cue (Color A/old CS+) versus control/nonreward cue (Color B/new CS+), satisfying cue-reactivity contrast. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level GLM voxelwise results with thresholded clusters and reported peak coordinates/tables, meeting the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. The NeuroStore record shows coordinate tables and multiple contrasts directly relevant to reward cue>control. Participant demographics and cue type are reported; MRI field strength is not stated but this omission does not preclude inclusion per criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This fMRI study used visual sexual stimuli (photographs) that constitute natural reward cues and reports within-participant contrasts comparing sexual vs control conditions (e.g., Analysis 14: areas activated by visual sexual stimuli; fixed-effects group analysis). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported over the whole brain with coordinate tables and multiple reported foci (Tables tbl5, tbl2–tbl4), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected evidence. Results are presented in tables of coordinates, acceptable per I6. Participant demographic details and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study examines neural responses to visual sexual stimuli (a natural reward), satisfying relevance (I3). It reports within-participant analyses: paired t-tests/within-group interaction contrasts involving sexual versus neutral/positive/negative conditions (analyses 6–8 indicate within-subject paired tests), fulfilling the requirement for a within-participant cue>control contrast (I4). Group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction (FWE SVC) are reported for ROI anatomically defined (thresholding descriptions and reported peak tables), meeting the small-volume-corrected voxelwise evidence requirement (I5). Peaks are reported in tables (I6). Although models were fit within ROIs, SVC voxelwise results are provided, and coordinate tables are present. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Detailed participant sex and contrasts are reported; some secondary metadata (e.g., field strength/software) may be missing but do not preclude inclusion.

The study reports an event-related fMRI experiment with a within-subject reward vs no-reward manipulation using visual cues (monetary reward), and contains group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (corrected, p<0.05) with tables of peak coordinates for main effect of reward. This satisfies the review objective (natural reward cue reactivity to visual stimuli) and meets inclusion requirements: within-participant reward>no-reward contrast, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results, and reporting of results in tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Participant demographics and cue type are reported. MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not specified in the NeuroStore extract, but their absence does not exclude the study per I7. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) voxelwise analyses (model fit and inference restricted to atlas-defined mesolimbic/corticolimbic ROIs) with no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise results, so it fails the requirement for at least one qualifying whole-brain/SVC result. It does include a visual cue component (colored square cues) satisfying I3. However, the task uses monetary rewards (Monetary Incentive Delay) rather than drug or clearly natural rewards (e.g., food), so it does not clearly meet I4 for natural reward cue-reactivity. Therefore exclusion is based on E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria applied: E3.

The study does not meet the review's cue-reactivity inclusion criteria and reports only ROI-based, between-group results. NeuroStore indicates all analyses were model fit over region-of-interest (ROI) masks and inference was restricted to pairwise group comparisons (no within-participant cue>control contrasts). The task is a monetary incentive delay task examining operant response outcomes (between-group contrasts of smokers/ex-smokers vs controls), not within-participant drug or natural reward cue>control reactivity. Therefore it violates E3 (ROI-only, no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results) and E5 (reports only between-group contrasts without a within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not assess drug or natural reward cue-reactivity as defined), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain or SVC result). Full text is complete for screening. Excluding on these grounds.

This study reports a cue-reactivity fMRI contrast of visual food>nonfood (within-participant) using images of food and neutral objects, and provides participant demographics. However, the statistical model was fit and inference were restricted to predefined regions of interest (ROI); thresholding was region-level/Bonferroni and no whole-brain voxelwise or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results are reported. Thus it fails the requirement for at least one qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level result. Exclusion applied: E3 (ROI-only results). Inclusion met: I3 (visual natural reward cue-reactivity), I4 (within-participant food>control contrast), I7 (participant details reported). Inclusion not met: I5 (no whole-brain or SVC voxelwise result).

The study used fMRI monetary incentive delay task with explicit monetary incentive cues (visual) and reports within-participant cue>neutral contrasts (anticipation of gain/loss > neutral) as well as group and within-group (pre/post) contrasts. Results are reported as voxelwise small-volume-corrected (FWE SVC) analyses in ventral striatum (coordinate peaks/tables provided). Thus it satisfies I3 (visual monetary reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise small-volume-corrected results), and I6 (results reported in tables/peaks). Participant demographics are reported (I7 also satisfied). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only without SVC, not connectivity-only, etc.).

The study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity task comparing beer versus water with explicit visual word cues signaling delivery (abstract) and task stimuli are visual, satisfying I3. It reports within-participant contrasts of beer>water (analyses labelled anticipation/notification/tasting beer > water) and one-sample/GLM models consistent with voxelwise task-evoked contrasts, satisfying I4. Model fit and inference were conducted over the whole brain with reported peak coordinates, satisfying I5 and I6 (voxelwise whole-brain results reported as peaks). Participant information (sex, drinking assessments) and cue type are reported, though some metadata in the NeuroStore record conflict (e.g., task labelled as MID, participant n=150 vs abstract n=21). These inconsistencies reduce certainty but do not negate that qualifying within-subject whole-brain cue>control results are present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts) are met. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion.

The study uses visual food cues and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE, peak-level), but the only extracted task contrast is a group-by-condition interaction (between-group contrast: food>non-food interaction between insulin-resistant vs normal). No within-participant food>non-food (cue>control) contrast is reported in the provided document. Per criteria, this means the paper reports only between-group/interaction results without an accompanying within-subject cue>control voxelwise contrast, so it must be excluded (E5). Included criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked result), I6 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete in this record.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to visually presented palatable food cues (food pictures) versus non-food control images, meeting the review’s focus on visual natural-reward cue-reactivity. It reports a within-participant contrast (viewing foods > viewing non-foods) and group-level voxelwise model estimates (model fit over whole brain) with inference via small-volume correction (SVC) and peak coordinates reported in tables. Participant demographics (age, sex) and cue type are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical fMRI data).

This fMRI study used a Monetary Incentive Delay task with explicit incentive cues (visual cues indicating gain/loss/neutral), meeting the visual-cue requirement and qualifying as natural reward (monetary) cue-reactivity. It reports within-participant contrasts of reward>neutral and loss>neutral (Analyses 2–5). At least one qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result is provided: the within-group contrasts were tested whole-brain with voxelwise FDR thresholding and reported peak coordinates. Results are available in tables (peaks) and participant demographics (age/sex) are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears available in the provided NeuroStore record.

This study investigates neural responses to visual social and monetary reward cues (photographs of smiling persons and 1€ coins), meeting the visual cue requirement. It reports within-participant contrasts of reward cues > neutral cues (anticipation and feedback contrasts), satisfying the cue>control contrast requirement. At least one qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result is reported with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference (Analysis 25944965_analysis_0), fulfilling the whole-brain/SVC requirement. Coordinate space (MNI) and reported peaks are present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes within-subject cue>control contrasts; not connectivity-only). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI drug/natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

The study uses visual smoking cues (meets I3) but all reported analyses were ROI-based (Model fit over: region of interest; thresholding: region-level). No whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level task-evoked results are reported, violating I5 and matching exclusion E3. Also, although a Drug>Neutral contrast is listed, the NeuroStore extraction indicates inference was restricted to pairwise group comparisons and model fit over ROIs, so a qualifying within-participant voxelwise drug>control contrast is not evident (I4 not met). Therefore exclude under E3.

This fMRI study examines monetary reward anticipation using clear visual cues (circle/triangle cues and coin pictures) in a within-subject, double-blind crossover design. It reports a within-participant contrast of reward cues > no-reward cues (Analysis 21484950_analysis_0), estimated as a whole-brain voxelwise GLM (one-sample t-test) with peaks reported in a table, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics (n=16, ages reported, sex reported) are provided. Although the paper also reports seed-based connectivity analyses, it additionally provides a qualifying task-evoked whole-brain contrast, so no exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the study meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study reports resting-state (Rest Task, continuous) binarized degree centrality group differences (patients vs controls) and no task-evoked cue-reactivity paradigm or visual cues. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only resting-state analysis without any qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result) and E5 (reports only between-group contrasts without a within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant age/sex were reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no visual cue component / not a cue-reactivity task), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical result), I6 (not applicable because no task-evoked contrasts are reported). Full text appears complete for extraction. Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis of fMRI visual cue-reactivity for drug/natural rewards.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to sexual (natural reward) visual cues and includes within-participant contrasts of sexual > control (e.g., sexual > negative in a men-only within-group analysis). Group-level voxelwise results were reported using small-volume correction (FWE SVC) with coordinate peaks and tables, satisfying the requirement for a voxelwise small-volume-corrected task-evoked result. Visual stimuli were clearly used (picture viewing task).
