This study investigates monetary (natural) reward anticipation using visual cues (shape cues) in an fMRI Monetary Incentive Delay task, and reports whole-brain voxelwise results; however, NeuroStore-extracted analyses do not include any within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., reward-cue > neutral-cue). Extracted analyses are interactions/parametric modulations (valence x salience; expected value x salience) rather than a simple cue>control contrast required by inclusion criterion I4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (functional MRI of natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked result reported), I6 (voxelwise peaks reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast extracted). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Based on the provided document, the study should be excluded for failing to meet I4.

The study uses visual erotic vs neutral video cues (I3 satisfied) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results with FDR correction (I5 satisfied); NeuroStore extraction indicates voxelwise results are available in tables (I6 satisfied). However, all reported contrasts are treatment-by-condition interaction contrasts comparing erotic>neutral across drugs (e.g., Placebo>Paroxetine, Bupropion>Placebo), i.e., between-treatment interactions, and no simple within-participant cue>control (erotic>neutral) contrast for a single treatment is reported in the extracted analyses. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

The study examines natural reward-related (cola) cue-reactivity using visual cues (pictures of logos/bottles). It reports within-participant contrasts comparing strong vs weak brand cues (e.g., Coca/Pepsi > River/T-Cola; Coca Cola > Pepsi Cola), which serve as natural reward-related cue>control contrasts. Group-level, voxelwise task-evoked results were estimated over the whole brain (model fit over: whole brain) with reported peaks and MNI coordinates and cluster-level thresholding—satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise evidence. The paper is empirical fMRI (task-based) and does not rely solely on ROI, connectivity-only, or between-group contrasts. Some methodological details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not reported in the NeuroStore extract, but I7 is preferred rather than mandatory. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This fMRI study uses visual erotic stimuli (videos and still images) contrasted against control (sport) stimuli, meeting the review focus on natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity. It reports within-subject contrasts of erotic>control (analyses 15961048_analysis_0 and _2) and additional parametric/regression results linked to penile turgidity. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and peaks are reported in tables (Talairach coordinates), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked statistical results. Participant demographics (age, sex, health) and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

The study used a Monetary Incentive Delay task with visual cues (gain vs. neutral), providing within-participant contrasts of natural reward-related cues (gain cues > neutral) for cue anticipation and feedback. Group-level voxelwise results were reported with small-volume familywise error correction (SVC) within anatomically defined ROIs (ventral striatum, mPFC) and peak coordinates are listed (3 peaks per analysis), satisfying the requirement for small-volume-corrected voxelwise evidence. Participant demographics (age, sex) and cue type are reported; MRI field strength and preprocessing software are not listed but that missing information alone does not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria are met (not restricted to ROI-only analyses without SVC; not connectivity/resting-state only; includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study reports an event-related fMRI Reward Processing Task using visual symbols indicating possible monetary wins (visual cue component). It includes within-participant paired t-test contrasts of natural reward-related cues versus control (expectation high > no reward; high > low; win > omission), satisfying a cue>control within-subject contrast. Analyses were estimated over the whole brain with group-level random-effects models and report peak coordinates (tables), fulfilling the requirement for a voxelwise whole-brain result (or small-volume-corrected) and allowing coordinate-based extraction. Participant age and sex, cue type, and task details are reported; MRI field strength/software are not listed but these are preferred, not mandatory. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, empirical fMRI task data present). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7.

This study reports only ROI-based, cross-subject correlations between BOLD response and free testosterone during viewing of erotic (visual) stimuli in postoperative FtM transsexuals. It does not present a within-participant contrast of reward cues > control stimuli, nor any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. Exclusion criterion met: E3 (only ROI analyses reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural-reward erotic cues present), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, and MRI field strength reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5/I6 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or SVC results reported). Therefore the study is excluded.

Study uses visual food cues (pictures of previously tasted functional and standard foods) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrasts comparing food conditions (first-level food-condition contrasts entered into second-level SPM models). Whole-brain inference reported with coordinate peaks (AlphaSim cluster correction; peaks in tables), satisfying the requirement for a group-level voxelwise result. Although contrasts compare two types of food rather than food vs neutral, this constitutes a within-participant natural reward-related cue contrast (functional vs standard foods) relevant to visual reward cue-reactivity. Seed-based connectivity analyses are also reported but do not preclude inclusion because qualifying task-evoked whole-brain results are present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts without a within-subject cue contrast) are met.

The study reports fMRI responses to visual erotic films (natural reward cues), satisfying the review’s cue modality requirement. It includes within-participant contrasts of sexual-cue > rest (M-M > rest in homosexual group; F-M > rest in heterosexual group), meeting the within-subject cue>control criterion. Analyses are group-level, random-effects, voxelwise, whole-brain models with reported peak coordinates (voxelwise thresholding reported), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Peaks are reported (coordinates), which is acceptable. Participant demographics (age, sex) and task/stimulus details are provided. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-participant contrasts). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual natural reward cue-reactivity.

The study reports an event-related monetary (natural reward) task with clear visual cues (numbers and colored feedback). It includes a within-participant contrast of monetary gains > losses (reward-related cues > control) and provides group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical results (FWE-corrected voxel-level peaks and coordinates) reported in tables. Participant demographics (n, sex, abstinence) are provided. These facts satisfy inclusion criteria for visual reward cue-reactivity (I3), a within-participant cue>control contrast (I4), and voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (I5); reporting in tables meets I6, and participant details satisfy I7. The study does not report ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical results, so no exclusion criteria apply. Note: NeuroStore shows a ‘between-group’ tag for the contrast, but the reported model and contrast indicate a within-subject reward>control contrast was tested and reported at the group level.

The study examines neural responses to visual food cues (food photographs) in overweight adolescent girls and reports within-subject contrasts comparing food vs. nonfood stimuli across breakfast conditions. Analyses report voxelwise peak coordinates (tables) from ROI-based voxelwise inference (model fit and inference restricted to predefined ROIs) with cluster-level correction, which constitutes small-volume-corrected, group-level task-evoked results. Thus it meets the review objective for natural reward (food) cue-reactivity with visual stimuli and satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. Participant and task details are reported (I7 information preferred but not required). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only without SVC, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). The interaction contrasts compare food>nonfood across conditions but are derived from within-participant cue>control effects, so they qualify for inclusion.

This study meets the meta-analysis objectives and inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI task using visual natural reward (food) cues (I3). It reports a within-participant contrast of high-calorie > low-calorie foods (a natural reward-related cue contrast) within groups (I4). The reported results are group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistics with small-volume correction (FWE SVC) within anatomically defined ROIs and peak coordinate tables (I5, I6). Participant demographics (age/sex) and cue type are reported; MRI field strength/software are not listed but these are preferred, not required (I7 not fully reported). No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI analyses without SVC (E3), is not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), includes within-participant cue>control contrasts (not solely between-group) (E5), and is empirical human fMRI data (not E6). Therefore INCLUDE.

The study uses a Monetary Incentive Delay task with explicit visual cues (green/red/blue squares; star), so it meets I3. NeuroStore reports group-level ROI voxelwise results with FWE cluster correction and reported peak coordinates, satisfying I5 and I6. However, the extracted analyses are only between-group contrasts (combined smokers/ex-smokers > controls) for gain and loss anticipation; the document does not report any within-participant cue>control contrasts (e.g., gain>neutral) at the group level. Therefore it fails I4, and exclusion criterion E5 applies (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete in this record.

This study examines neural responses to visually presented reward cues (card-guessing task with visually presented cards) and reports within-participant task contrasts of reward anticipation/outcome > baseline (analyses 7–10), satisfying the cue>control within-subject requirement. It provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked results both whole-brain (analyses 7–10) and ROI-corrected results (analyses 0–6), with reported coordinate peaks and thresholding, meeting the whole-brain / small-volume-corrected reporting requirement. Visual cue component is explicit. Although some preferred metadata (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not listed in the NeuroStore extract, missing these does not exclude the study. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

The study tests visual alcohol-related cues (15 alcohol pictures vs 15 neutral IAPS pictures) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Analysis 22868938_analysis_0 reports a whole-brain, voxel-level FWE-corrected contrast involving alcohol-associated stimuli > neutral stimuli (interaction of cue>control by group), which constitutes a qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked cue>control result. Additional analyses include small-volume-corrected task-evoked and PPI connectivity results, but the presence of the whole-brain task-evoked result satisfies the requirement for voxelwise reporting. Participant and task details reported. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI, only-connectivity, or only between-group-without-cue contrasts) prevent inclusion. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity.

Exclusion because the study does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast required by I4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward-related visual cues: erotic video clips), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported with corrected voxelwise thresholds), I6 (voxelwise results reported in tables/peaks). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant contrast of sexual cues > control stimuli is reported; analyses are parametric correlational mappings between plethysmographic signal and BOLD rather than a direct cue>control contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

The study reports fMRI reward anticipation using visual cues (grayscale pictures predicting monetary reward), satisfying visual cue requirement. It includes within-participant contrasts of reward-predicting > non-reward-predicting and rewarded > neutral cues (within-group contrasts). Group-level voxelwise analyses were fit over the whole brain with voxel-level thresholding and tables of Talairach coordinates reported, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (coordinates in tables). Participant age/sex are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This study used fMRI with explicit erotic video stimuli (visual cues) and performed within-subject block contrasts between sexually arousing and non-arousing video clips (as stated in the abstract) and a parametric within-group regression with penile turgidity. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise results are reported (Talairach coordinates; cluster-size correction and whole-brain inference are described). Peaks are reported in tables. Therefore it satisfies: I3 (visual natural-reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts performed), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables), and I7 (participant details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears available via the NeuroStore extraction, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports visual cue-reactivity to exercise and sedentary images (visual stimuli) and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts (exercise>landscape; sedentary>landscape) at the group level. At least one qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result is reported whole-brain with voxelwise FDR correction (Analyses 24366575_analysis_0 and _1) and coordinates are provided in tables, satisfying the requirement that results be reported as whole-brain voxelwise statistics or in tables. The document provides participant age/sex and cue type; MRI field strength and preprocessing details are not reported in this record but their absence does not preclude inclusion per I7. No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts without within-participant cue>control contrasts) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This study does not assess visual cue-reactivity: the task involves TMS pulses and instructions to recall/imagery of recent drug/alcohol experiences rather than presentation of visual cue stimuli, so I3 is not met. It also does not report any within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli or natural reward-cues > control (no cue>control contrasts are presented), so I4 is not met. The study does meet I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported; whole-brain model fit and peak tables are provided) and I6 (results reported in tables of coordinates). I7 (preferred reporting of age/sex etc.) is partially reported but not essential. No exclusion criteria from E3, E4, E5, or E6 strictly apply. Therefore the paper is excluded because it fails required inclusion criteria I3 and I4.

This study uses a Monetary Incentive Delay Task with visual monetary cues (win/lose stimuli), so it meets I3 (natural reward-related visual cues). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with coordinates/tables (model fit over whole brain; reported peaks), satisfying I5 and I6. However, the NeuroStore record shows only between-group contrasts (BEpost-tx vs NBEpost-tx) and does not report any within-participant cue>control contrasts (e.g., reward-cue > neutral/control) required by I4. Because no qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast is provided, exclusion criterion E5 applies (studies reporting only between-group contrasts without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion IDs met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion ID not met: I4. Exclusion applied: E5.

The study examines natural rewards (money and social approval) using clear visual cues (cue symbols and facial expressions), and reports voxelwise small-volume-corrected (SVC) group-level results; however, the NeuroStore extraction shows only between-group interaction contrasts (men>women, women>men) reported at the voxel level. There is no reported within-participant cue>control (or reward>neutral) voxelwise contrast in the extracted analyses; the only within-subject-like analysis is a region-of-interest (right NAcc) ROI analysis. Therefore the study lacks the required within-participant cue>control voxelwise result and meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without a qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward cue-reactivity with visual cues), I5 (at least one group-level voxelwise result via SVC), I6 (coordinate reporting acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast).

This fMRI study uses visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level task contrasts (food>baseline) presented in tables, so it satisfies I3, I5, and I6. However, all reported statistical results in the NeuroStore record are between-group interaction contrasts comparing genetic subtypes (DEL vs UPD) for Food>Baseline; the record does not present a within-participant cue>control (e.g., food>baseline) contrast for a single group. Because the paper reports only between-group/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast, it violates exclusion criterion E5 and fails inclusion criterion I4. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study examines visual food cue reactivity (high- vs low-caloric food and non-food pictures) and reports within-participant contrasts (food>non-food), so it meets I3 and I4, and reports voxel peaks in a table (I6). However, the reported voxelwise whole-brain result (Analysis 2) is from a single participant using a fixed-effect single-arm design (n=1). Inclusion criterion I5 requires at least one qualifying analysis to be a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result (whole-brain or SVC). Because all analyses are single-subject/fixed-effect (not group-level), the study does not satisfy I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) strictly apply, but failure to meet I5 mandates exclusion. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (group-level voxelwise result). Full text is complete as provided.

The study is excluded because it does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast (required I4). The reported analyses are parametric modulations of valence/willingness ratings during presentation of food pictures, not explicit food>neutral or cue>control contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward-related visual cues — food pictures), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results reported with peak coordinates), I6 (results reported in tables/coordinates acceptable). I7 (reporting of participant age/sex and cue type present; MRI field strength/software not reported) is not required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria (I4 missing) and is excluded.

This study reports only resting-state, seed-based functional connectivity analyses (ACC-seeded rsFC) with no task or cue presentation (task listed as Rest, eyes closed). It therefore does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual cues (I3 not met), contains no within-participant cue>control task contrast (I4 not met), and provides no task-evoked voxelwise results (I5/I6 not met). It also does not fully satisfy reporting preferences in I7 (some participant info present but cue type/MRI field strength/preprocessing details are not reported). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only seed-based/resting-state analyses with no qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result).

This fMRI study uses visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports voxelwise small-volume-corrected results (reported peaks), but it does not include a within-participant contrast of reward cues > control stimuli (e.g., food images > neutral/control images). Included criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise SVC results), I6 (coordinate table peaks reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported); I7 (MRI field-strength and preprocessing/statistical software not reported). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I4.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 and E5. The NeuroStore record reports only resting-state rs-fMRI analyses (global connectedness) and a between-group interaction (STIM vs SHAM) of change from Day 1 to Day 2, with no task-evoked cue-reactivity results. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant age/sex reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no clear visual cue component — cues are Pavlovian cues linked to food odors, not clearly visual), I4 (no within-participant cue>control task contrast for drug or natural reward cues), I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked result; only resting-state voxelwise maps). Therefore the study does not meet the review requirement for task-evoked visual cue-reactivity and must be excluded.

The NeuroStore record does not provide a within-participant cue>control voxelwise contrast for natural reward stimuli (e.g., sexual>neutral or infant>neutral). The only extracted voxelwise group analysis is 'negative > fixation' (whole-brain, FDR-corrected), which does not qualify as a natural reward cue>control contrast. Although the abstract describes VTA increases to crying infant and sexual images after oxytocin, no qualifying voxelwise cue>control result (whole-brain or SVC) for those stimulus types is presented in the provided document. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues present) and I5 (group-level voxelwise result reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no qualifying cue>control contrast reported); I6 (no clear indication in this document that qualifying voxelwise cue>control results are available in tables/figures/supplementary). No exclusion criteria were triggered.

The study uses visual erotic IAPS pictures (natural reward-related cues) and reports within-participant contrasts including erotic pictures versus baseline and parametric within-group contrasts comparing erotic vs non-erotic self-relatedness. Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (voxel-level threshold p<0.001, cluster extent 10) with peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. It is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports fMRI cue-reactivity to natural rewards (palatable food images) using a visual task and within-subject contrasts (palatable foods > neutral items). NeuroStore shows group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with FWE thresholding and reported peak coordinates (Tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. Results are reported in tables of coordinates. While some preferred metadata (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not shown in this record, missing those details alone does not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore the paper meets inclusion I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This study examines neural responses to sweet taste with visual predictive cues (meets I3). It reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume FWE correction (meets I5) and publishes coordinate tables/peaks (meets I6). Participant age and sex and cue type are reported (meets I7). However, all reported inferential results in the NeuroStore record are between-group contrasts/interactions (obese-resistant vs obese-prone; males vs females) or cross-subject regressions; no qualifying within-participant cue>control (SU>AS) main effect at the group level is reported. Therefore the study reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control group-level result, meeting exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criterion I4 (a within-participant cue>control analysis) is not met. Full text is available in the record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study reports fMRI cue-reactivity to a natural reward (food) using visual stimuli (pictures) and within-participant contrasts (appetizing food > unappetizing food; appetizing food > water). Analyses were estimated over the whole brain and reported voxelwise peak coordinates (tables), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics (age, sex, BMI) and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3–I7 and can be included.

The study reports only ROI-based voxelwise results (striatum ROI; model fit and inference restricted to ROI) and does not report any whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level results. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3. The task uses visual reward cues (card-guessing monetary rewards), and reported contrasts are within-subject reward>baseline (satisfying I3 and I4), but the absence of whole-brain or SVC voxelwise results prevents inclusion.

Excluded (E5): The report presents a between-group interaction (Group*CRP) of coupling between BOLD and pleasantness ratings and does not report a within-participant natural-reward cue > control-stimulus contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward visual cues — food pictures), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked model with inference restricted to an ROI — small-volume-corrected), I6 (voxelwise results reported in table/peaks), I7 (participant age/sex and some preprocessing/statistical software reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported). Therefore E5 applies and the study must be excluded.

Excluded because this study reports only region-of-interest voxelwise results and only between-group interaction contrasts rather than a within-participant cue>control contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (only ROI analyses reported) and E5 (only between-group/interaction contrasts reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task includes clear visual cue components) and I7 (participant age/sex and some sample details reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (no within-participant drug- or natural-reward cue>control contrast reported), I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise result), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results available in tables/figures). fulltext_incomplete=false

The study uses visual natural reward cues (erotic images) and reports within-subject contrasts comparing erotic vs. control (romantic) images and positive vs. neutral conditions. Analyses are group-level voxelwise results with whole-brain inference (FDR-corrected p<0.05) and coordinates reported in tables. Participant demographics (age/sex) are provided. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria.

This record reports an fMRI study of monetary (natural) reward with clear visual cues (I3 satisfied) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level inference (I5 satisfied). However, the NeuroStore extraction only lists a between-group interaction contrast (Risk > HC for anticipation of reward) and does not provide any within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., reward-cue > neutral-cue) at the voxelwise group level. Therefore the study appears to report only between-group analyses without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast, which meets exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5 (also I6 and I7 are effectively satisfied: voxelwise results reported and participant age/sex and cue type provided). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported). Conclusion: EXCLUDE under E5.

The study uses the Monetary Incentive Delay Task (monetary reward/loss) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (peaks in tables), but the reported analyses are longitudinal/time contrasts (posttreatment>pretreatment, Scan1>Scan2) and a group-by-time interaction. No within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., reward-cue > neutral/control) is reported in the provided document. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I4 requiring at least one within-participant cue>control contrast. I3, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied (natural reward task, whole-brain voxelwise results, coordinate table reporting, participant details reported). As I4 is not met, the study must be excluded from the cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

This fMRI study tests visual heroin-related cues (I3) and includes within-participant contrasts heroin>neutral (I4). Voxelwise results are reported as peaks/tables (I6). However, all reported analyses are modelled and tested only within predefined regions of interest ("Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest") with no indication of whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise inference. Therefore it meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only reporting with no qualifying whole-brain or SVC result). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain or explicit small-volume-corrected evidence); I7 not fully met (MRI field strength not reported). Full text is complete in this record.

This fMRI study used visual sexual stimuli (photographs of male and female genitals) as natural reward cues and includes within-participant contrasts of sexual stimuli > nonsexual control stimuli. Analyses were reported as group-level voxelwise results with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference (FWE cluster-level thresholding) and coordinate peaks/tables are provided. Participant age and sex and cue type are reported. These features satisfy inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), and I6 (results reported in tables/peaks). MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software are not reported in the extracted record, so I7 is not fully satisfied, but that alone does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical task-evoked data present).

The study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli, reporting within-participant contrasts of food>object and HD>LD. It includes group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain inference (Analysis 30205209_analysis_2: Food>OBJ, whole-brain FWE-corrected) and a small-volume-corrected HD>LD result (Analysis 30205209_analysis_6). Participant demographics are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, empirical task-evoked data present).

The paper reports only between-group interaction contrasts (obese high-ED > lean low-ED) and no within-participant cue>control (e.g., high-ED > control) voxelwise contrasts required by the review. Exclusion E5 applies. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (clear visual cue component present), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I6 (voxelwise results reported in tables/peaks), I7 (participant demographics reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported). Full text is complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images vs blurred/animal controls). It reports within-participant contrasts of Food > Non-food (multiple analyses) and stimulus × motivational state interactions. Results are whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps with corrected whole-brain thresholding and coordinates reported in tables. Although the analysis used a fixed-effects model and the sample is small (n=9), the inclusion criteria require a whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group result and do not exclude fixed-effects per se. Some preferred methodological details (MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not reported, but I7 is advisory and their absence does not preclude inclusion. Therefore the study meets the review criteria for inclusion.

The study examines visual food cues (natural rewards) but reports only ROI-based, between-group interaction contrasts rather than within-participant cue>control voxelwise results. NeuroStore shows model fit and inference restricted to anatomically defined ROIs (hypothalamus, amygdala, anterior insula), and the two extracted analyses are described as interaction/between-group contrasts (e.g., HC high-calorie > ANWR objects [interaction, between-group]; AN high-calorie > ANWR objects [interaction, between-group]). No group-level whole-brain or small-volume-corrected within-participant cue>control contrast is reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E3 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain/SVC result) and E5 (reports only between-group/interaction contrasts without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criterion I3 (visual natural reward cues) is met; inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using visual cues (colored photographs) that predict monetary reward vs neutral outcomes, with within-subject contrasts (reward-predicting > neutral). Analyses were estimated over the whole brain (model fit over: whole brain) with voxelwise inference and reported peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant age and sex are reported. Therefore the paper meets the review’s criteria for natural reward-related (monetary) cue-reactivity with visual cues and whole-brain voxelwise reporting. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study uses visual natural reward cues (photographs of unhealthy snacks) so I3 is satisfied. However, it does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., food cues > control stimuli); the reported craving-related contrast is self-control > control condition, which reflects regulation versus control strategy rather than cue-reactivity, so I4 is not met. Although ROI small-volume-corrected task results are reported for the self-control contrast, there is no qualifying voxelwise (whole-brain or SVC) result for a cue>control contrast, so I5 (as applied to the required cue-reactivity contrast) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I4 (and consequently I5 for the required cue>control analysis).

This study reports only seed-based psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity analyses (Left and Right NAcc seeds) and a between-group interaction contrast (family-history by valence). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (monetary reward cues in the MID provide a natural reward visual cue component) and I7 (participant age/sex and task details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast is reported for task-evoked activation) and I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation results reported; only connectivity parameters are reported). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only seed-based/effective connectivity reported without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result) and E5 (results are reported as a between-group interaction rather than a within-participant cue>control contrast). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Study tests visual cue-reactivity to food (natural reward) using an explicit Cue Reactivity Task with food and non-food photographs and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (peaks in MNI coordinates) using small-volume correction within a priori frontal/parietal ROIs. Analyses explicitly model condition (food vs non-food blocks) and report within-group (cross-subject) regressions correlating food-processing activation with behavior (e.g., set-shifting, anxiety) and list peak coordinates (SVC thresholding). Participant demographics and task/cue details are reported. Thus the paper meets: I3 (fMRI of natural reward visual cues), I4 (within-participant analyses of food cue processing/condition), I5 (group-level voxelwise results with SVC), I6 (coordinates/peaks reported), and I7 (demographics and cue details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. No evidence the fulltext is unreadable; fulltext_incomplete=false.

This paper reports a task-evoked fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (food images) and includes within-participant contrasts of food cues > non-food control stimuli (food choices vs non-food choices). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (one-sample t-tests) with whole-brain model fitting and reported peak coordinates (table), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. Visual cue component, coordinate reporting, and participant demographics are provided. Although MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not listed in this record, I7 deems missing such details acceptable. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study uses visual natural reward cues (erotic pictures) and reports within-participant contrasts of reward>control (Analysis 20881127_analysis_5 lists MR; ER > C), satisfying cue>control contrast requirement. Multiple analyses are group-level voxelwise whole-brain second-level GLM results with voxelwise FWE inference and reported peaks, meeting the whole-brain/small-volume requirement. Visual cue component is explicit (erotic pictures, monetary images, pictogram cues). Participant demographics are reported (age, sex), and coordinate tables/peaks are available. Missing details (e.g., MRI field strength) do not preclude inclusion per I7. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity with visual natural rewards and reports qualifying voxelwise results.

The study uses visual sexual penetration stimuli (natural reward-related cues) and reports within-participant contrasts of penetration > control (PEN > BOD and related contrasts). Analyses were whole-brain voxelwise with FWE voxel-level inference and reported peak coordinates in tables, satisfying requirements for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported in tables of coordinates). MRI field strength and preprocessing software are not reported (I7 not fully satisfied, but this is a preferred detail only). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record.

This study is excluded because it reports resting-state seed-based functional connectivity (VTA seed) during a fixation/rest paradigm, not a task-based visual cue-reactivity experiment. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only seed-based connectivity/resting-state analyses without any qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not assess drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual cues), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (no task-evoked group-level voxelwise result; connectivity maps are resting-state seed-based, not task-evoked). Full text appears complete in the record; exclusion is based on study content.

The study uses fMRI with clear visual snack cues (I3) and reports group-level voxelwise results both whole-brain (Analysis 0, FWE) and small-volume-corrected results (Analyses 1–2), satisfying I5, I6 and I7 (demographics and task details reported). However, it does not include a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (e.g., snack images versus neutral/control images). All reported contrasts compare regulation strategies (positive/negative) to a 'now' craving condition or use multivariate decoding between strategies, not a cue>control contrast, so it fails inclusion criterion I4. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are specifically met, but per review rules any missing inclusion criterion requires exclusion.

This study does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast required by the review (I4 not met). The available analysis contrasts up-regulation versus passive viewing (a regulation vs passive condition) using appetitive food pictures, but no contrast of natural reward cues (food) > control/neutral stimuli is reported. It does meet other requirements: it assesses natural reward-related visual cues (I3), reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain inference with corrected peaks (I5, I6), and provides participant/cue information (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered from the provided document. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to provide the required within-participant cue>control contrast (I4).

This fMRI study examines neural responses to food vs non-food photographic cues (natural reward; clear visual component). It includes within-participant contrasts of Food>Non-food in the AN group (Analysis 32663934_analysis_2) and a whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis (Analysis 32663934_analysis_1: whole-brain inference, FWE cluster-level), satisfying the requirement for at least one qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result. Visual cue type, participant age/sex, and task details are reported. Therefore it meets the review’s scope and inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity and provides qualifying voxelwise results.

This study reports task-based seed-to-voxel functional connectivity contrasts (seed-based connectivity analyses) comparing patients and controls for HC>LC (group-by-condition interactions). It uses visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports participant details. However, it does not report a qualifying within-participant voxelwise task-evoked activation contrast of cue>control (HC>LC) at the group level; all reported results are seed-based connectivity group comparisons. Therefore exclusion criteria E4 (only seed-based connectivity without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result) and E5 (reports only between-group/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast) are met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I7 (participant/cue details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked result). fulltext_incomplete=false

This fMRI study examines neural responses to visual food cues (natural rewards) using a within-subject contrast (food > non-food). The analysis was a group-level voxelwise whole-brain test (inference over whole brain; FDR thresholding) with reported MNI peaks, satisfying the requirement for a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result. Participant demographics and cue details are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level result), I6 (reported peaks/coordinates available), and I7 (participant/cue details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study investigates neural responses to food (natural reward) using visual stimuli and reports whole-brain voxelwise group results, but the NeuroStore record only lists between-group contrasts (e.g., AN > CON for high- and low-calorie pictures) and does not report any within-participant cue>control contrasts (e.g., high-calorie > neutral or food > non-food) that are required. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues - food), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level results), I6 (results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported). No evidence the full text was unreadable, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to visual food cues (high- and low-calorie photographs) in healthy adults, addressing natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity (meets I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of natural reward cues > control (high-calorie > control; low-calorie > control) (meets I4). Multiple group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported as whole-brain analyses with voxelwise thresholds and tables of peak coordinates (analyses 0–3), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results (meets I5) and acceptable reporting of coordinates in tables (meets I6). Participant demographics and cue type are provided; MRI field strength and preprocessing software are not reported but missing methodological details do not exclude the study per criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study investigates visual food cue-reactivity (natural reward) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results reported in tables; however, the NeuroStore record lists only between-group contrasts (e.g., boys>girls, restrained>unrestrained) of the within-subject food>fixation contrast and does not report a qualifying within-participant cue>control (food>control) group-level main effect or within-subject contrast result. This means the paper provides only between-group interaction contrasts without an accompanying within-participant cue>control group result. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported), and I6 (results reported as coordinate tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no qualifying within-participant cue>control analysis reported).

Exclusion E5 applies: the paper does not report a within-participant cue>control task-evoked voxelwise contrast required by I4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward—food—with a visual label component), I5 (there are group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported as peak coordinates), and I6 (results reported in tables of coordinates). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant drug- or natural reward-cue > control-stimulus contrast is reported). The reported voxelwise results are between-group contrasts (FD vs HC) and interactions; some reported analyses are seed-based connectivity only. Because E5 is met, the study must be excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not report any within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (required I4). The only reported within-group voxelwise contrast is CS− > CS+ (control > alcohol-conditioned), which is the reverse of the required cue>control direction. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: it examines alcohol cue conditioning with visual CS (I3), reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise results with reported coordinates (I5, I6), and provides participant details (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Thus, failure to meet I4 leads to exclusion.

The study reports task-evoked fMRI contrasts using visual cues (Monetary Incentive Delay Task with visual shapes and target) that index reward-related cue-reactivity. Within-participant contrasts of reward cues versus neutral control (anticipation of gain > anticipation of neutral; outcome of loss > no loss) are used in reported group-level voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain; voxelwise thresholding; tables of reported peaks). These satisfy the requirement for a within-participant cue>control contrast (I4) and provide whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (I5). The presence of visual cue stimuli meets I3, and coordinate/peak tables satisfy I6. Missing reporting details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are permissible per I7. No exclusion criteria apply (whole-brain results are present; not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes within-participant contrasts). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in this meta-analysis of visual reward cue-reactivity.

The study used visual sexual cues and reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise results, but it does not clearly report a within-participant cue>control (sexual>nonsexual) group-level contrast. Available analyses are between-group interaction contrasts (PHB>control for sexual>nonsexual) and within-group regression on sexual condition; no qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast is presented. Per exclusion criterion E5, studies that report only between-group contrasts or interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast should be excluded.

The study uses an fMRI color-word drug Stroop with visual drug words (visual cue component). It reports within-subject contrasts of drug > neutral words (multiple analyses) and at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain second-level random-effects t-test with FWE cluster-level correction and reported peak coordinates/tables. Participant demographics (n, age, sex) and cue type are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (visual drug cues), I4 (within-participant drug>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain result), I6 (results reported as peaks/tables), and I7 (participant info present; other optional details missing but allowed). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical).

This fMRI study examines natural reward cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue (Coke can image) and includes a within-participant cue>control contrast (Analysis 2: Coke can > neutral light). Model estimation and inference were performed voxelwise over the whole brain (group-level task-evoked results reported; peaks provided). The design uses visual stimuli and reports whole-brain voxelwise results satisfying cluster/FDR thresholds. Participant samples are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes a within-subject cue>control contrast). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-related reward-reactivity and should be INCLUDED.

This study examined fMRI responses to food pictures (natural reward cues) but the reported group-level voxelwise analysis contrasts the participant physiological states (fasting > eating), not a within-participant cue>control stimulus contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cue-reactivity: food pictures), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked result reported), I6 (peaks reported in a table). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant contrast of reward cues > control stimuli is reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) directly apply, but failing I4 mandates exclusion. Full text is complete according to the provided document.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with within-subject contrasts (individual contrasts for unhealthy foods > non-foods and healthy foods > non-foods during each sleep period) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported as coordinate peaks/tables. The task is a visual Cue Reactivity Task, results are reported at the whole-brain voxel level with reported peaks/tables, and participant demographics are provided. These facts satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-participant cue>control, or non-empirical) are met. Full text is sufficiently represented by the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria: it is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using pictorial visual food cues (I3). It reports a within-participant contrast comparing high-calorie versus low-calorie food cues (I4). The reported analysis is a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result with models fit over the whole brain and whole-brain inference with cluster correction and reported peak coordinates (I5, I6). Participant demographics and cue type and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-subject cue contrasts rather than only between-group contrasts. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study reports fMRI cue-reactivity to alcohol-related visual stimuli and includes within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > neutral (analyses 4 and 5). Results are group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistics reported within a region-of-interest with cluster-level correction (AlphaSim), and peaks are provided in a table, satisfying the requirement for small-volume-corrected voxelwise evidence. Participant demographics (age/sex) and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI with no small-volume correction, only connectivity/resting-state, or lack of within-participant cue>control contrasts) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study provides task-evoked fMRI contrasts comparing food (natural reward) to control visual stimuli (places and clocks). Specifically, contrasts Food > Places and Clocks (and Food > Faces, Places, Clocks) are reported as within-participant, group-level voxelwise results with whole-brain inference and peak coordinates (tables). Visual stimuli were used (images of food), and the model is a whole-brain random-effects analysis with nonparametric TFCE thresholding, satisfying voxelwise reporting. Participant demographics (age/sex) and cue type are reported; some preprocessing/MRI field-strength details are not present in the extracted record, but per criteria their absence does not preclude inclusion. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis objectives for natural reward (food) cue-reactivity and includes qualifying whole-brain voxelwise contrasts.

This study used visual food cues (high-fat/high-sugar food, vegetables, water) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results corrected across the whole brain, so it meets I3 and I5 (and I6 for acceptable reporting). However, all reported neuroimaging contrasts in the NeuroStore record are group×time interaction contrasts (between-group interactions comparing intervention vs control across pre/post) rather than standalone within-participant cue>control contrasts. The record does not show a simple within-subject cue>control contrast that could qualify under I4. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control result) and must be excluded.

Exclusion E5 met: the paper does not report a within-participant drug-cue > control (or natural reward > control) voxelwise contrast. While the study meets I3 (fMRI with clear visual drug-related cues — alcohol pictures) and provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain FDR-corrected win>lose; I5) and reports coordinates/tables (I6), the available voxelwise whole-brain results pertain to a reward (win>lose) gambling contrast rather than a drug-cue > control contrast. ROI analyses reported for "high personal reference > low personal reference" are not clearly equivalent to a drug-cue > control within-subject contrast in the extract. Therefore it fails I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast) and must be excluded under E5.

This fMRI study examines alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual alcohol vs soft-drink stimuli and reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise contrasts. The paper includes within-participant cue contrasts (e.g. alcohol pull > soft drink pull and the approach-bias contrast [(alcohol pull>alcohol push) > (soft drink pull>soft drink push)]) at the group level, and whole-brain results with reported peak coordinates. These satisfy inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI (I3), a within-participant drug>control contrast (I4), and voxelwise whole-brain group-level results (I5); coordinates are reported (I6). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-participant contrasts). Full text appears available in the provided record.

The study uses visual food cues (snack and vegetable pictures) and reports whole-brain, task-evoked voxelwise results (peaks in tables), but the NeuroStore record does not report any within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., snack>vegetable or food>neutral) — only main effects of condition (hungry>satiated), main effect of task (NoGo>Go), interactions involving task and stimuli, and a three-way interaction. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I4 requiring a within-participant cue>control contrast. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This fMRI study examines food-related cue-reactivity using visual food word stimuli (food Stroop), includes a within-subject contrast Food>Neutral (Analysis 1) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results for that contrast. These satisfy the review objective (natural reward visual cues) and inclusion criteria requiring a within-participant cue>control contrast and a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. Although the paper also reports seed-based gPPI connectivity, that does not exclude inclusion because a qualifying whole-brain task contrast is present. Participant demographics and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion criteria met: E3, E4, E5. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food stimuli). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported); I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked result — analyses and inference are restricted to region-of-interest); I6 not applicable. Rationale: NeuroStore extraction shows only ROI-based ICA component-loading connectivity analyses and between-group contrasts (lean vs overweight/obese). No within-subject food>nonfood voxelwise task contrasts are reported, and the reported analyses are ICA/connectivity (E4) and ROI-restricted (E3) with only between-group contrasts (E5). Full text is available in this record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study used visual food images (natural rewards) and reports a within-subject contrast comparing tasty versus non-tasty food (ADMIT_TASTY > ADMIT_NONTASTY). At least one analysis was estimated over the whole brain with voxelwise thresholding and reported peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. Participant age/sex and cue type are reported; MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not provided in the record but their absence does not preclude inclusion per review guidelines. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This study used an fMRI Monetary Incentive Delay Task with visual cues (satisfying I3). However, the NeuroStore extraction reports only a between-group omnibus contrast (main effect of group) estimated and inferred at the whole-brain level; no within-participant cue>control (e.g., reward cue > neutral/control) voxelwise contrast is reported. Therefore the study does not provide the required within-subject cue>control task-evoked result (I4 not met) and there is no qualifying group-level voxelwise within-participant contrast (I5 not met). This meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study examines natural reward cue-reactivity using erotic (IAPS) visual stimuli (meets I3). It includes within-participant contrasts of erotic > non-erotic expectancy within a treatment × expectancy ANOVA (meets I4). Participant demographics are reported (meets I7). However, all reported imaging results were estimated and inferred within predefined regions of interest (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest) with no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise results provided. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results).

Exclusion E5 applies: the NeuroStore record reports only a between-group interaction contrast (lifelong PE patients > controls for erotic vs scenic pictures) and does not report an explicit within-participant cue>control (erotic > scenic) contrast. Met inclusion criteria: I3 (task fMRI with visual natural-reward erotic cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise analysis fitted over the whole brain), I6 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no explicit within-participant cue>control contrast reported). No other exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study must be excluded from the cue-reactivity meta-analysis because it lacks a qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast.

This fMRI study used visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports within-subject contrasts comparing food vs non-food/no-food conditions (e.g., Food > no Food; food > non-food). Analyses were estimated and inferenced at the whole-brain level with reported peak coordinates and tables, satisfying voxelwise, group-level task-evoked results. The paper reports participant demographics and cue types; MRI field strength and preprocessing software are not stated but these are preferred details and their absence does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and it is empirical task fMRI). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

The study examines natural reward-related (erotic) visual cues using 20 erotic vs 20 non-erotic IAPS pictures (meets I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of erotic > emotional/non-erotic pictures (meets I4). Analyses were estimated over the whole brain and report voxelwise peak coordinates/tables at voxel-level thresholds (group-level task-evoked voxelwise results), satisfying I5 and I6. Participant age/sex and MRI field strength are reported, though preprocessing/statistical software is not fully specified (I7 not fully met but noted as preferred only). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), include within-subject cue>control contrasts (not only between-group; E5), and the paper is empirical (not E6). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study examines fMRI responses to food cues (visual pairs of food items), i.e., natural reward-related cue-reactivity, and includes a within-participant contrast (Challenge > No Challenge) comparing cue conditions. Analysis 28077722_analysis_0 was fit over the whole brain and reports a small-volume-corrected voxelwise result (TFCE nonparametric permutation, voxel-level inference restricted to an ROI), satisfying the requirement for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. Although one analysis is ROI-only, at least one qualifying small-volume-corrected voxelwise result is present. Participant/cue/contrast details are reported. Therefore the study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria for natural reward visual cue-reactivity and reports qualifying voxelwise results.

The study examines neural reactivation to visual cues (trial-unique color pictures) associated with reward, satisfying the review’s focus on natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a visual component. It includes within-subject contrasts of high reward > low reward (Analyses 0 and 2). It reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results: Analysis 2 reports whole-brain inference and Analysis 0 reports small-volume FWE-corrected inference (ROI SVC). Voxelwise results/peaks are reported. Participant age and sex are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical fMRI work). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

This study used visual cues (food and activity images), meeting I3. It reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results with FWE cluster-level correction and coordinate peaks, satisfying I5 and I6. However, the NeuroStore record lists only between-group interaction contrasts (group-by-stimulus and group differences in inhibition) and does not report any within-participant cue>control (e.g., food>non-food) contrasts at the group level. Therefore it does not meet I4, and exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast) applies. Conclusion: EXCLUDE.

The study uses natural reward visual cues (pictures of snack foods) so meets I3. It reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results with cluster correction and reported peaks, satisfying I5 and I6. However, NeuroStore extraction shows only an omnibus/between-group analysis of cognitive regulation condition (and no explicit within-participant contrast of natural reward cues > control stimuli or cue-reactivity contrast). Therefore it does not meet I4. Because there is no qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast, exclusion criterion E5 applies (studies reporting only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control). Inclusion IDs met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion IDs not met: I4. Full text appears available (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study does not meet the visual-cue requirement for this review. Inclusion IDs met: I4 (within-participant contrasts: milkshake > tasteless and related contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported, whole-brain and/or SVC), I6 (coordinates/peaks reported in tables). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (no clear visual cue component — stimuli are gustatory milkshake and autobiographical imagery scripts rather than externally presented visual cues); I7 partially not met (MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software not reported in the provided record). Exclusion IDs met: none. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails I3 (and lacks full reporting for I7).

This fMRI study used visual sexual images as task-irrelevant distractors (natural reward-related cues) and implemented within-subject contrasts comparing sexually preferred versus non-preferred distractors. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates (Tables 1–2), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics (age, sex) and task details are reported. Although the control condition consists of non-preferred sexual distractors rather than neutral stimuli, the within-participant cue>control contrast of sexual (reward-related) versus control distractors fits the meta-analysis objective of natural reward cue-reactivity. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical study) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study uses visual food cues (images of beverages and milkshakes), so it addresses natural reward cue-reactivity (I3 met). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (analyses with whole-brain inference and reported coordinate peaks/tables), satisfying I5 and I6. However, all task contrasts reported are comparisons between types of food cues (healthy vs unhealthy) rather than a within-participant cue>control (e.g., food cue > neutral/control) contrast required by I4. No qualifying cue>control within-subject contrast is present in the extracted analyses. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Because I4 is not met, the study must be excluded.

This study reports fMRI whole-brain analyses of visual slot-machine stimuli in pathological gambling and cocaine dependence and provides coordinate results, but does not present a within-participant cue>control (drug or natural reward cue versus neutral control) contrast. All extracted analyses are reported as between-group (group-level comparisons) of task conditions (e.g., winning outcome vs baseline; matched vs unmatched final-reel) rather than a within-subject cue>control contrast required by I4. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward-related gambling cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported), I6 (coordinates/peaks reported), I7 (participant details provided). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast documented). Full text appears available in the record (no access notice).

The study uses visual food and sports images (natural rewards), but all reported voxelwise analyses were restricted to regions of interest (ROI) rather than whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise results. The NeuroStore record lists only ROI model fit/inference and reports contrasts focused on ‘Sport’ (within-group post>pre and responder>non-responder between-group). There is no within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., food>neutral) reported as a qualifying voxelwise result. Therefore the paper fails to meet the requirement for a qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result and lacks the required within-participant cue>control contrast.

This study is an fMRI investigation using visual food cues (high- and low-energy snack pictures) and reports a voxelwise small-volume-corrected result, so it meets I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (small-volume-corrected voxelwise result), and I6 (results clearly reported). However, the reported group contrast (NSC > SC) compares two task conditions (no-self-control vs self-control choices) rather than a within-participant natural reward-related cue > control-stimulus contrast required by I4. The extraction does not report any cue>neutral or cue>control contrast (e.g., food images > neutral images), so I4 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I4.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria. The task uses visual conditioned stimuli (geometric shapes) paired with a natural reward (sucrose), so I3 (visual cue component) is satisfied. Within-participant contrasts comparing reward-predicting cues vs control cues are reported (e.g., expected sucrose > expected No solution; unexpected sucrose > expected No solution), satisfying I4. Several analyses are group-level voxelwise, whole-brain task-evoked results with FWE correction and coordinates reported (I5, I6). Participant demographics and task details are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and within-participant cue>control contrasts are present. Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

All reported analyses were region-of-interest (ROI) only (model fit over: region of interest; inference restricted to ROI) with no whole-brain or explicitly small-volume-corrected voxelwise result reported. This meets exclusion E3. The study does meet inclusion I3 (visual natural reward cues: photographs of beloved vs familiar neutral), I4 (within-participant contrast rejecter>neutral), I6 (voxelwise peak coordinates reported in tables for ROI results), and I7 (participant age/sex and cue details reported). It does not meet I5 because no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked result is available. Therefore exclude.

This study examines visual natural reward (food) cue reactivity and reports within-participant food>non-food contrasts (I3, I4). Voxelwise results are reported as peak coordinates in tables (I6). However, all reported group-level voxelwise results are seed-based PPI (task-modulated connectivity) analyses; no task-evoked activation (GLM contrast) whole-brain or SVC activation results are provided. According to exclusion criterion E4 (PPI/seed-based connectivity-only studies are excluded), this study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I6. Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying task-evoked voxelwise activation contrast).

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual appetizing food images (meets I3). The paper reports a within-participant contrast (milkshake > water for food images) consistent with a cue>control comparison (meets I4), and reported peak coordinates/tables are available (meets I6). However, all extracted analyses that report statistical inference are described as region-of-interest/region-level results (model fit over: region of interest; region-level thresholding). No group-level whole-brain voxelwise or small-volume-corrected (SVC) task-evoked results are documented in the extraction. Therefore the study is excluded for reporting only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain or SVC voxelwise result (exclusion E3), and it fails to satisfy inclusion criterion I5.

The study assesses neural responses to visual food cues (natural rewards) using fMRI and includes a within-participant contrast food > nonfood (Analysis 14573322_analysis_5) reported as group-level voxelwise activation maps with whole-brain cluster-level inference and reported peak coordinates/tables. The document provides participant demographics and task/cue details. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, or lack of within-participant cue>control contrasts) are met. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of visual reward-related cue-reactivity.

This study is excluded because it does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast (inclusion I4 not met) and instead reports an omnibus group × stimulation × stimulus interaction (a between-group/interaction analysis). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI with visual natural reward cues — food pictures), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked result reported with reported peaks and MNI coordinates), I6 (voxelwise results reported as peaks/tables acceptable), I7 (participant age/sex and other details reported). Fulltext_incomplete: false.

The study examines natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (photographs of junk food) and includes within-participant task-evoked contrasts versus baseline/control (e.g., Probe Train Low Chose Low > baseline and Probe Train Both Chose Low > baseline). Analyses were whole-brain voxelwise with inference over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates (tables), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise results. Participant demographics and task details are reported. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural-reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results), I6 (results reported in tables of coordinates), and I7 (participant and task details reported). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Hence the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study investigates natural reward-related cue-reactivity (food vs non-food visual stimuli) in humans, reporting a within-participant contrast (food > non-food; Analysis 32848943_analysis_0) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain; reported peaks). These facts satisfy the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity, a within-participant cue>control contrast, and at least one qualifying whole-brain voxelwise result. Some descriptive details (e.g., sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not fully reported in the NeuroStore extract, but I7 is preferred rather than mandatory. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study reports original fMRI data using the Monetary Incentive Delay Task (monetary reward/loss cues = natural reward visual cues). It includes within-participant contrasts (A1 Win > Win neutral; A1 Loss > Loss neutral) and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates (Table t1). These meet the review’s requirements for visual reward cue-reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrasts, and qualifying whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text is available in the provided record.

This study reports a task-based fMRI investigation using visual food cues (food pictures vs non-food pictures) in obese participants, with at least one within-participant contrast of food>non-food (Analysis 27216819_analysis_0). The contrast is tested at the group level with voxelwise whole-brain analysis (second-level random-effects GLM) and reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result. Although some methodological details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not listed in the NeuroStore record, missing those details does not preclude inclusion per the review’s guidance. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual reward-related cue-reactivity.

The study used visual natural reward cues (food images) and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (tables of peak coordinates), but it does not include a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (no food-vs-control cue contrast is reported). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward visual cues), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I6 (results reported as coordinate tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no cue>control within-participant contrast). I7 (preferred reporting of MRI field strength) is not fully reported (field strength not specified) but is only a preference and not the primary reason for exclusion.

This is an fMRI study using visual sexual cues (photographs of children) so I3 is satisfied, and voxelwise peaks are reported (reported peaks: 4) so I6 is satisfied. However, the reported analysis is a within-subject time-by-cue interaction (before-treatment > after-treatment for boys vs girls) from a single patient (n=1) rather than a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result, so it does not meet the requirement for a group-level whole-brain or SVC voxelwise result (I5 not met). Also, the document does not present a standalone within-participant cue>control contrast as a qualifying analysis (I4 not met); because only an interaction/between-occasion contrast is reported without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast, exclusion criterion E5 applies. Therefore the study must be excluded.
